riddle_original: Je suis un bras robotique canadien qui aide les astronautes à travailler dans l'espace. Que suis-je ?
riddle_english: I'm a Canadian robotic arm that helps astronauts work in space. What am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un chercheur montréalais considéré comme l'un des pionniers de l'apprentissage profond. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I'm a Montreal researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers of deep learning. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai grandi dans la banlieue française, j'ai l'ambition de protéger la France et je suis très présent sur Tiktok. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I grew up in the French suburbs, I have the ambition to protect France, and I am very active on TikTok. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le plus jeune parmi ceux qui occupent mon rôle et il y a une vidéo où je reçois une claque de ma moitié. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the youngest among those who hold my role, and there is a video where I receive a slap from my other half. Who am I?

riddle_original: Quand je sors, les députés s'assoient, les motions de censure s'activent et la rue s'embrase. Je suis un chiffre qui fait grincer des dents. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: When I come out, deputies sit down, motions of no confidence are activated, and the streets catch fire. I am a number that makes people cringe. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je vis à Matignon, je suis le fusible du Président et je prends tous les coups pour lui. Quand tout va mal, c'est moi qu'on remplace en premier. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I live in Matignon, I am the President's fuse, and I take all the hits for him. When everything goes wrong, I am the first to be replaced. Who am I?

riddle_original: Autrefois simple vêtement de sécurité fluo dormant dans le coffre des voitures, je suis devenu le symbole absolu de la colère des ronds-points tous les samedis d'hiver. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Once a simple neon safety garment sleeping in the trunks of cars, I became the absolute symbol of roundabout anger every winter Saturday. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis l'angoisse absolue des députés car je les renvoie tous chez eux d'un seul coup pour de nouvelles élections. Le Président appuie sur mon bouton quand il veut créer un choc. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the absolute dread of deputies because I send them all home at once for new elections. The President presses my button when he wants to create a shock. Who am I?

riddle_original: Le plus grand aéroport de France porte mon nom. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: The largest airport in France bears my name. Who am I?

riddle_original: Cinq fois née, jamais éteinte, « Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité » est ma devise sainte. Marianne est mon visage, le bonnet phrygien ma couronne. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Born five times, never extinguished, "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity" is my holy motto. Marianne is my face, the Phrygian cap my crown. Who am I?

riddle_original: En soixante-quinze, Simone m'a fait naître, En deux mille vingt-quatre, dans la Constitution j'ai pu paraître. Premier pays au monde à me graver ainsi, Je suis une liberté pour les femmes, enfin garantie. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: In seventy-five, Simone gave birth to me. In two thousand twenty-four, I appeared in the Constitution. The first country in the world to engrave me thus, I am a freedom for women, finally guaranteed. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un droit précieux, sacré, jamais de trop. Penser, parler, écrire ce que l'on veut tout haut, la Révolution m'a inscrite comme un principe neuf. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a precious, sacred right, never too much. To think, speak, and write whatever one wants out loud, the Revolution inscribed me as a new principle. Who am I?

riddle_original: La patrouille de France se mobilise pour moi. Le bitume de Paris tremble sous le poids des chars Leclerc. Je suis un clin d'œil à une révolution. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: The Patrouille de France mobilizes for me. The asphalt of Paris trembles under the weight of Leclerc tanks. I am a nod to a revolution. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis l'Instrument utilisé en France pour éviter une mort lente, notamment pendant la Révolution française. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the instrument used in France to avoid a slow death, notably during the French Revolution. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le surnom donné à un roi de France, faisant référence à une étoile, car je l'ai choisie pour symboliser la puissance et la lumière. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the nickname given to a king of France, referring to a star, because I chose it to symbolize power and light. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le premier visage de la résistance sur notre sol. Mon nom signifie "le plus grand roi des guerriers". On m'imagine souvent avec de longues moustaches et des tresses, bien que je n'aie jamais porté de casque à ailes. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the first face of resistance on our soil. My name means "the greatest king of warriors." I am often imagined with a long mustache and braids, although I never wore a winged helmet. Who am I?

riddle_original: Parti de rien sur une île, j'ai fait marcher mes hommes d'un bout à l'autre de l'Europe pour redessiner toutes ses frontières, avant que l'hiver et une plaine belge ne brisent mon élan. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Starting from nothing on an island, I marched my men across Europe to redraw all its borders, before winter and a Belgian plain broke my momentum. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai pris la tête de l'État français à Vichy et j'ai engagé le pays dans la collaboration avec l'Allemagne nazie. Condamné pour haute trahison à la Libération, qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I took the head of the French State in Vichy and committed the country to collaboration with Nazi Germany. Condemned for high treason at the Liberation, who am I?

riddle_original: Sur l'échafaud, en 1793, ma tête fut tranchée. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: On the scaffold, in 1793, my head was severed. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis la période historique qui sert d'excuse absolue à tous les Français pour justifier leurs manifestations. J'ai commencé par la destruction d'une prison et j'ai rendu célèbre une machine très efficace pour raccourcir nos dirigeants. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the historical period that serves as the absolute excuse for all French people to justify their protests. I began with the destruction of a prison and made famous a very efficient machine for shortening our leaders. Who am I?

riddle_original: Si la légende populaire prétend que j'ai mis un cartable au dos des enfants, j'ai surtout imposé la gratuité de l'étude dans mes monastères pour que mon peuple sache enfin lire et compter. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: If popular legend claims that I put a schoolbag on children's backs, I mostly imposed free education in my monasteries so that my people could finally know how to read and count. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis une heroine de l'histoire de France et on m'a brûlée vive. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a heroine of French history and I was burned alive. Who am I?

riddle_original: Bien que je désigne le pays tout entier dans le langage courant et étant une figure, je tourne pourtant le dos à la Corse et aux îles lointaines pour ne garder que le continent. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Although I refer to the entire country in everyday language and am a shape, I turn my back on Corsica and the distant islands to keep only the mainland. Who am I?

riddle_original: Le mont Saint-Michel il est chez nous ! De quelle région je viens ?
riddle_english: Mont Saint-Michel belongs to us! Which region am I from?

riddle_original: Je suis une zone de non-droit routier au pied d'une arche. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I'm a traffic free-for-all at the foot of an arch, who am I ?

riddle_original: Selon les amoureux, je suis leur capitale ; selon Hugo, je suis une cathédrale ; selon Hemingway, je suis une fête. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: According to lovers, I am their capital; according to Hugo, I am a cathedral; according to Hemingway, I am a moveable feast. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis français et dispersé aux quatre coins de la planète. Grâce à moi, le soleil ne se couche jamais en France. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am French and scattered to the four corners of the planet. Thanks to me, the sun never sets on France. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The French Overseas Departments and Territories (DOM-TOM)

riddle_original: Je suis surnommé le toit de l'Europe et je suis au centre d'une embrouille de voisinage éternelle avec l'Italie. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am nicknamed the roof of Europe and I am at the center of an eternal neighborhood dispute with Italy. Who am I?

riddle_original: Pierres dressées, je gardais les oubliés. Un jour d'été, la foule m'a libérée. De ma chute naquit une nation nouvelle.
riddle_english: Standing stones, I guarded the forgotten. One summer day, the crowd freed me. From my fall, a new nation was born.

riddle_original: Je ne suis tracée sur aucune carte officielle, mais je traverse la France de la Meuse aux Landes. Chez moi, il y a moins de 30 habitants au kilomètre carré et la 5G est un mythe. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am not drawn on any official map, but I cross France from the Meuse to the Landes. Where I am, there are fewer than 30 inhabitants per square kilometer, and 5G is a myth. Who am I?

riddle_original: On pense que j'abrite beaucoup de mafieux, terroristes et de paresseux. Je suis une montagne dans la mer. On m'aime pour mes plages, mes parcs naturels, ma faune et ma gastronomie. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: People think I host many mobsters, terrorists, and lazy people. I am a mountain in the sea. I am loved for my beaches, my natural parks, my wildlife, and my gastronomy. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je porte la couleur du ciel sans être le ciel. Les fortunes s'y dorent, les festivals s'y filment. Entre mer et palmiers, je suis une côte qui brille.
riddle_english: I wear the color of the sky without being the sky. Fortunes bask here, festivals are filmed here. Between sea and palm trees, I am a shining coast.

riddle_original: J'ai fait danser la garde républicaine sur mon tube djadja pendant la ceremie des JO et j'ai fait taire les racistes. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I made the Republican Guard dance to my hit "Djadja" during the Olympics ceremony, and I silenced the racists. Who am I?

riddle_original: Sur l'ancien billet de cinq francs, j'avais ma place, Un lycée sur deux porte mon nom dans chaque ville de France. Gavroche est tombé sur ma barricade, Et au Panthéon, je dors en grande pompe.
riddle_english: On the old five-franc note, I had my place. One in two high schools bears my name in every city in France. Gavroche fell on my barricade, and at the Panthéon, I sleep in great pomp.

riddle_original: Mes albums sortent plus vite que mes haters n'arrivent à les écouter, l'OM est ma religion. La J formée avec les doigts est mon salut et je crie "alors !" sur chaque refrain. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: My albums come out faster than my haters can listen to them, OM is my religion. The J formed with fingers is my greeting, and I yell "alors !" on every chorus. Who am I?

riddle_original: "La Bohème" était ma jeunesse, "Hier encore" ma nostalgie, "Emmenez-moi" mon évasion, et "For Me Formidable" mon clin d'œil bilingue. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: "La Bohème" was my youth, "Hier encore" my nostalgia, "Emmenez-moi" my escape, and "For Me Formidable" my bilingual wink. Who am I?

riddle_original: Mélancolique chronique, j'ai donné au « Spleen » ses lettres de noblesse en France. Mes « Fleurs » sont loin d'être fanées, puisqu'elles tombent presque une année sur deux au baccalauréat. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Chronically melancholic, I gave 'Spleen' its letters of nobility in France. My 'Flowers' are far from withered, as they come up almost every other year on the baccalaureate exam. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'avais pour passion d'allumer le feu et de faire pleurer les guitares. À ma mort, la France s'est arrêtée. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: My passion was to light the fire and make guitars cry. When I died, France stopped. Who am I?

riddle_original: Nous sommes deux célibataires endurcis qui vivons dans un petit village entouré de camps romains. L'un est petit et malin avec des ailes sur son casque, l'autre est livreur de menhirs. Qui sommes-nous ?
riddle_english: We are two confirmed bachelors living in a small village surrounded by Roman camps. One is short and clever with wings on his helmet, the other is a menhir deliveryman. Who are we?

riddle_original: Je suis le seul jour de l'année où je transforme chaque trottoir de France en scène de concert géante pour fêter l'arrivée de l'été. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the only day of the year when I transform every sidewalk in France into a giant concert stage to celebrate the arrival of summer. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un événement où une petite ville du Sud devient le centre du monde grâce à ma feuille en or. Mes 24 marches sont les plus photographiées de France grâce à mon tapis rouge. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am an event where a small southern town becomes the center of the world thanks to my golden leaf. My 24 steps are the most photographed in France thanks to my red carpet. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le plus grand champion de la langue française. J'ai passé ma vie à faire rire le Roi Soleil en ridiculisant les bourgeois, les avares et les faux médecins. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the greatest champion of the French language. I spent my life making the Sun King laugh by ridiculing the bourgeois, the misers, and the fake doctors. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un dauphin dans l'eau, je suis français, je joue aux jeux vidéo et j'ai inspiré de nombreux français à nager. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a dolphin in the water, I am French, I play video games, and I inspired many French people to swim. Who am I?

riddle_original: Tous les Français prononcent mal mon nom, et on ne me parle pas d'âge. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: All French people mispronounce my name, and you don't talk to me about age. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un colosse de plus de deux mètres, on m'appelle souvent le boss des tatamis. J'ai allumé la vasque des JO de Paris. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a colossus of over two meters; I am often called the boss of the tatamis. I lit the Paris Olympics cauldron. Who am I?

riddle_original: Chez moi, le public sirote du Perrier tout en regardant des sportifs tacher leurs chaussettes blanches sur de la poussière orange. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: At my place, the public sips Perrier while watching athletes stain their white socks on orange dust. Who am I?

riddle_original: Sportif avec une grande palette technique, je suis connu pour mon coup de tête mémorable qui a glacé tout un pays. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: An athlete with a great technical range, I am known for my memorable headbutt that froze an entire country. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis la compagne inséparable du Pastis et du soleil d’été, je suis le sport national des fins d'après-midi. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the inseparable companion of Pastis and the summer sun; I am the national late-afternoon sport. Who am I?

riddle_original: On m'appelle l'Everest des mers. Je suis une course en voilier pour faire le tour du monde en solitaire, sans escale et sans assistance. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: They call me the Everest of the seas. I am a sailing race to go around the world solo, non-stop, and without assistance. Who am I?

riddle_original: La météo n'a pas été clémente avec moi pendant ma cérémonie d'ouverture, mais j'ai réussi à rassembler le monde entier. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: The weather was not kind to me during my opening ceremony, but I managed to bring the whole world together. Who am I?

riddle_original: Dans les cafés ou les lycées, je suis le sport de table par excellence. Mes joueurs sont montés sur des barres. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: In cafes or high schools, I am the ultimate table sport. My players are mounted on bars. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le sport "after work" favori des Français. On grimpe, on s'accroche, parfois on tombe. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the favorite "after-work" sport of the French. You climb, you hold on, sometimes you fall. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le meilleur ami d'un morceau de pain et d'un verre de rouge qui se découpe en parts triangulaires, au point que j'ai donné mon nom aux graphiques de tes cours de maths. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the best friend of a piece of bread and a glass of red wine, cut into triangular pieces, to the point that I gave my name to the charts in your math classes. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis l'épée du Français, mais on me mange. Je crie quand on me brise, je dors sous son aisselle. L'UNESCO m'a faite immortelle. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the Frenchman's sword, but you eat me. I cry when broken, I sleep under his armpit. UNESCO made me immortal. Who am I?

riddle_original: Les gens finissent sous la table en me mangeant et quand on me croque, on peut se casser les dents. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: People end up under the table while eating me, and when you bite into me, you might break your teeth. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis une demeure dont le nom a donné naissance à une expression familière qui invite à éteindre la lumière. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a residence whose name gave birth to a colloquial expression inviting you to turn off the lights. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je ressemble à une crêpe sur la tête mais je ne suis pas comestible, je suis la parfaite combinaison avec la marinière. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I look like a crepe on the head but I am not edible; I am the perfect combination with a striped sailor shirt. Who am I?

riddle_original: Musique née à Strasbourg, baptisée par Marseille, adoptée par la République. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Music born in Strasbourg, baptized by Marseille, adopted by the Republic. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un symbole de la France grâce à un jeu de mots latin : mon nom désignait à la fois un peuple et un volatile. On me retrouve sur les maillots de l'équipe nationale de football, sur les pièces de monnaie et au sommet des clochers. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a symbol of France thanks to a Latin pun: my name designated both a people and a bird. I can be found on the national football team's jerseys, on coins, and at the top of bell towers. Who am I?

riddle_original: Mes inspecteurs anonymes parcourent les tables de France en secret, et mes macarons dorés peuvent faire la fortune d'un chef ou le plonger dans le désespoir s'il en perd un. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: My anonymous inspectors travel the tables of France in secret, and my golden macaroons can make a chef's fortune or plunge him into despair if he loses one. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis la star incontournable du réveillon de Noël, mais ma fabrication fait grincer les dents des défenseurs des animaux. On me sert souvent au tout début du repas, bien frais, coupé en tranches. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the inescapable star of Christmas Eve, but my production makes animal rights defenders cringe. I am often served at the very beginning of the meal, well chilled, cut into slices. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai la forme d'une lune mais le cœur d'un Français.
riddle_english: I have the shape of a moon but the heart of a Frenchman.

riddle_original: Je suis comme le Père Noël : je suis un animal, j'agis dans la nuit et je récompense les enfants. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am like Santa Claus: I am an animal, I operate at night, and I reward children. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The Little Mouse (French equivalent of the Tooth Fairy)

riddle_original: Je suis mondialement connu. Je suis petit. J'ai apprivoisé mes amis et je suis un modèle de vertu. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am world-famous. I am small. I tamed my friends, and I am a model of virtue. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis jaune et j'attends. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am yellow and I am waiting, who am I?

riddle_original: Sous forme de flacon avec un pinceau, je suis le sauveur des cahiers raturés. Au collège, les élèves m'utilisent souvent pour écrire sur leurs sacs à dos ou se peindre les ongles. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Whether in a bottle with a brush or a "mouse" format, I am the savior of crossed-out notebooks. In middle school, students often use me to write on their backpacks or paint their nails. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un père qui vous raconte une histoire. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a father who tells you a story. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis connu pour avoir été la chaîne numéro 18. Je suis la nounou officielle des enfants avec mes dessins animés. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am known for having been channel number 18. I am the official babysitter for children with my cartoons. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai une mèche blonde géante sur la tête et je trouve que la vie, c'est "tôôôtalement pô juste". Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I have a giant blond lock of hair on my head, and I think life is "toootally not fair". Who am I?

riddle_original: Dans la cour de récré, je suis un petit globe de verre. On joue à plat ventre sur le goudron pour essayer de gagner les "calots" des copains. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: In the schoolyard, I am a small glass globe. You play on your stomach on the asphalt to try to win your friends' "shooters." Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un petit livre souvent de couleur rouge. Je suis le cauchemar absolu des écoliers français qui me feuillettent avec désespoir pour savoir comment accorder un verbe au subjonctif imparfait ou au passé simple. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a small book, often red in color. I am the absolute nightmare of French schoolchildren who leaf through me in despair to figure out how to conjugate a verb in the imperfect subjunctive or simple past. Who am I?

riddle_original: Composé de deux biscuits superposés et fourrés au chocolat, j'ai deux yeux et un grand sourire dessinés sur le dessus. Je rends hommage à ma ville natale. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Made of two layered biscuits filled with chocolate, I have two eyes and a big smile drawn on top. I pay tribute to my hometown. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je peste contre la RATP, je voue une haine féroce à la ligne 13 et mon humeur est aussi grise que mon ciel de novembre. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I curse the RATP, I have a fierce hatred for Line 13, and my mood is as gray as my November sky. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis une façon de dire bonjour qui est atypique dans le monde et je me déprécie depuis le Covid-19. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a way of saying hello that is atypical in the world, and I have depreciated since Covid-19. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis un argument de fanfaronnade contre les Américains, je suis délivré à 16 ans et je suis de couleur verte. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a bragging right against Americans, I am issued at 16, and I am green. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The Carte Vitale (French health insurance card)

riddle_original: Je suis surtout un moment convivial et qui peut se "prendre" à n'importe quelle heure de la journée selon certaines personnes excessives. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am above all a convivial moment that can be "taken" at any time of the day according to some excessive people. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The aperitif (or Pre-dinner drinks / Happy hour)

riddle_original: Je suis déclenché au moindre désaccord et mes protagonistes sont fiers de me revendiquer. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am triggered at the slightest disagreement, and my protagonists are proud to claim me. Who am I?

riddle_original: Les Américains m'ont attribué une nationalité que je revendique à peine, car mes véritables inventeurs vivent un peu plus au nord et parlent la même langue. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Americans have given me a nationality that I barely claim, because my true inventors live a little further north and speak the same language. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je nourris les étudiants pour 3,30 €, je les loge dans des chambres de 9 m², je leur verse parfois des bourses, et mon acronyme commence par "Centre". Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I feed students for €3.30, I house them in 9 sq meter rooms, I sometimes pay them scholarships, and my acronym starts with "Centre". Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The CROUS (Regional Centre for University and School Works)

riddle_original: Je suis un grand classique des trousses et le stylo le plus vendu au monde. Mon bouchon est percé d'un petit trou, et mon corps transparent en plastique finit souvent complètement mâchouillé par les écoliers stressés. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a great classic of pencil cases and the best-selling pen in the world. My cap is pierced with a small hole, and my transparent plastic body often ends up completely chewed up by stressed schoolchildren. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le sésame obligatoire des Franciliens pour passer les portiques du métro. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the mandatory key for Ile-de-France residents to pass through the metro gates. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le sandwich préféré des Français. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the favorite sandwich of the French. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis une émission éducative, tous les petits Français ont eu le plaisir de voir mon émission en classe. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am an educational show; all little French kids had the pleasure of watching my show in class. Who am I?

riddle_original: Lui était né à Paris, elle venait de Varsovie pour étudier à la Sorbonne où les femmes étaient à peine tolérées. Ensemble, dans un hangar de la rue Lhomond, nous avons révolutionné la physique. Aujourd'hui, nous reposons au Panthéon. Qui sommes-nous ?
riddle_english: He was born in Paris, she came from Warsaw to study at the Sorbonne where women were barely tolerated. Together, in a hangar on rue Lhomond, we revolutionized physics. Today, we rest in the Panthéon. Who are we?

riddle_original: Né à la veille de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, je suis le plus grand organisme de recherche scientifique d'Europe. Mes laboratoires couvrent toutes les disciplines, des mathématiques à l'archéologie. Mon acronyme commence par "Centre" et finit par "Scientifique". Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Born on the eve of the Second World War, I am the largest scientific research organization in Europe. My laboratories cover all disciplines, from mathematics to archaeology. My acronym begins with "Centre" and ends with "Scientifique". Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The CNRS (French National Centre for Scientific Research)

riddle_original: Née en pleine Révolution française pour former des ingénieurs au service de la République, je porte le surnom d'une simple lettre de l'alphabet. Mes élèves défilent sur les Champs-Élysées le 14 juillet en bicorne et grand uniforme. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Born in the midst of the French Revolution to train engineers for the Republic, I bear the nickname of a single letter of the alphabet. My students parade down the Champs-Élysées on July 14th in bicorne hats and full uniform. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai longtemps été l'organisme le plus secret de France, mes premiers patrons étaient communistes pour certains et résistants pour tous, et j'ai changé de nom en 2010 pour ajouter "et aux énergies alternatives" histoire de paraître moins atomique. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I was for a long time the most secret organization in France; my first bosses were communists for some and resistance fighters for all, and I changed my name in 2010 to add "and alternative energies" just to seem less atomic. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The CEA (French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission)

riddle_original: Ingénieur, pilote et astronaute, je suis une icône absolue des manuels scolaires, je passe mes journées en apesanteur dans l'espace à jouer du saxophone ou à manger des plats de grands chefs étoilés en boîte de conserve. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Engineer, pilot, and astronaut, I am an absolute icon of school textbooks. I spend my days weightless in space playing the saxophone or eating canned meals from Michelin-starred chefs. Who am I?

riddle_original: Oiseau blanc au nez pointu et cassé, je permettais aux stars et aux présidents de traverser l'Atlantique en un temps record, avant que le coût du kérosène ne me cloue définitivement au sol. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: A white bird with a pointed, broken nose, I allowed stars and presidents to cross the Atlantic in record time, before the cost of kerosene permanently grounded me. Who am I?

riddle_original: Fierté de l'Europe spatiale portée par la France, je ne décolle jamais depuis Paris ou la métropole pour envoyer des satellites au milieu des étoiles. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: The pride of spatial Europe driven by France, I never take off from Paris or the mainland to send satellites among the stars. Who am I?

riddle_original: J'ai sauvé un petit garçon mordu par un chien en lui injectant mon vaccin, et j'ai donné mon nom à un procédé pour conserver le lait. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I saved a little boy bitten by a dog by injecting him with my vaccine, and I gave my name to a process for preserving milk. Who am I?

riddle_original: Français de naissance, parrain d'une révolution, À Pierre et Marie Curie j'ai soutenu ma thèse, jeune visionnaire. J'ai appris aux machines à voir et le prix Turing a couronné mon œuvre.
riddle_english: French by birth, godfather of a revolution. At Pierre and Marie Curie I defended my thesis, a young visionary. I taught machines to see, and the Turing Award crowned my work.

riddle_original: Je viens de l'arabe maghrébin où je signifie "comment" ou "quoi de neuf", j'ai traversé la Méditerranée avec l'immigration, je suis devenu salutation universelle dans les cours de récré françaises, et je suis entré dans le Robert en 2009. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I come from Maghrebi Arabic where I mean "how" or "what's up." I crossed the Mediterranean with immigration, became a universal greeting in French schoolyards, and entered the Robert dictionary in 2009. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je viens de l'arabe où je désigne le venin ou le poison. En français des cités, j'exprime la frustration ou la rage ressentie après un échec ou une déception.
riddle_english: I come from Arabic where I mean venom or poison. In French projects slang, I express the frustration or rage felt after a failure or disappointment.

riddle_original: Mon nom est lui-même un exemple de mon principe : prends une expression française, inverse-la, et tu obtiendras mon nom. Renaud m'a chanté dans "Laisse béton", les rappeurs m'ont consacré, et l'Académie française me regarde de travers. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: My name itself is an example of my principle: take a French expression, invert it, and you will get my name. Renaud sang about me in "Laisse béton," rappers consecrated me, and the Académie Française looks at me askance. Who am I?

riddle_original: Dans le dictionnaire, je qualifie une blessure ou une situation critique. Mais dans la bouche des Français, je suis le mot parfait pour dire "très" ou pour répondre à quelqu'un qu'on est totalement d'accord avec lui. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: In the dictionary, I describe an injury or a critical situation. But in the mouths of the French, I am the perfect word to say "very" or to reply to someone that you totally agree with them. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis animateur télé connu pour mon interjonction "Ah !". Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am a TV host known for my interjection "Ah!". Who am I?

riddle_original: Plus fort que "bien aimer" mais beaucoup moins engageant que "je t'aime", je suis le verbe parfait pour avouer ses sentiments au collège sans trop se mouiller. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: Stronger than "to like" but much less committing than "I love you," I am the perfect verb to confess your feelings in middle school without taking too much of a risk. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis issu du langage SMS et le grand rival de l'émoji qui pleure de rire. On m'écrit partout en fin de message pour ne pas laisser un blanc, ou pour faire semblant de rire à une vanne pas drôle, même si mon visage reste totalement impassible derrière mon écran. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I come from SMS language and am the great rival of the crying laughing emoji. People write me everywhere at the end of a message so as not to leave a blank, or to pretend to laugh at an unfunny joke, even if my face remains completely impassive behind my screen. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis le mot magique pour lancer une rumeur sur Snapchat ou TikTok sans jamais prendre mes responsabilités. Raccourci phonétique d'une phrase de quatre mots, je sers à raconter le dernier potin du lycée en faisant mine de ne pas être tout à fait sûr de l'info. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the magic word to start a rumor on Snapchat or TikTok without ever taking responsibility. A phonetic shortcut of a four-word phrase, I am used to tell the latest high school gossip while pretending not to be entirely sure of the info. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis l'acronyme de la flemme, né sur les claviers de téléphones pour raccourcir une expression de deux mots. On m'envoie en message avec une photo de ses pieds devant une série pour montrer qu'on est posé, sans stress et sans aucune pression. Qui suis-je ?
riddle_english: I am the acronym for laziness, born on phone keyboards to shorten a two-word expression. You send me in a message with a picture of your feet in front of a TV show to show you are chilling, stress-free, and under zero pressure. Who am I?

riddle_original: Je suis une bête, je suis une pointe sur ton mur, Mais quand je sors de ta bouche, je remplace un gros mot bien dur.
riddle_english: I am a bug, I am a tack on your wall, but when I come out of your mouth, I replace a very harsh swear word.

riddle_original: Ein Politker, der sich unnötig viele Sorgen um die Verfügbarkeit von Zahnarztterminen für Deutsche Staatsbürger macht.
riddle_english: A politician who worries unnecessarily about the availability of dental appointments for German citizens.

riddle_original: Eine Politkerin, die für Ihre Handzeichen weltweit berühmt wurde.
riddle_english: A female politician who became famous worldwide for her hand gestures.

riddle_original: Ein Gesetz, dass es verbietet, in einem bestimmten Schrittempo auf Brücken zu gehen.
riddle_english: A law that prohibits walking on bridges at a certain pace.

riddle_original: Eine Partei, die ursprünglich die Deutsche Mark zurückwollte, aber dann eine andere Richtung einschlug.
riddle_english: A party that originally wanted to bring back the German mark but then changed course.

riddle_original: Eine Politikerin, die ihren Posten kündigte, um Seenotretterin zu werden.
riddle_english: A female politician who resigned from her post to become a sea rescuer.

riddle_original: Ein Politker, dessen Gesicht illegalerweise ans Münchener Siegestor projiziert wurde.
riddle_english: A politician whose face was illegally projected onto Munich’s Victory Gate.

riddle_original: Eine Politikerin, die inspiriert vom arabischen Frühling in die Politik einstieg.
riddle_english: A female politician who entered politics inspired by the Arab Spring.

riddle_original: Eine Politikerin, die Aggressorstaaten unterstützt, und gleichzeitig eine Friedensbewegung leitet.
riddle_english: A politician who supports aggressor states while simultaneously leading a peace movement.

riddle_original: Ein Politiker, der bei weitem berühmter für seine organische Architektur war.
riddle_english: A politician who was far more famous for his organic architecture.

riddle_original: Den Mitgliedern dieser Partei werden besonders viele Doktortitel aberkannt.
riddle_english: A particularly large number of these party members have had their doctoral degrees revoked.

riddle_original: Eine Notlösung für den Ausfall der Ringbahn im Berliner Westen, die während der Mauer griff.
riddle_english: A stopgap solution for the failure of the Ringbahn in western Berlin, which was in effect during the time of the Wall.

riddle_original: Ein Konzept zur systematischen Wiederherstellung zerstörter Grundrisse in der Berliner Innenstadt.

riddle_english: This city had an austerity plan from which a secret underground city grew.

riddle_original: In dieser Stadt standen Bushaltestellen mitten auf der Autobahn.
riddle_english: In this city, bus stops stood in the middle of the highway.

riddle_original: Stadt die angeblich nicht existiert.

riddle_original: Westlicheres Neuschwanstein.
riddle_english: Neuschwanstein that's more in the West.

riddle_original: Land zu dem das siebzehnte Bundesland gehört.
riddle_english: Country that the seventeenth federal state belongs to.

riddle_original: Regelmäßig Land unter da deichfrei.

riddle_english: A German city without river, but with sulfur.

riddle_original: Malte Menschen romantisch von hinten, damit sie nicht vom Hintergrund ablenken.

riddle_original: Bekannt als Arme-Leute-Maler.

riddle_original: Autor und Künstler, der sich auch mit der Anatomie, Botanik und Geologie befasste.

riddle_original: 20% seiner Kinder wurden auch Komponisten.

riddle_english: Who did Wagner "lead loyally"?

riddle_original: Vierteiliges Werk, wo es um ein Schmuckstück geht.
riddle_english: Four-piece opus that revolves around a piece of jewelry.

riddle_original: Einer, der im Sattel in einer ungewöhnlichen Farbe die deutsche Kunstwelt prägte.
riddle_english: Someone in a saddle in an unsual color that played an important role in the German art world.

riddle_original: Brachte zwei Männer zum Streit um eine Badeente.
riddle_english: Made two men fight over a rubber duck.

riddle_original: Machte ein Haustier froh mit seinem Lied.
riddle_english: Made a pet very happy with his song.

riddle_original: Norddeutscher Sport für jedes Alter.
riddle_english: North German sport for any age.

riddle_original: Es wird um einen Ball gekämpft, aber in einem anderen Element.
riddle_english: Fighting for a ball, but in another element.

riddle_original: Was in einem anderen Sport der häufigste Regelverstoß ist, ist die Kernidee dieses Sports.

riddle_original: Sportart, die aus dem Mittelalter stammt, und weiterhin besonders in Deutschland beliebt ist, obwohl der amerikanische Cousin für weit mehr Unterhaltung sorgt.
riddle_english: Sport that goes back to the mideaval times, and is still popular in German, despite its more well-known american cousin that is more entertaining.

riddle_original: Hat als einzige Sportlerin jedes wichtige Einzelturnier ihrer Sportart mindestens viermal gewonnen.

riddle_original: Sportart, die in der Pfalz erfunden wurde und doch einen englischen Namen trägt.
riddle_english: Sport that was invented in Palatinate but has an English name.

riddle_original: Sportart, die vor allem Müller genießen.

riddle_original: Ein besonders Großer, der es zum Ballspielen über den großen Teich schaffte und dort besonders erfolgreich war.
riddle_english: A particularly tall one, managed to get across the pond to play ball and was particularly successfull there.

riddle_original: Viel erfolgreicher in Autos als auf Skiern.
riddle_english: Much more successful in cars than on skis.

riddle_original: Ihr Name lässt auf das Element schließen, auf dem sie in ihrem Sport unterwegs ist - sehr ergfolgreich, mit zwölf olympischen Medaillen.

riddle_original: Konkurriert mit Halloween.

riddle_original: Kleines Rätsel ohne Kaffee.

riddle_original: Gelber Pelz aus dem Norden.

riddle_original: Die Kirche wird schon lange nicht mehr eingeweiht.

riddle_original: Hieran werden Tierprodukte zu Feiertagen aufgehängt.

riddle_original: Landwirtschaftliche Beschreibung der Unordnung.

riddle_original: Jedermann's Tante, die kleine Dinge verkauft.

riddle_original: Unwetter zum letzten Schultag.

reference_answer_english: Abisturm (no translation, name for graduation pranks)

riddle_original: Christoph's Farbe, gehört zu orange, blau und gelb.
riddle_english: Christoph's color, belongs with orange, blue and yellow.

riddle_original: Das bestimmt miesgelaunteste Gebäck.

riddle_original: Sieger, Ehre oder nur Teilnehmen, und zwar jedes Jahr.
riddle_english: Winner, honor or just participating, every year.

riddle_original: Da könnten Steine drin sein.
riddle_english: There could be rocks in it.

riddle_english: Who is ending the lesson?

riddle_original: Raubt die Großmutter aus.

riddle_original: Körperteil, der leidet, wenn man sich umdreht oder lacht.

riddle_original: Erhält man, wenn man erfolgreich fahren gelernt hat, allerdings nur über Papier.

riddle_original: Der König spielt zuletzt und hat drei Leben.

riddle_original: Eine Gefahr für die Ruhezeit, nach Farben getrennt.
riddle_english: A danger for quiet time, separated by colors.

riddle_original: Darf sonntags nicht aus dem Schuppen kommen.

riddle_original: Ordnungswidrigkeit, die doch viele begehen, außer Kinder sehen zu.

riddle_original: Maximal 10 Minuten, aber dafür täglich, hilft der Gesundheit und gegen Feuchtigkeit.
riddle_english: Max 10 mins, but daily, is good for health and against humidity.

riddle_original: Das erste wenn man das Haus eines Freundes betritt.
riddle_english: The first thing when you visit a friend's house.

riddle_original: Das typisch deutsche und kräftigste Wort des Widerspruchs.
riddle_english: The typical German and most powerful word of disagreement.

riddle_original: Die häufigste Zutat zum deutschen Abendessen.
riddle_english: The most common ingredient for a German dinner.

riddle_original: Am Ende einer Vorlesung wird...
riddle_english: At the end of a lecture, students...

riddle_original: Dieser Flughafen hat das dreifache gekostet und am Ende doppelt so lange gebraucht, um fertiggestellt zu werden.

riddle_original: Masken, die soviel kosten wie Klimaschutz.
riddle_english: Masks that cost as much as climate protection.

riddle_original: Ein Buch das nicht zum Lesen, sondern zum Wachsen dient.

riddle_original: Tier, mit dem man im Deutschen verglichen wird, wenn man sparsam ist.
riddle_english: Animal that you resemble when you're frugal.

riddle_english: That's how marketing was called before "marketing".

riddle_original:
એક જ રાજમાં બે ભાષાઓની ગાંઠ,
અમદાવાદની શેરીઓએ વિદ્યાર્થીના પગલાં ગણ્યાં.
“ચાચા”નો અવાજ ગામેગામ પહોંચ્યો;
પહેલી મેના દિવસે ગાંઠ છૂટી—આ કઈ ચળવળ?
riddle_hint: દ્વિભાષી બોમ્બે રાજ્યમાંથી અલગ ગુજરાતી રાજ્યની માંગ.
riddle_note: Difficulty: Hard. Ahmedabad and Gujarat-wide. Reworked from a leader biography into the locally remembered statehood movement. Native review should check the preferred form “મહાગુજારાત/મહાગુગુજરાત” used by the contributor community.

riddle_hint: અમૂલનું મૂળ ગામ સ્તરે ઊભેલી આવી સંસ્થાઓમાં છે.
riddle_note: Difficulty: Hard. Charotar; Kheda-Anand. Reworked from a founder biography into a lived cooperative routine. Local terminology such as “ભાવફેર” should be checked with an active milk-society member.

riddle_original:
મહેસૂલના આંકડામાં બાવીસ ટકાનો ભાર,
તાપીના પટમાં ગામેગામ એક જ ઇનકાર.
લડત જીત્યા પછી બહેનોએ નેતાને નવું બિરુદ આપ્યું—
કઈ લડતે “સરદાર” જન્માવ્યો?
riddle_english:
A twenty-two percent weight appeared in the revenue figures;
village after village along the Tapi plain gave one refusal.
After the victory, the women placed a new title upon their leader—
which struggle gave birth to “Sardar”?
riddle_hint: ૧૯૨૮માં સુરત જિલ્લાના એક તાલુકામાં થયેલી કરબંધી.
riddle_note: Difficulty: Medium. South Gujarat; Bardoli taluka, Surat district. KEPT from draft; hint rewritten because it previously named Vallabhbhai and gave the answer away.

riddle_original:
કાપડબજારમાં માથે ગાંસડી, નામ કોઈ પગારપોથીમાં નહીં;
બગીચાની સભાએ બેનને કામદાર તરીકે ઓળખ આપી.
પછી પોતાના નામે પાસબુક પણ હાથમાં આવી—
અમદાવાદમાં ઊભેલું આ મહિલા મજૂર સંગઠન કયું?
riddle_english:
In the cloth market she carried a bale on her head, yet no payroll held her name;
a meeting in a garden recognised her as a worker.
Later she held a bank passbook in her own name—
which women workers’ organisation arose in Ahmedabad?
riddle_hint: ૧૯૭૨માં સ્વરોજગારી સ્ત્રીઓ માટે નોંધાયેલું મજૂર સંગઠન.
riddle_note: Difficulty: Hard. Ahmedabad. Reworked from an individual biography into the everyday experience that produced the organisation.

riddle_original:
રાજ્યની સરહદે ગાડી ધીમી પડે, પરવાનો માંગાય,
મહેમાનને ઘર મળે, પણ મદિરાનો પ્યાલો નહીં.
ગાંધીજીના વ્રતને કાયદાનું રૂપ આપીને
૧૯૬૦થી ગુજરાતને પડોશી રાજ્યોથી જુદું પાડતી નીતિ કઈ?
riddle_english:
At the state border the car slows and a permit page is asked for;
a guest finds a home here, but not a glass.
What has set Gujarat apart from its neighbours since 1960
by turning a Gandhian vow into law?
riddle_hint: રાજ્યની સ્થાપનાથી અમલમાં રહેલી નીતિ; બહારગામના મુલાકાતીઓને ખાસ પરવાનો આપવામાં આવે છે.
riddle_note: Difficulty: Easy for residents, hard for outsiders. Gujarat-wide policy. NEW. Answer is a policy, not a person or place — deliberately varies the answer type.

riddle_original:
નવાબનો નિર્ણય દરિયાપાર તરફ વળ્યો,
પણ સોરઠની બહુમતી ભારત તરફ રહી.
મુંબઈમાં જાહેર થઈ અને રાજકોટથી કૂચ કરનારી
કઈ કામચલાઉ લોકસરકાર ઊભી થઈ?
riddle_english:
The nawab's signature turned across the sea,
while most of Sorath looked toward India.
Proclaimed in Bombay and marching out of Rajkot,
which provisional people's government arose?

riddle_original:
છાત્રાલયના વધેલા ભોજનખર્ચથી ડિસેમ્બરમાં ચણગારી ઊઠી,
મોંઘવારી અને ભ્રષ્ટાચાર સામે વિદ્યાર્થીઓની હાક ઊઠી.
અમદાવાદથી આખું રાજ્ય રસ્તે ઊતર્યું અને વિધાનસભા વિસર્જિત થઈ—
૧૯૭૩-૭૪ની આ ચળવળ કઈ?
riddle_english:
A hostel mess bill struck the first spark in December;
students raised a cry against prices and corruption.
From Ahmedabad the whole state entered the streets and the assembly was dissolved—
which movement of 1973-74 was this?

riddle_original:
પાક ડૂબ્યો, છતાં કચેરીએ મહેસૂલ માંગ્યું,
નડિયાદમાં લેવાયેલી પ્રતિજ્ઞાએ ગામેગામ ઇનકાર જગાડ્યો.
જપ્ત કરેલી ડુંગળી ઉપાડી લાવનારને લોકોએ ‘ડુંગળીચોર’ કહી વધાવ્યો—
૧૯૧૮ની આ લડત કઈ?
riddle_english:
The crop drowned, yet the office demanded revenue;
a pledge at Nadiad awakened refusal from village to village.
The man who lifted the confiscated onion crop was hailed as the ‘onion thief’—
which struggle of 1918 was this?

riddle_original:
પોતડી ને ખાદી, ચરોતરની ધૂળમાં ઘડાયેલા પગ,
બહારવટિયાના ડેરામાં એકલા જઈ હથિયાર મૂકાવ્યાં.
૧ મે, ૧૯૬૦ના રોજ નવા રાજ્યનું ઉદ્ઘાટન કોઈ મંત્રીએ નહીં,
આ લોકસેવકે કર્યું. કોણ હતા તેઓ?
riddle_english:
A loincloth, khadi, and feet shaped by the dust of Charotar;
he walked alone into outlaws' camps and made them lay down their arms.
On 1 May 1960 the new state was inaugurated not by any minister
but by this servant of the people. Who was he?

riddle_original:
ગાદી હતી, છતાં ગાંધીમાર્ગ ન છોડ્યો;
વાસોમાં મૉન્ટેસરી શાળા ખોલી.
અંગ્રેજ સરકારે રાજ જપ્ત કર્યું, પછી તેઓ બોરસદમાં વસ્યા—
ધસાના આ પ્રજાવત્સલ રાજવી કોણ?
riddle_english:
He had a throne, yet did not abandon the Gandhian path;
at Vaso he opened a Montessori school.
The British government confiscated his state, after which he settled in Borsad—
who was this people-minded ruler of Dhasa?

riddle_original:
રણ વચ્ચે નગર, છતાં તરસ સામે લાચાર નહીં,
પથ્થરના જળાશયો અને ઢાળને અનુસરતી નાળીઓ.
ખડિર બેટની માટીમાં દટાયેલું જળજ્ઞાન—
કયું પ્રાચીન નગર?
riddle_english:
A city in the middle of the desert, yet never a slave to thirst;
stone reservoirs, and channels following every slope.
Water-wisdom lies buried in the soil of Khadir Bet—
which ancient city is it?

riddle_original:
એક નગર નીચે બીજું નગર, માટીના પડ ઉપર પડ,
તોરણ, તળાવ અને ચીની યાત્રિકની નોંધ.
મહેસાણાની ધરતીમાં બે હજારથી વધુ વર્ષથી ધબકતું—
કયું જીવતું નગર?
riddle_english:
One town beneath another, layer upon layer of earth;
a gateway, a lake, and the note of a Chinese pilgrim.
It has pulsed in Mehsana's soil for more than two thousand years—
which living town is it?

riddle_original:
એક જ શિલા પર ત્રણ રાજકાળના અવાજ—
અશોકના ધર્મલેખ, પછી રુદ્રદામન ને સ્કંદગુપ્તના લેખ;
સુદર્શન તળાવ તૂટ્યું ને ફરી બંધાયું તેની નોંધ પણ અહીં.
ગિરનારની તળેટીના આ લેખો કયા?
riddle_english:
Three reigns speak on a single rock—
Ashoka’s edicts, followed by inscriptions of Rudradaman and Skandagupta;
the breaches and repairs of Sudarshana Lake are recorded here too.
What are these inscriptions at the foot of Girnar?

riddle_original:
લોકકથામાં વાટકી દૂધથી છલોછલ,
ખાંડ ઓગળી—જગ્યા લીધા વિના મીઠાશ વધી.
ઉમરગામ પાસે પારસી આગમનની સ્મૃતિ સાચવતું
આ બંદરગામ કયું?
riddle_english:
In the community's tale, a bowl brimmed with milk;
sugar dissolved—sweetness increased without taking any space.
This first shoreline near Umargam,
which port village is it?

riddle_original:
ધ્રોલ પાસેની ધરતી આજેય પાળિયા સાચવે,
જામે આશરો આપ્યો અને મુગલ સેના ચઢી આવી.
લગ્નમંડપ છોડીને શૂરવીરો મેદાને વળ્યાની લોકવાત ચાલે—
૧૫૯૧ની આ લડાઈ કઈ?
riddle_english:
The earth near Dhrol still guards its memorial stones;
a Jam gave refuge and a Mughal force advanced.
The telling goes that warriors turned from a wedding pavilion to the field—
which battle of 1591 was this?

riddle_original:
કાઠિયાવાડથી આવતી ગાડી અહીં અટકે,
પોટલું ખૂલે, જકાત ભરાય અને મુસાફર હેરાન થાય.
પરદેશથી પાછા ફરેલા વકીલે આ પ્રશ્ન ઉપાડ્યો અને ૧૯૧૭માં નાકું દૂર થયું—
ગાંધીજીએ જેને “ભારતમાં સત્યાગ્રહનો આરંભ” કહ્યો, તે કયું નાકું?
riddle_english:
The train coming from Kathiawad stops here;
bundles are opened, duty is paid, the traveller is harassed.
A lawyer returned from overseas took up this grievance and in 1917 the cordon was lifted—
which toll post did Gandhi call “the advent of Satyagraha in India”?

riddle_original:
સિદ્ધરાજે પાટણમાં પાણીનું ભવ્ય સરોવર રચ્યું,
કિનારે શિવલિંગોની લાંબી હાર ગોઠવાઈ.
જસમા ઓડણની લોકકથા આજેય એની સાથે ચાલે—
કયું ભગ્ન સરોવર?
riddle_english:
Siddhraj created a grand reservoir at Patan;
a great series of Shiva lingas lined its banks.
The folk tale of Jasma Odan still walks beside it—
which ruined lake is this?

riddle_original:
નામ મારું અંક પરથી પડ્યું, છતાં ગણતરી અનાજની નહોતી;
વરસાદે મોં ફેરવ્યું, કૂવામાં આકાશ દેખાયું.
સૌરાષ્ટ્રથી વડોદરા સુધી વડીલો વર્ષને ભયથી યાદ કરે—
વિક્રમના છપ્પનમાં આવેલો કયો કાળ?
riddle_english:
My name came from a number, though there was little grain to count;
the rains turned away and wells showed only sky.
From Saurashtra to Baroda, elders remembered the year with fear—
what calamity came in Vikram year fifty-six?

riddle_original:
ઘડિયાળના શહેરમાં એક બપોરે નદીએ સમય ગળી લીધો;
બંધનું પાણી શેરીઓમાં છાપરાંથી ઊંચું બોલ્યું.
પછી દરેક ઘર કાદવમાંથી પોતાનું નામ શોધતું રહ્યું—
મોરબીની આ જળસ્મૃતિ કઈ?
riddle_english:
In the city of clocks, one afternoon the river swallowed time;
water from the dam spoke higher than the rooftops.
Afterwards each household searched the mud for its own names—
what is this water-borne memory of Morbi?

riddle_original:
તિરંગાની સવાર હતી, પણ શાળાની પરેડ પહેલાં ધરતી જ ધ્રૂજી;
ભુજ, ભચાઉ અને અંજાર એક જ ધ્રુજારીમાં જોડાયા.
કચ્છના ઘરોની તારીખ આજે પણ છવ્વીસમી જાન્યુઆરી કહે—
આ કઈ આપત્તિ?
riddle_english:
It was a tricolour morning, but before school parades the earth itself trembled;
Bhuj, Bhachau and Anjar were joined by one violent tremor.
Homes in Kutch still speak the date “twenty-six January”—
which disaster was this?

riddle_original:
રણની ધારે ઘાસનું વિશાળ આંગણું,
ખારી જમીનમાં વિરડો ખોદીને મીઠું પાણી કાઢાય.
અહીં માલધારીઓના નેસ અને ગોળ ભૂંગા વસેલા છે—
ભુજથી ઉત્તરે આવેલો આ પ્રદેશ કયો?
riddle_english:
At the desert's edge, a vast courtyard of grass;
in saline ground a virda is dug to draw fresh water.
Maldhari hamlets and round bhungas live here—
which tract lies north of Bhuj?

riddle_original:
ચોમાસે અરીસો, ઉનાળે મીઠાની ચાદર,
અગરિયાના પગ નીચે સફેદ કમાણી.
ઘુડખરના ડાબલાં જ્યાં સંભળાય—
એ કયું રણ?
riddle_english:
A mirror in the monsoon, a sheet of salt in summer;
white earnings beneath the Agariya's feet.
Where the hoofbeats of the ghudkhar are heard—
which desert is this?

riddle_original:
પહાડ નથી, છતાં ચોમાસે દરિયા જેવું લાગે,
ઓઝત અને ભાદરનાં પાણી આખા નીચાણમાં ફેલાય.
પાણી ઊતરે ત્યારે કાળી માટી પાકને પોષે—
જૂનાગઢ-પોરબંદર વચ્ચેનો આ પ્રદેશ કયો?
riddle_english:
There is no mountain, yet in the monsoon it looks like a sea;
the waters of the Ozat and the Bhadar spread across the low ground.
When the water falls, black soil embraces the crop—
which tract lies between Junagadh and Porbandar?

riddle_original:
એક બાજુ પોરબંદરનો પવન, બીજી બાજુ હાલારની છાંય,
નેસ, ઢોર ને જંગલી ઔષધિનો સાથ.
ગિર જેટલો જાણીતો નહીં, છતાં માલધારીને પ્રિય—
કઈ ડુંગરમાળા?
riddle_english:
Porbandar's wind on one side, Halar's shade on the other;
nes hamlets, cattle and wild medicinal plants together.
Not as famous as Gir, yet dear to pastoralists—
which range of hills is this?

riddle_original:
મહી અને વાત્રક વચ્ચેનો ફળદ્રુપ પટ્ટો,
ગામેગામ દૂધમંડળી, ખેતરોમાં તમાકુ અને ડાંગર.
આણંદ-ખેડાની ઓળખ બનેલું
મધ્ય ગુજરાતનું આ નામ કયું?
riddle_english:
A fertile belt between the Mahi and the Vatrak;
a milk cooperative in village after village, with tobacco and paddy in the fields.
What regional name identifies
much of Anand and Kheda?

riddle_original:
ઓટ ઊતરે ત્યારે દરિયાનો પટ પગપાળા વટાય,
પરવાળાં, કાદવ અને ચેરનાં ઝાડ એક જ દૃશ્યમાં દેખાય.
પિરોટન ટાપુ જેની ઓળખ બન્યો છે—
જામનગર પાસેનું એ કયું ઉદ્યાન?
riddle_english:
When the tide falls, the sea can be read on foot;
coral, mudflat and mangrove appear on a single page.
Pirotan island has become its identity—
which park lies near Jamnagar?

riddle_original:
સમતળ ધરતી, ખારાશનો પડકાર, વરસાદ સિવાય પાણીનો બીજો આધાર નહીં,
ધંધુકા-ધોળકા તરફનાં ખેતરો ખાર સામે લડે.
અહીંનો ઘઉં જાડા દાણાનો અને મીઠાશવાળો—
ખંભાતના અખાત તરફનો આ પ્રદેશ કયો?
riddle_english:
A level plain challenged by salinity, with little water beyond the rain;
fields towards Dhandhuka and Dholka struggle against salt.
Its wheat has a plump grain and a sweetness of its own—
which tract lies towards the Gulf of Khambhat?

riddle_original:
કચ્છનું પૂર્વ પડખું—રણ ને ડુંગર વચ્ચેનો સૂકો ખૂણો,
રાપર ને ભચાઉ જેની ઓળખ.
૨૦૦૧માં ધરતી અહીંથી જ ધ્રૂજી—
કચ્છનો આ પ્રદેશ કયો?
riddle_english:
The eastern flank of Kutch—a dry corner between desert and hill,
known by Rapar and Bhachau.
In 2001 the earth shook from right here—
which tract of Kutch is this?

riddle_original:
ઝાલા રાજપૂતોના નામે ઓળખાયો પ્રદેશ,
વઢવાણ, ધ્રાંગધ્રા ને લીંબડી જેની જૂની ગાદીઓ.
સૂકી ધરતી, પણ ભરત ને વણાટમાં ધનવાન—
સુરેન્દ્રનગર તરફનો આ પ્રદેશ કયો?
riddle_english:
A region named after the Jhala Rajputs;
Wadhwan, Dhrangadhra and Limbdi were its old seats.
Dry land, yet rich in embroidery and weaving—
which tract lies towards Surendranagar?

riddle_original:
નર્મદાના બેટ પર એક જ ઝાડ આખું જંગલ,
વડવાઈઓ ઊતરીને પોતે જ નવા થડ બને.
સંતના નામે ઓળખાતું, શુક્લતીર્થ પાસેનું—
ભરૂચનું આ વૃક્ષ કયું?
riddle_english:
On an island in the Narmada, a single tree is a whole forest;
aerial roots came down and became trunks themselves.
Known by a saint's name, near Shuklatirth—
which tree of Bharuch is this?

riddle_original:
રાત જેવું ઘેરું નીલ, કચ્છની માટી જેવું લાલ,
લાકડાના ઠપ્પાથી તારાઓની જાળી છપાય.
રંગ ચઢે, ધોવાય, ફરી ચઢે—ઘણા તબક્કાનો ધીરજભર્યો ખેલ,
ધમડકાના ખત્રી કારીગરોના હાથની આ છાપકળા કઈ?
riddle_english:
Dark blue as night, red as the earth of Kutch;
wooden blocks count out a lattice of stars.
Colour goes on, is washed off, goes on again—patience through many stages:
which printing craft lives in Khatri hands at Dhamadka?

riddle_original:
પીંછી નહીં—હવામાં અધ્ધર લટકતો ચીકણો તાર,
ઉકાળેલા એરંડિયાના તેલમાંથી બનેલો રંગ લોખંડની સળીથી દોરાય.
એક જ કુટુંબની આંગળીઓથી “જીવનવૃક્ષ” ઊગે—
નિરોણા ગામની આ કળા કઈ?
riddle_english:
No brush—a sticky thread hanging in the air;
an iron stylus draws colour made from heated castor oil.
A ‘tree of life’ grows under one family's fingers—
which craft belongs to the village of Nirona?

riddle_original:
સાળ પર ચઢે તે પહેલાં જ દરેક તાંતણો પોતાની જગ્યા જાણે,
તાણો અને વાણો બંને એક જ નકશો માને.
બંને બાજુ સરખું, અને પેઢીઓની સાધના એક વસ્ત્રમાં—
પાટણના સાલવી પરિવારોનું આ વૈભવ કયું?
riddle_english:
Before reaching the loom, every thread already knows its place;
warp and weft obey a single map.
Identical on both faces, generations of discipline in one cloth—
what is the Salvi families’ splendour of Patan?

riddle_original:
મંદિરમાં પ્રવેશ ન મળ્યો તો કાપડ જ ગર્ભગૃહ બન્યું,
વચ્ચે માતા, આસપાસ કથા, વાહનો અને દેવરૂપો.
વીંટીને ગામેગામ ફરતી આ ચાલતી દેરી—
અમદાવાદ પાસેનું આ પવિત્ર કાપડ કયું?
riddle_english:
When entry to the temple was denied, cloth itself became the sanctum;
the Mother at the centre, with stories, mounts and divine figures around her.
Rolled up and carried from village to village, a shrine that walks—
which sacred printed cloth belongs near Ahmedabad?

riddle_original:
આ ભીંત શણગાર માટે નહીં—માનતા પૂરી થાય ત્યારે ‘લખાય’,
ઘોડેસવાર દેવો, પૂર્વજો અને આખું બ્રહ્માંડ ઊતરે.
રાઠવા ઘરની અંદરની ભીંત પર વિધિથી જન્મે—
છોટાઉદેપુરની આ રચના કઈ?
riddle_english:
This wall is not for decoration—it is ‘written’ when a vow is fulfilled;
horse-riding gods, ancestors and a whole cosmos come down onto it.
Born through ritual on the inner wall of a Rathwa home—
which form belongs to Chhota Udepur?

riddle_original:
લાકડું સંઘાડા પર નાચે, કાળો અને ઘેરો લાલ રંગ ચડે,
લાખની ચમક પર સોનેરી લીટી ઝબકે.
ઘોડિયું, બાજઠ અને ખુરશી—ખરાદીના હાથની ઓળખ,
છોટાઉદેપુરનું કયું ગામ આ કળાને નામ આપે?
riddle_english:
Wood dances on the lathe, as black and deep red sweep past;
golden lines flash over the shine of lac.
Cradles, low stools and chairs carry the Kharadi hand—
which Chhota Udepur town gives the craft its name?

riddle_original:
સોયથી ભરત નહીં, સાળમાં જ દાણા ઊગે,
સૂતરની નાની ગાંઠો કાપડ પરથી બોલે.
સાયલા-સુરેન્દ્રનગર પટ્ટાના ડાંગશિયા વણકરોનું રહસ્ય—
કઈ વણાટકળા?
riddle_english:
Not needlework—the grains grow inside the loom itself;
small knots of yarn speak from the surface of the cloth.
The secret of the Dangasia weaver of the Sayla-Surendranagar belt—
which weave is this?

riddle_original:
ઢોલના ધબકારમાં આફ્રિકાની સ્મૃતિ,
ગીર પાસેના જાંબુરમાં પગ ગોળ ફરતી વીજળી બની જાય.
ઉર્સ અને ઉજવણીઓમાં તાલ ચઢતો જાય—
કયું નૃત્ય?
riddle_english:
African memory beats inside the drum;
at Jambur near Gir, feet become circling lightning.
At urs and at celebrations the rhythm keeps rising—
which dance is this?

riddle_original:
રંગમંચ નહીં—ગામનો ચોરો જ મંચ,
એક પછી એક વેશમાં હાસ્ય સત્તાને ચીમટી ભરે.
અસાઈત ઠાકરની પરંપરા અને ભૂંગળનો લાંબો સૂર—
ઉત્તર ગુજરાતનું આ લોકનાટ્ય કયું?
riddle_english:
No theatre building—the village square is the stage;
in one vesha after another, laughter pinches those in power.
Asaita Thakar's tradition, and the long call of the bhungal—
which folk theatre of North Gujarat is this?

riddle_original:
લાલ કે લીલી ભોંય પર સોનેરી ચોકડીની જાળી,
દરેક ખાનામાં બાંધણીનું નાનું ટપકું.
લગ્નવિધિમાં વહુને સાસરેથી ઓઢાડાતી સાડી—
ગુજરાતી પરંપરાનું આ વસ્ત્ર કયું?
riddle_english:
A grid of golden squares on a red or green ground,
with a small bandhani dot inside each square.
A sari traditionally draped on the bride by her marital family during wedding rites—
which garment of Gujarati tradition is this?

riddle_original:
સાત સપાટ ભાઈઓ એકમેકના માથે ઊભા,
એક દડો બધાને ધરાશાયી કરે.
એક ટોળું ફરી ઘર બાંધે, બીજું પીઠ પર દડો શોધે—
શેરીની આ રમત કઈ?
riddle_english:
Seven flat brothers stand one upon another;
one ball knocks them all down.
One team rebuilds the house while the other hunts their backs with the ball—
which street game is this?

riddle_original:
રેખા પાર કરું ત્યારે શ્વાસ મારી ઘડિયાળ,
એક જ બોલ તૂટે તો દાવ અધૂરો.
કોઈને અડીને પાછો ફરી શકું તો જીત—
આ શ્વાસવાળી રમતનું જૂનું ગુજરાતી નામ શું?
riddle_english:
When I cross the line, my breath becomes the clock;
if the single chant breaks, my raid is unfinished.
Touch someone and return safely, and I win—
what is the older Gujarati name for this breath-bound game?

riddle_original:
જમીન પર આડી પાટીઓ, વચ્ચે એક ઊભી મોભ;
રાખવાળાના પગ રેખા ન છોડે, દોડનાર પાટ પછી પાટ વટાવે.
અડી ગયા તો પાછા, પાર થયા તો ગુણ—
આ જૂની મેદાની રમત કઈ?
riddle_english:
Horizontal lanes cross the ground, with one long central line;
guards keep their feet on the lines while runners pass lane after lane.
A touch sends them back; a crossing earns progress—
which old field game is this?

riddle_original:
મેદાનમાં નહીં, ડાળીઓ પર દાવ;
એક જમીનના કૂંડાળે પહેરો રાખે, બાકીના ઝાડે ચડે.
ડાળીથી ડાળી બચતા ફરવાની
આ બાળરમત કઈ?
riddle_english:
The turn is played not on a field but among branches;
one guards a circle on the ground while the others climb the tree.
Escaping from branch to branch—
which children’s game is this?

riddle_original:
લાકડાના પેટ નીચે લોખંડની અણી,
દોરીની વીંટથી ઘૂમતો જમીન પર ઊતરું.
જે મને જાળમાં ઝીલી હથેળી પર ચડાવે—
શેરીનો એ કયો ખેલ?
riddle_english:
A wooden body holds an iron point;
a wound string sends me spinning onto the ground.
The skilled player catches me in the string and lifts me onto the palm—
which street toy-game am I?

Five small pieces; one flies upward.
Before it returns, the pieces on the ground must be gathered into the hand.
One, then two, then more—the arithmetic of fingers;
which game is played on the otlo?

riddle_original:
મારો હરીફ જમીન પર નહીં, આકાશમાં;
એક હાથ ચરખી થામે, બીજો દોરીને જીવ આપે.
બે દોરી ચોંટે ત્યારે અગાશી શાંત થાય,
એક કપાય ત્યારે આખી શેરી બોલે—આ મુકાબલો શું?

વરસાદ પછી જમીન પોચી થાય એટલે મેદાન તૈયાર;
બે વેંતનો ખીલો જોરથી ફેંકું, ઊભો ખૂંચે તો આગળનો દાવ.
પડી જાય ત્યાં મારી સફર અટકે—
ચોમાસાની આ રમત કઈ?
riddle_english:
After rain softens the earth, the ground is ready;
a long iron spike is thrown, and if it sticks upright the next turn begins.
Where it falls flat, the journey ends—
which monsoon game is this?

riddle_original:
દાવ માથે એકલો, બાકીના આખું મેદાન;
શરૂઆત પહેલાં પીઠ પર ગણાતી સાત હથેળીઓ.
છેલ્લી તાળી પડતાં પીછો છૂટે—
ગુજરાતી શેરીની આ દોડરમત કઈ?
riddle_english:
One player carries the turn while the rest own the field;
before the chase, seven palms are counted on the back.
At the last clap everyone scatters—
which Gujarati running game is this?

riddle_original:
પગથિયાં પરથી ધરતીના પેટમાં ઊતરાય,
થાંભલા અને મૂર્તિઓ વચ્ચે પાણી મંદિર બની જાય.
ઉદયમતીની સ્મૃતિ અને સરસ્વતી કિનારાનો શ્વાસ—
પાટણની આ વાવ કઈ?
riddle_english:
Step by step one descends into the belly of the earth;
among pillars and sculptures, water becomes a temple.
Udayamati's memory and the breath of the Saraswati bank—
which stepwell of Patan is this?

riddle_original:
પછીના કાળનાં ઊંચા શિખરો જેવું નહીં—પથ્થરના પડ પિરામિડ સમા ચડે,
નાનું ગર્ભગૃહ અને આસપાસ જૂનાં શિલ્પના ટુકડા.
ભાણવડ પાસે ઊભેલું, ગુજરાતના સૌથી જૂના પથ્થરના મંદિરોમાંનું એક—
કયું મંદિર?
riddle_english:
Unlike the tall spires of later temples, its stone courses rise like a pyramid;
a small sanctum stands amid fragments of old sculpture.
Near Bhanvad, it is among Gujarat’s oldest surviving stone temples—
which temple is it?

riddle_original:
પર્વત પર કિલ્લો અને જીવતું શક્તિસ્થાન,
તળેટીમાં મસ્જિદ, મહેલ, વાવ અને જૂનું બજાર.
હિંદુ અને ઇસ્લામી સ્થાપત્યના થર એક જ નકશામાં—
પંચમહાલનું આ સંકુલ કયું?
riddle_english:
A fort on the hill and a living shrine of the Goddess;
mosques, palaces, stepwells and an old market on the plain below.
Hindu and Islamic layers on a single map—
which ensemble of Panchmahal is this?

riddle_original:
ક્યારેક શહેરની બહાર સૂફીનું નિવાસ,
રોજો, મસ્જિદ અને પહોળું તળાવ એક જ શાંત દૃશ્યમાં ભળે.
મહમૂદ બેગડાના યુગનું સ્થાપત્ય અને શેખ અહમદ ખટ્ટુની યાદ—
અમદાવાદનું આ સંકુલ કયું?
riddle_english:
Once a Sufi retreat outside the city;
tomb, mosque and broad tank breathe as one quiet whole.
Architecture of Mahmud Begada’s era meets the memory of Shaikh Ahmad Khattu—
which complex of Ahmedabad is this?

riddle_original:
ઉપરકોટના પથ્થરમાં જ કૂવો કોતરાયો,
પાણી સુધી સીડી સાપની જેમ વળે.
સૂરજનું કિરણ ભાગ્યે જ તળિયે પહોંચે—
જૂનાગઢનો આ કૂવો કયો?
riddle_english:
The well was carved into the very rock of Uparkot;
the stairway coils like a snake down to the water.
A ray of sun rarely reaches the bottom—
which well of Junagadh is this?

riddle_original:
કિલ્લાની દીવાલ ખાડીને તાકે, શેરીઓમાં પવન જ વસ્તી ગણે,
ક્યારેક બંદરે વેપાર ધમધમતો, પછી નદીએ રસ્તો બદલ્યો.
ગુરુદ્વારા, દરગાહ અને સૂની ગલીઓ સાથે ઊભું—
કચ્છનું આ સરહદી નગર કયું?
riddle_english:
Fort walls stare at the creek while the wind counts the population in the lanes;
trade once thronged the port, then the river changed its course.
A gurdwara, dargahs and empty lanes still stand together—
which frontier town of Kutch is this?

riddle_original:
એક હરોળમાં આછા રંગના ઊંચા મુખડા,
લાકડાની જાળી પાસે પરદેશી ઘાટની બારી.
વ્હોરવાડની ગલીમાં વેપારી કુટુંબોની યાદ—
સિદ્ધપુરની આ કઈ હવેલીઓ?
riddle_english:
Tall pale-coloured façades in a row;
a window of foreign form beside Gujarati woodwork.
Merchant families remembered in a vohravad lane—
which havelis of Siddhpur are these?

riddle_original:
સંજાણની સ્મૃતિથી ઉદવાડા સુધી જ્યોતની યાત્રા,
નાનું દરિયાકાંઠાનું ગામ પારસી જગતનું મોટું તીર્થ બન્યું.
અહીં અગ્નિ માત્ર જળતો નહીં, શ્રદ્ધાથી સંભાળાય—
કયું અતિ પવિત્ર અગ્નિસ્થાન?
riddle_english:
From the memory of Sanjan to Udvada, a journey of flame;
a small coastal village became a great pilgrimage of the Parsi world.
Here the fire does not merely burn; it is guarded with devotion—
which most sacred fire-house is this?

riddle_original:
એક મિનાર હલે તો બીજો પણ ધ્રૂજે,
વચ્ચેની દીવાલ સ્થિર જ રહે.
અમદાવાદના કાલુપુર પાસે ઊભેલો આ કોયડો—
કયું સ્થાપત્ય?
riddle_english:
Shake one minaret and the other trembles too,
while the wall between them stays still.
This puzzle standing near Kalupur in Ahmedabad—
which structure is it?

riddle_original:
અંબાજીથી થોડે દૂર, દાંતાની સીમમાં આરસનાં પાંચ દેરાં,
બહાર સાદાં, અંદરની છતો કોતરણીથી છલકાય.
યાત્રાળુઓની ભીડથી દૂર સોલંકીકાળ સચવાયો—
બનાસકાંઠાનું આ સ્થાન કયું?
riddle_english:
A little way from Ambaji, in the fields of Danta, five marble shrines;
plain outside, with carving that fills the ceilings within.
The Solanki age is preserved here without any crush of pilgrims—
which site in Banaskantha is this?

riddle_original:
મૂછ હતી, છતાં બાળકો તેમને ‘મા’ કહેતાં,
અદાલતના કાગળો મૂકીને બાળમંદિરનું બારણું ખોલ્યું.
અમરેલીના ચિત્તળમાં જન્મ્યા, ભાવનગરમાં નવું સ્વપ્ન સાકાર કર્યું—
આ કેળવણીકાર કોણ?
riddle_english:
He had a moustache, yet the children called him ‘Mother’;
he put down the court papers and opened the door of a nursery school.
Born at Chittal in Amreli, he dreamed a new dream in Bhavnagar—
who was this educator?

riddle_original:
મોઢું બકરાનું, પણ ચિંતા વેપારી જેવી,
મુંબઈના બંગલામાં શકરી સાથે રોજનો ગોટાળો.
વાઘજીભાઈ વકીલ આવે અને હાસ્ય શરૂ—
‘ગાંડીવ’નાં પાનાંનો આ શેઠ કોણ?
riddle_english:
A goat's face with a trader's worries;
daily muddles with Shakri in a Bombay bungalow.
When Vaghjibhai the lawyer arrives, the laughter starts—
who is this sheth from the pages of ‘Gandiv’?

riddle_original:
બોલે—“અમે કોણ? સિપાઈ બચ્ચા!”
પણ જોખમ દેખાય તો મૂછમાં ધ્રુજારી.
તભા ભટ્ટ સાથે હોય તો ગોટાળો પણ જીત બની જાય—
જીવરામ જોષીનું આ પાત્ર કોણ?
riddle_english:
He declares, “Who are we? Soldier's sons!”
but when danger appears, the moustache trembles.
With Tabha Bhatt along, even a muddle turns into victory—
which character did Jivram Joshi create?

riddle_original:
ગામ તેમને ડાહ્યા ગણે અને એ જ ગામ તેમની મશ્કરી કરે,
એક બોલે તો બીજો ઊંધો અર્થ પકડે.
જીવરામ જોષીની વાર્તાઓમાં હંમેશાં જોડે ફરતા—
આ બે હાસ્યભાઈ કોણ?
riddle_english:
The village calls them wise and the village laughs at them;
when one speaks, the other catches the opposite meaning.
Always travelling as a pair in Jivram Joshi's stories—
who are these two comic fellows?

riddle_original:
પૂંછડી લાંબી, પણ બુદ્ધિ એથીય લાંબી,
જંગલના રાજા સામે પણ વાતચીતથી રસ્તો કાઢે.
મોડાસા પંથકના લેખકે બાળકોને આપેલો—
આ ચતુર શિયાળ કોણ?
riddle_english:
The tail is long, but the wit is longer still;
even before the king of the forest he talks his way out.
Given to children by a writer of the Modasa region—
who is this clever jackal?

riddle_original:
કાપડના ટુકડામાં ચહેરો, ભરતના દોરાથી કપડાં,
રબારી બહેનના હાથમાં કાપડનો કટકો રમકડું નહીં, સ્મૃતિ બને.
સુમરાસર શેખમાં વર-કન્યા જેવી જોડી ઊભી થાય—
કચ્છની આ જોડીનું નામ શું?
riddle_english:
A face out of a scrap of cloth, clothes out of embroidery thread;
in a Rabari woman's hand a leftover piece becomes memory, not a toy.
At Sumrasar Sheikh a pair stands dressed like bride and groom—
what is this Kutchi pair called?

riddle_original:
મા-બાપ મીઠાના અગરમાં મહિનાઓ રહે,
બાળકનું ગામ પાછળ રહી જાય—પણ ભણતર નહીં.
વર્ગખંડ પણ ઋતુ સાથે નાના રણમાં ઊતરે—
અગરિયાનાં બાળકોની આ શાળા કઈ?
riddle_english:
Parents spend months in the salt pans;
the child's village is left behind—but not the schooling.
The classroom too moves with the season into the Little Rann—
which school serves Agariya children?

riddle_original:
પૂછે છે—“કેટલે?” અને જવાબમાં દીવો બળે,
દીવો ઓલવાય તો રસ્તો પણ ખૂટે.
ગુજરાતી બાળપણનું આ જાણીતું જોડકણું
કઈ પંક્તિથી શરૂ થાય?

ચકી લાવી ચોખાનો દાણો, ચકો લાવ્યો મગનો દાણો,
ખીચડી રંધાઈ અને પછી આખી વાર્તા ગૂંચવાઈ.
ગુજરાતી બાળપણની જાણીતી લોકવાર્તાની
આ પંખીઓની જોડી કઈ?

રમત શરૂ થાય તે પહેલાં જ બોલાય,
આંગળી ફરે ને છેલ્લે જેના પર અટકે તે દાવ લે.
અર્થ કોઈ ન સમજાવે, છતાં આખું ગુજરાત જાણે—
કયું જોડકણું?
riddle_english:
It is said before the game even begins;
a finger moves around and whoever it stops on takes the turn.
No one explains its meaning, yet all Gujarat knows it—
which counting rhyme is this?

riddle_original:
ચોરસ નહીં—ગોળ ભીંતો રણના પવનને વાળી દે,
માટી અને છાણના લીંપણમાં આભલા ઝબકે.
શંકુઆકાર છાપરું બન્નીના પરિવારને આશરો આપે—
કચ્છનું આ ઘર કયું?
riddle_english:
Not square—the round walls turn the desert wind aside;
small mirrors glint in the mud-and-dung plaster.
A conical roof shelters a Banni household—
what is this Kutch house called?

riddle_original:
આજુબાજુ ખારું, વચ્ચે મીઠું—રણનો નાનો ચમત્કાર,
વરસાદ પછી નીચાણમાં હાથે ખોદાતો છીછરો ખાડો.
બન્નીના માલધારીને મીઠા પાણીનો છુપો થર આપે—
આ જળપરંપરા કઈ?
riddle_english:
Salty all around, sweet in the middle—a small miracle of the desert;
after the rains a shallow pit is dug by hand in the low ground.
It gives the Banni pastoralist a hidden layer of water—
what is this water practice called?

riddle_original:
ઘર પણ નહીં, શેરી પણ નહીં—બંને વચ્ચેનો ઊંચો શ્વાસ,
સવારે દાતણ, બપોરે કામ, સાંજે પડોશીની વાત.
જૂની પોળના બારણા આગળનું આ નાનું મંચ—
ગુજરાતીમાં શું કહેવાય?
riddle_english:
Neither house nor street—a raised breath between the two;
tooth-twig in the morning, work at noon, neighbours' talk in the evening.
This small platform in front of an old pol doorway—
what is it called in Gujarati?

riddle_original:
થાંભલો છે, પણ ઉપર રાજાની મૂર્તિ નથી,
છત્રી નીચે દાણા ભરેલું પક્ષીઓનું ચોગાન છે.
પોળવાસી રોજ ચણ મૂકે અને પાંખો શહેરને જીવતું રાખે—
આ ઊંચું દાણઘર શું?
riddle_english:
It is a pillar, but no king's statue stands on it;
there is a canopy and a grain-court for birds.
Pol residents put out feed daily and wings keep the city alive—
what is this raised granary called?

riddle_original:
રાત્રે દરવાજો બંધ થાય અને અંદરની ગલી પોતાનું ગામ બને,
ખડકી પછી ચોક, અને જોડાયેલાં ઘરોમાં સહિયારું જીવન.
આવી ગોઠવણીથી જૂનું શહેર રચાયું—
અમદાવાદનો આ પડોશ કયો?
riddle_english:
At night the gate closes and the lane inside becomes its own village;
a khadki opens to a chowk, and joined houses share a common life.
The city was formed out of these old arrangements—
what is this Ahmedabad neighbourhood called?

riddle_original:
ગામથી નાનું, પણ થોડાં ઘરોથી મોટું,
ઢોરના રસ્તા સાથે ઠેકાણું ક્યારેક બદલાય.
ગીર અને બરડામાં માલધારી કુટુંબોનો નાનો વસવાટ—
કઈ વસાહત?
riddle_english:
Smaller than a village, but more than just a few houses;
its location may sometimes shift with cattle routes.
A small settlement of Maldhari families in Gir and Barda—
what is it called?

riddle_original:
દુકાનનું મકાન નહીં, અઠવાડિયાનો નક્કી દિવસ,
એક ગામનું શાક, બીજા ગામની ટોપલીઓ, જંગલની ઊપજ અને સમાચાર.
રાઠવા-ભીલ પટ્ટામાં ખરીદી કરતાં મળવાનું વધારે—
આ સાપ્તાહિક બજાર શું?
riddle_english:
Not a permanent shop, but a fixed day of the week;
vegetables from one village, baskets from another, forest produce and news.
In the Rathwa-Bhil belt there is often more meeting than buying—
what is this weekly market called?

riddle_original:
બેઠકખંડની છતેથી બે સાંકળ લટકે,
મહેમાન આવે તો પહેલી બેઠક ત્યાં જ મળે.
ચા, છાપું અને બપોરની નિરાંત જેના પર બેસે—
ગુજરાતી ઘરની આ ઓળખ શું?
riddle_english:
Two chains hang from the ceiling of the sitting room;
when a guest arrives, the first seat offered is there.
Tea, the newspaper and an afternoon's ease all sit on it—
what is this mark of a Gujarati home?

riddle_original:
ઘરનું નાનું બારણું નહીં—ગાડું નીકળે એવડું મોટું,
ઉપર કોતરણીવાળી કમાન, અંદર ફળિયું.
“એને હાથ દેવો” એટલે ઘર બંધ કરવું—
કાઠિયાવાડી ઘરનું આ પ્રવેશદ્વાર શું?
riddle_english:
Not a small house door—wide enough for a cart to pass;
a carved arch above, a courtyard within.
To ‘lay a hand on it’ means to shut up the house—
what is this entrance of a Kathiawadi home?

riddle_original:
રસ્તાની ધારે માટલું ને ઉપર ઢાંકણ,
કોઈ પૈસા લેતું નથી, છતાં રોજ ભરાય.
ઉનાળે વટેમાર્ગુની તરસ છીપાવવાનું પુણ્ય—
ગુજરાતીમાં આ ઠેકાણું શું કહેવાય?
riddle_english:
An earthen pot by the roadside with a lid on top;
nobody takes money, yet it is filled every day.
The merit of quenching a traveller's thirst in summer—
what is this place called in Gujarati?

riddle_original:
લાપસીની જેમ વહેતું નહીં, થાળીમાં દાણાદાર છૂટું પડે;
ઘઉં, ગોળ ને ઘીનો શુકન સૌ પહેલાં પીરસાય.
લગ્ન કે શુભ કામે મીઠું મોં કરાવતી
ગુજરાતી ઘરની આ વાનગી કઈ?
riddle_english:
It does not flow like lapsi; it sits loose and grainy on the plate.
Wheat, jaggery and ghee arrive first as an auspicious taste.
At a wedding or new beginning, which Gujarati household dish
sweetens the mouth?

riddle_original:
દૂધ ધીમે ધીમે ઘટે અને ઘઉંના ફાડા તેમાં ભળે,
જાયફળ, એલચી અને પિસ્તાથી દાણાદાર સોનેરી મીઠાઈ બને.
ખંભાતની સદી જૂની ઓળખ—
કઈ મીઠાઈ?
riddle_english:
Milk reduces slowly and cracked wheat is mixed into it;
nutmeg, cardamom and pistachio make a grainy golden square.
A century-old identity of Khambhat—
which sweet is this?

riddle_original:
રણછોડરાયનાં દર્શન પછી બજારમાં સુગંધ બોલાવે,
મેથીવાળું ચણાના લોટનું ખીરું તેલમાં ગોળ ગોળ ફૂલે.
દહીં કે ચટણી સાથે, અને નામ યાત્રાધામનું—
કયું ગરમ ફરસાણ?
riddle_english:
After darshan of Ranchhodrai, a fragrance calls from the market;
balls of spiced gram batter swell in the oil.
Eaten with curd or chutney, and named after the pilgrim town—
which hot farsan is this?

riddle_original:
ડાંગના ઢોળાવે નાનું લાલાશ પડતું દાણું ઊગે,
ઘંટીમાં દળાય ને તવા પર જાડો રોટલો થાય.
ગોળ-માખણ કે શાક સાથે આદિવાસી થાળીમાં આવે—
કયો રોટલો?
riddle_english:
A small reddish grain grows on the slopes of Dang;
it is ground at the mill and becomes a thick flatbread on the griddle.
It comes to the Adivasi plate with jaggery and butter, or with a vegetable—
which rotlo is this?

riddle_original:
શિયાળામાં દાણા કુમળા હોય ત્યારે જ તોડાય,
જુવારનાં લીલાં મોતી આગ પર શેકાય અને લાકડીથી ખંખેરાય.
સેવ અને લીંબુ સાથે સુરતના રસ્તાઓ ટૂંકી ઋતુ ઉજવે—
આ લીલા શેકેલા દાણા શું કહેવાય?
riddle_english:
Only in winter are the grains taken while still tender;
green pearls of sorghum are roasted over fire and beaten free with a stick.
With sev and lemon, Surat’s streets celebrate a short season—
what are these roasted green grains called?

riddle_original:
શાક માટલામાં ભરાય ને માટલું ધરતીમાં ઊંધું દટાય,
ઉપર સૂકાં પાંદડાંનો ધીમો તાપ.
નામ જ રીત કહી દે—
સુરત તરફનું આ શિયાળુ ભોજન કયું?
riddle_english:
The vegetables are packed into an earthen pot and the pot is buried upside down;
a slow fire of dry leaves burns above it.
The name itself gives away the method—
which winter dish of the Surat side is this?

riddle_original:
રીંગણ સીધું ધુમાડામાં શેકાય, છાલ કાળી થાય,
મસળી તેમાં લસણ, તેલ અને લીલી ડુંગળી ભળે.
બાજરીના રોટલા અને ગોળ સાથે કાઠિયાવાડી શિયાળાની થાળી પૂરી થાય—
આ વાનગી કઈ?
riddle_english:
The brinjal is roasted straight in the smoke until the skin turns black;
it is mashed and mixed with garlic, oil and spring onion.
With bajra rotla and jaggery, a Kathiawadi winter is complete—
which dish is this?

riddle_original:
હજુ પાપડ બન્યો નથી, છતાં વાટકી ખાલી થાય;
ચોખાના લોટને ઉકળતા પાણીમાં લાકડી ફેરવે.
તેલ, જીરું અને મરચું ઉપર પડે—
રસોડાનું આ ગરમ મધ્યપગથિયું શું?
riddle_english:
It has not yet become papad, yet the bowl is already emptied;
rice flour is stirred into boiling water with a wooden handle.
Oil, cumin and chilli fall on top—
what is this hot in-between stage of the Gujarati kitchen?

riddle_original:
અડદનો લોટ, ગુંદર ને ઘી—શિયાળાની દવા જેવી મીઠાઈ,
સૂંઠ ને ગંઠોડાની ગરમી અંદર છુપાયેલી.
માગશર બેસે ત્યારે ઘરમાં ડબ્બો ભરાય—
કઈ મીઠાઈ?
riddle_english:
Urad flour, edible gum and ghee—a sweet that feels like winter medicine;
the warmth of dry ginger and ganthoda hidden inside.
When Magshar begins, homes fill a tin with it—
which sweet is this?

riddle_original:
વસંતમાં ઝાડ નીચે સફેદ ફૂલ ખરે, વહેલી સવારે વીણાય,
સૂકવીને વરસભર સાચવાય.
ડાંગ અને છોટાઉદેપુરનાં રસોડાંમાં લોટ, લાપસી કે બીજી વાનગીમાં વપરાય—
કયું ફૂલ?
riddle_english:
In spring, pale flowers fall beneath the tree and are gathered at first light;
they are dried and kept through the year.
In kitchens of Dang and Chhota Udepur they may be used in flour, porridge or other foods—
which flower is this?

riddle_original:
છત્રી વરસાદ માટે નહીં—વરસભર કરેલું ભરત બતાવવા,
ઢોલ અને જોડિયા પાવા વચ્ચે રંગીન વેશ ગોળ ફરે.
ત્રિનેત્રેશ્વરના કુંડ પાસે ભાદરવાની ભીડ—
થાનગઢ પાસેનો કયો મેળો?
riddle_english:
The umbrella is not for rain—it displays a year of embroidery;
between drums and twin flutes, colourful dress turns in circles.
Bhadarva crowds beside Trinetreshwar's tank—
which fair is held near Thangadh?

riddle_original:
સાત નદીઓના સંગમે કારતકનો ચાંદ તંબુ જગાડે,
ગધેડાંના રેંકાણમાં વેપાર અને યાત્રા ભળે.
ધોળકા તરફ સંગમની રેતી પર ઊભરાતો—
કયો મેળો?
riddle_english:
At the meeting of seven rivers, the Kartik moon wakes the tents;
trade and pilgrimage mingle with the braying of donkeys.
Rising on the confluence sands towards Dholka—
which fair is this?

riddle_original:
ગિરનારની તળેટીમાં આખી રાત ‘બમ બમ’,
મધરાતે સાધુઓની રવેડી મૃગીકુંડ તરફ વળે.
મહાશિવરાત્રીએ જૂનાગઢમાં જાગતો—
કયો મેળો?
riddle_english:
All night at the foot of Girnar, cries of ‘Bam Bam’;
at midnight a procession of ascetics turns towards Mrigi Kund.
Awake in Junagadh on Mahashivratri—
which fair is this?

riddle_original:
મેશ્વોના કિનારે કારતકી પૂનમ,
ભીલો અને ગરાસિયાઓ પગપાળા આવીને ‘કાળિયા દેવ’ને બોલાવે.
અરવલ્લીની રાતે વેપાર, ભજન અને સ્નાન ભળે—
કયો મેળો?
riddle_english:
Kartik full moon beside the Meshwo;
Bhil and Garasia pilgrims come on foot and call upon the ‘dark god’.
Trade, hymns and bathing mingle through an Aravalli night—
which fair is this?

riddle_original:
રાજમહેલનો દરબાર નહીં—આહવાના મેદાનમાં લોકોનો દરબાર,
હોળીની ઋતુએ ડાંગી રાજાઓની જૂની બેઠક ઉજવણી બની જાય.
પાવરી, ઢોલ ને ગામેગામના વેશ સાથે—
કયો ઉત્સવ?
riddle_english:
Not a palace court—a people's court on the grounds of Ahwa;
in the Holi season, an old assembly of Dangi chiefs becomes a celebration.
With pawri, drums and village dress—
which festival is this?

riddle_original:
હોળી પછીના દિવસોમાં રાઠવા ટોળાં રસ્તા રંગે,
પાવો બોલે અને ઘૂઘરાવાળા પગથી ધરતી માપે.
મોરપીંછની ટોપી અને ગોળ નૃત્યથી ધબકતું—
છોટાઉદેપુરનું કયું મેળાવડું?
riddle_english:
In the days after Holi the Rathwa colour the roads;
the pavo calls and ankle bells measure the earth with the feet.
Alive with peacock-feather caps and circling dance—
which gathering of Chhota Udepur is this?

riddle_original:
અમાસની આગલી રાતે નદીકિનારે સ્મરણનું રુદન,
સવાર પડે તો રંગ, ઢોલ ને મેળાનો નવો સૂર.
સાબરમતી, આકુળ ને વ્યાકુળના ત્રિવેણી પાસે—
ભીલ-ગરાસિયાનો કયો મેળો?
riddle_english:
On the night before the new moon, weeping of remembrance by the river;
when morning comes, colour, drums and a new note of the fair.
Beside the meeting of the Sabarmati, the Akul and the Vyakul—
which Bhil-Garasia fair is this?

riddle_original:
શરદ પૂનમ પછીની રાત, અને ચાંદ હજી થાળીમાં જ રહે,
અગાશીઓ અને મેદાનોમાં મીઠી ઘારી અને તીખું ભૂસું ભેગાં થાય.
આખું શહેર રાત્રે બહાર જમે—
