સુરતનો કયો પડવો?
riddle_english:
The night after Sharad Purnima, and the moon still stays on the plate;
on terraces and open grounds, sweet ghari meets sharp bhusu.
The whole city eats outdoors that night—
which Padvo belongs to Surat?

riddle_original:
ખીજડાના લાકડાનો રથ, ઉપર પાંચ જ્યોત,
ગામના સત્તાવીસ ઠેકાણે એને ઘી ચઢાવાય.
આસો સુદ નોમની રાતે શેરીઓમાં ઘીની નદીઓ વહે—
ગાંધીનગર પાસેના ગામનું આ પર્વ કયું?
riddle_english:
A chariot of khijada wood, with five flames upon it;
ghee is poured on it at twenty-seven places in the village.
On the ninth night of Aso Sud, rivers of ghee flow through the lanes—
which festival belongs to this village near Gandhinagar?

riddle_original:
દીકરીના લગ્ન કે સીમંત ટાણે મામા ગાડું ભરીને આવે,
સાડી, દાગીના અને મીઠાઈ આખી નાતની સામે મૂકાય.
નરસિંહ મહેતાની જાણીતી કથા પણ આ જ વિધિની—
કઈ પરંપરા?
riddle_english:
At a daughter’s wedding or simant ceremony, the maternal family arrives with gifts;
saris, ornaments and sweets are displayed before the community.
Narsinh Mehta’s famous tale is linked to this same custom—
which tradition is it?

riddle_original: Nemcsak a mezőgazdaságból élőknek, de egy zöld-fehér sportklubnak is főnöke lett.
riddle_english: He became the boss not only of those living off agriculture but also of a green‑white sports club.

riddle_original: A déli féltekére akart egy ott is honos gyümölcsöt exportálni ez a politikus.
riddle_english: This politician wanted to export to the southern hemisphere a fruit native there as well.

riddle_original: A magyar tenger partján mondott beszédet egy politikus, nem kellett volna.
riddle_english: A politician gave a speech on the shore of the ‘Hungarian sea’—he shouldn’t have.

riddle_original: Elismerte, hogy néhány napszakban nem mondtak igazat, és nem ő volt az első ilyen.
riddle_english: He admitted they didn’t tell the truth at certain times of day—and he wasn’t the first to do so.

riddle_original: Egy tornászlány, aki később sporteseményeket közvetített, de a magyarok egy nagy részének más jut róla eszébe.
riddle_english: A gymnast who later broadcast sports events, but most Hungarians think of something else about her.

riddle_original: Kedvenc szeszesitaláról elnevezett hírhedt bűnöző.
riddle_english: A notorious criminal nicknamed after his favorite liquor.

riddle_original: Női keresztneve ellenére egy kegyetlen külföldi bérgyilkos, kiirtott egy ismert alföldi családot.
riddle_english: Despite a woman’s given name, a cruel foreign hitman who wiped out a well‑known Great Plain family.

riddle_original: Egy idősebb úrnak szóló kedves gyermeki köszöntést is jelenthetne ennek a hazánkban is rettegett ukrán bűnözőnek a neve.
riddle_english: This feared Ukrainian criminal’s name could also mean a child’s kind greeting to an older gentleman.

riddle_original: Utasokat szállítók maguk akadályozták a forgalmat a székesfőváros útjain.
riddle_english: Passenger carriers themselves blocked traffic on the capital’s roads.

riddle_original: Egy juhász nem csak focipályát épített, de még az utolsó vacsorát is eladta, el is zárták.
riddle_english: A shepherd not only built a football pitch but ‘sold the Last Supper’—and was locked up.

riddle_original: Mi volt a hazát szerző magyarok jellegzetes harci taktikája, mit tudtak négylábúak hátáról nagyon jól csinálni?
riddle_english: What was the hallmark battle tactic of the homeland‑securing Hungarians—what could they do very well from the back of four‑legged animals?
reference_answer_english: Shooting arrows backward while feigning retreat

riddle_original: A monda, amiben egy magyar megölte ellenségét egy hangszerrel.
riddle_english: The legend in which a Hungarian killed his enemy with a musical instrument.

riddle_original: A magyar hős egy-egy máshitűt a két hóna alá csapott, egyet a foga közé szorított és úgy járta.
riddle_english: The Hungarian hero tucked one unbeliever under each arm, clenched one between his teeth, and paraded that way.

riddle_original: Hogy hívták születésekor azt híres ősünket, akit egy napon ünnepelünk az új kenyérrel?
riddle_english: What was the birth name of our famous forebear whom we celebrate on the new‑bread holiday?

riddle_original: Egy bátor magyar, aki fejest ugrott a hazáért, miközben ölelt egy idegen jelképet. Nem is volt magyar, sőt, nem is létezett.
riddle_english: A brave Hungarian who dived headfirst for the homeland while embracing a foreign symbol. He wasn’t Hungarian—and didn’t even exist.

riddle_original: Ha megkondul a nap derekán, mind tudjuk az okát, valaki győzött valahol.
riddle_english: When the bell tolls at midday we all know the reason: someone won somewhere.

riddle_original: Korábban bolgár, tejszínű erődítmény volt, ma már más nyelvet beszélnek itt.
riddle_english: Once a Bulgarian ‘cream‑colored’ fortress—today they speak a different language here.

riddle_original: Sötét erők támogatták, de mikor meghalt, a hazugság ellenfeleként siratták.
riddle_english: Dark forces supported him, yet when he died, they mourned him as an opponent of lies.

riddle_original: Szerencsétlen szám, főleg ha nyakkendő helyett más van a nyakad körül.
riddle_english: An unlucky number—especially if something other than a tie is around your neck.

riddle_original: Bátor suhancok egy ellenségről elnevezett “tüzes itallal” támadtak idegenből érkező “nagyobb testvéreikre”.
riddle_english: Brave lads attacked the ‘bigger brothers’ arriving from abroad with a fiery drink named after the enemy.

riddle_original: Hogyan lehet eljutni az Osztyapenkótól a Felszabra?
riddle_english: How do you get from Osztyapenko to Felszab?

riddle_original: A reformátusoknak olyan ez a város, mint hitbéli társaiknak Csizmaország központja.
riddle_english: For Calvinists this city is like the boot‑country’s capital for their co‑believers.

riddle_original: Itt könyeret möggyel ösznek és korábban meggyűlt a bajuk a vízzel.
riddle_english: Here they ‘öt’ bread with cherries, and earlier they had trouble with water.

riddle_original: Melyik az a híres budapesti építmény, amit olyan állat őriz, amelyiknek hiányzik a nyelve
riddle_english: Which famous Budapest structure is guarded by an animal that lacks a tongue?

riddle_original: Korábban egy bajszos idegen nevét viselte, ma már egy vízfolyásét ez a település
riddle_english: This settlement once bore the name of a mustached foreigner; today it bears that of a watercourse.

riddle_original: Ez a dunántúli hely visszamondja neked, amit kiabálsz, de vigyázz, a szerzetesek is hallják.
riddle_english: This Transdanubian spot echoes what you shout—careful, the monks hear it too.

riddle_original: Hogy jutok legkönnyebben a Hősökről a Moszkvára?
riddle_english: What’s the easiest way from Heroes’ to Moscow Square?

riddle_original: Egy hely, ahol az első magyar belépett a Kárpát-medencébe és egy műalkotás, ami erről készült.
riddle_english: A place where the first Hungarian entered the Carpathian Basin—and an artwork made about it.

riddle_original: Valahol lóháton állva kancsikát csattogtatnak, így igazítják a nagytestű kérődzőket útba.
riddle_english: Somewhere they stand on horseback cracking whips to direct the large ruminants.

riddle_original: Bár korábban három tenger mosta partjaink, mára nekünk ez maradt, de nagyon szeretjük.
riddle_english: Though once three seas washed our shores, this is what remains to us now—and we love it.

riddle_original: Viccek agyafúrt gyerekszereplője, ‘90 előtt így általában így hívták, utána meg úgy.
riddle_english: The clever child character of jokes—before ’90 he was usually called this, after ’90 that.

riddle_original: Egy hosszú faágat nyújt ki karjával, úgy mutatja a pökhendi idegen lovasnak merre van az arra.
riddle_english: He extends a long tree branch with his arm to show the arrogant foreign rider the way.

riddle_original: Kamaszok védik a játszóterüket a színes felsőruhás nagyfiúk ellen, közben egyiküket árulással vádolják és szegény meg is hal.
riddle_english: Teens defend their turf against big boys in colorful tops; one is accused of betrayal and sadly dies.

riddle_original: Egy kotlós nagyon jól érzi magát a házban, a Teremtő jól rendezte el a sorsát, de egy kutyának el kell magyarázni, hogy nem szabad őt bántania.
riddle_english: A broody hen feels great at home—the Creator arranged her fate well—but a dog must be taught not to harm her.

riddle_original: Valakinek egy kés van a hátában, de nem adja vissza a jogos tulajdonosának. Egy slampos öreg meg csak kavar a háttérben, miközben csattognak a pofonok.
riddle_english: Someone has a knife in his back but won’t return it to its owner; a slovenly old man just schemes while slaps crack.

riddle_original: A főhős magas tudományos kitüntetést nyer kártyán. Később titkárául szegődik egy fura alak, akit kitüntetnek helyette egy katonai szervezetben is. Egy igen értékes autó is központi szerepet kap.
riddle_english: The protagonist wins a high scientific honor at cards. Later he hires a strange secretary who is decorated instead in a military body. A very valuable car also plays a central role.

riddle_original: Nem csillagokról szól. Két kisgyereket messzire hurcolnak otthonról, de később egy óriási birodalom központjából is megszöknek, hősiesen küzdenek ellene a vár fokán.
riddle_english: Not about stars. Two small children are taken far from home; later they escape from an empire’s capital and fight heroically on a castle rampart.

riddle_original: Egy furcsa szívű ember gyermekeinek romantikus kalandjai.
riddle_english: The romantic adventures of a man with a strange heart’s children.

riddle_original: Egy kemény, de tisztességes öreghez kerülnek a kamaszfiúk, akik megemberesedve tértek haza a balatoni nyári vakációból.
riddle_english: Teenage boys end up with a tough but fair old man after returning matured from a Balaton summer holiday.

riddle_original: Fél tucat és egy napja csak anyukám jár a fejemben. Megy felfelé egy lavórt cipelve a ház felső szintjére, ősz haja lobban.
riddle_english: For half a dozen and a day I can think only of my mum; she climbs upstairs with a basin, her gray hair flaring.

riddle_original: Gyorsléptű katona, egész magas rangig vitte. Mégis az egész ország tegezte és imádta, pedig végül nem is itt kergette a pettyest.
riddle_english: A quick‑stepping ‘soldier’ rose to high rank; the whole country addressed him informally and adored him—yet in the end he chased the ball abroad.

riddle_original: Megtelt a betonteknő, mikor a rendőrök és a katonák népszerű labdazsonglőrei csaptak össze.
riddle_english: The concrete bowl filled up when the police and soldiers’ popular ball‑jugglers clashed.

riddle_original: Ugyan kettőnél többet kaptunk, de a dupláját adtuk cserébe, gombócból is sok, azóta is ünnepeljük.
riddle_english: We conceded more than two, but gave back double—many ‘dumplings’—and we still celebrate it.

riddle_original: A magyar futball Trianonja és Mohácsa, fél tucattal a zsákban.
riddle_english: The Trianon and Mohács of Hungarian football, with half a dozen in the bag.

riddle_original: Ha a kolbászosok és a fényképesek egymásnak esnek, nem a rúgásoké a főszerep.
riddle_english: When the sausage‑makers and the photographers go at it, kicking is not the main act.

riddle_original: Nyíl és Törő egymás ellen, de melyik klubokról van szó?
riddle_english: Nyíl and Törő against each other—which clubs are we talking about?

riddle_original: Döme a világ egyik akkori legjobbja, Germániában, Itáliában és Hellászban is sztár volt.
riddle_english: Döme was among the world’s best then, a star in Germany, Italy, and Greece.

riddle_original: Háromszor egymás után a dobogó tetején az ötkarikás játékokon, ez csak egy csapatunkak sikerült.
riddle_english: Three times in a row on the Olympic top step—only one of our teams achieved this.

riddle_original: A földgolyó másik oldalán egy úszómedencében keményen álltak ki megtámadott hazájukért a magyar legények.
riddle_english: On the other side of the globe, in a swimming pool, Hungarian lads stood firm for their attacked homeland.
reference_answer_english: 1956 Olympic Water Polo (Blood in the Water)

riddle_original: Salzburgból Lipcsébe, onnan meg a ködös Albionba terelgettem a labdát.
riddle_english: From Salzburg to Leipzig, then on to foggy Albion, I shepherded the ball.

riddle_original: Eme vöröskeresztes gömb nedve nem édes a hasadnak.
riddle_english: This red‑crossed sphere’s juice is not sweet for your stomach.

riddle_original: Meséld el a viccet, amiben keresztnevek és városnevek keverednek, mert egy kisfiú nem tudja, hogy hívják és miért küldték a boltba.
riddle_english: Tell the joke where first names and city names get mixed up because a little boy doesn’t know his name or why he was sent to the shop.

riddle_original: Ezt a tésztát a kémény belsejében készítik és nem hangszerre hasonlít.
riddle_english: This pastry is prepared on the inside of a chimney and doesn’t resemble a musical instrument.

riddle_original: Édes, úri szobákban lenne a helye szép csillogó ruhájában, de inkább fákon lóg.
riddle_english: Sweet, it would belong in elegant parlors in its shiny dress, yet instead it hangs on trees.

riddle_original: Nagy termetű, növényevő hím testnedvét látják eme hevesi nedűben.
riddle_english: In this Heves‑county drink people ‘see’ the bodily fluid of a large herbivore male.

riddle_original: Még az uszodáját is jellegzetes fűszernövényéről formázta ez a városka.
riddle_english: This small town even shaped its swimming pool after its signature herb.

riddle_original: Kócos kis jószág, azt sem tudni melyik az eleje, melyik a hátulja, mégis jól mutatja az irányt nála jóval nagyobbaknak.
riddle_english: A shaggy little creature—you can’t tell front from back—yet it shows the way to much larger ones.

riddle_original: Hajlított asztalon focilabdával lábtengózni.
riddle_english: Playing foot‑tennis with a football on a curved table.

riddle_original: Egyes magyar városokban - eltérő módokon - folyami állatokból folyékony ételeket készítenek.
riddle_english: In some Hungarian towns—by different methods—they make liquid dishes from river animals.

riddle_original: Rövid ideig élő állatok látványos násztánca, mégis növényeknek hívjuk őket.
riddle_english: The spectacular mating dance of short‑lived animals—yet we call them ‘plants’.

riddle_original: Ki az a gyorslábú kis vörös, akinek az útjából a vadászok jobban teszik, ha kitérnek.
riddle_english: Who is the swift little red one that hunters would be wise to avoid?

riddle_original: Egy rendőr, akinek egy kutya volt a szirénája.
riddle_english: A policeman whose siren was a dog.

riddle_original: Egy zöld szörny folyton arról énekel, hogy virág szeretne lenni.
riddle_english: A green monster keeps singing that he wants to be a flower.

riddle_original: Kedves, lelkesen szerel, de rendetlen cselekedete nem nyer, kellemetlen helyzetekbe kevered, cégére rendre leverettet.
riddle_english: Kind and eager to fix things, but his messy deeds fail; he gets into scrapes, his shop sign keeps getting knocked down.

riddle_original: Messzi földről származó őskori alakok, akik remek rímekben szólalnak meg magyarul.
riddle_english: Prehistoric figures from far away who speak in excellent Hungarian rhymes.

riddle_original: Ha akarom, kifordított bundakesztyű, szobafestő pemzli vagy papucs orrán pamutbojt.
riddle_english: If I wish, I’m a turned‑inside‑out fur glove, a painter’s brush, or a cotton bobble on a slipper’s toe.

riddle_original: Papa, mama, gyerekek, csupa szív, szeretet, egy se nyafog, kesereg, de kik ők?
riddle_english: Papa, mama, children—full of heart and love—none whine or mope; who are they?

riddle_original: Egy zöld kisállat, akinek mértani alakzatokból áll a füle, azzal repül.
riddle_english: A small green animal whose ears are made of geometric shapes—and it flies with them.

riddle_original: Szeretem egy bizonyos édesség minden fajtáját, emiatt már repülni sem tudok.
riddle_english: I love every kind of a certain sweet—because of that I can no longer fly.

riddle_original: Egy vicces, háromszemű robot vagyok, és kisgyerekek társaságában keveredek galaktikus kalandokba.
riddle_english: I’m a funny three‑eyed robot who gets into galactic adventures with little kids.

riddle_original: Mennyire volt jókedvű a piros nyakkendős srác a nyolcvanas években?
riddle_english: How cheerful was the red‑necktied boy in the 1980s?
reference_answer_english: Like a Squirrel (up on the tree)

riddle_original: Egy kártyajáték, amelynek másik neve egy kétjegyű szám, amelyben mindkét jegy ugyanaz.
riddle_english: A card game whose other name is a two‑digit number with identical digits.

riddle_original: Egy hosszú lépéssel vagy egy távoli ugrással kerülünk közelebb a mámoros célhoz?
riddle_english: Do we get closer to the tipsy goal with a long step or a distant jump?

riddle_original: Mi volt a nyolcvanas években a magyar fizetőeszköz legkisebb címletének hátulján?
riddle_english: What was on the back of the smallest denomination of Hungarian currency in the 1980s?

riddle_original: Egy állat, akiről bulvármagazint neveztek el a rendszerváltás után.
riddle_english: An animal after which a tabloid magazine was named after the regime change.

riddle_original: Harminc éve csak egy ötvenest értem, de ma már egy ötszázast.
riddle_english: Thirty years ago I was worth only fifty; today I’m worth five hundred.

riddle_original: Kicsoda Stüszi vadász és Tök filkó, mi a közös bennük?
riddle_english: Who are Stüszi the Hunter and Tök Filkó—what do they have in common?

riddle_original: Találmányommal játszanak kicsik és nagyok, pedig geometriai formákat kell csak forgatni.
riddle_english: Children and adults play with my invention—one only needs to rotate geometric shapes.

riddle_original: Ezzel az itallal nem ütjük össze poharainkat, bár egyesek szerint már lejárt a tilalmi időszak.
riddle_english: We don’t clink glasses with this drink, though some say the prohibition period has passed.

riddle_original: Imádtuk ezt a játékot, dobtunk a kockával és lett minden a lakásba, amire vágytunk.
riddle_english: We loved this game—rolled the dice and got everything for the flat we desired.

riddle_original: Egy bátor nő folyton megveri a rosszakat és közben sikítozik, meg kismotorral száguldozik.
riddle_english: A brave woman keeps beating up baddies, screaming, and zooming on a small motorbike.

riddle_original: Ugyanott lakik egy kopasz mentős, egy ladás taxis, egy nyomdász fiú és még sokan mások.
riddle_english: In the same place live a bald paramedic, a Lada‑driving taxi driver, a printer’s apprentice, and many more.

riddle_original: Mikiék elvileg nem ellenségek, sőt rokonok is, mégis keresztbe tettek egymásnak több mint 20 éven át. Egy ország nézte, senki sem ismerte be, hogy nézi.
riddle_english: Miki’s side and the other aren’t enemies—indeed they’re kin—yet they sabotaged each other for over 20 years. A nation watched but no one admitted it.

riddle_original: Ruhaakasztókkal kereskedő a lósport szerelmese, unokaöccsét felügyeli, mennek mindenfelé.
riddle_english: A clothes‑hanger dealer, lover of horse racing, watches over his nephew; they go all over the place.

riddle_original: Hősünk csak arra szeretne vigyázni, hogy a folyó ne öntsön ki, de mindenféle politikai játszmákba rángatják, még börtönbe is kerül.
riddle_english: Our hero just wants to stop the river from flooding, but he is dragged into political games and even lands in jail.

riddle_original: Anyósával élő vasúti felügyelő alkalmaz egy tehenész fiút, és ételdobálásba fullad a sok kalamajka.
riddle_english: A railway supervisor living with his mother‑in‑law hires a cowherd boy, and all the fuss ends in food‑throwing.

riddle_original: Igazából gyerekeknek készült, de felnőttek is imádják a cincogók és nyávogók közötti csatározásokat, meg a vérszívók zenekarát.
riddle_english: Meant for kids, but adults love the squeakers’ and meowers’ skirmishes—and the vampires’ band.

riddle_original: Az egyik dombság vezetője lóra pattan, hogy sorozatosan borsot törjön az elnyomó sógorok orra alá.
riddle_english: The leader of one hill region mounts a horse to repeatedly spite the oppressive in‑laws.

riddle_original: Nagykamaszok kalandjai, egy ikonikus fővárosi helyszínről (amit egy másik fővárosról neveztek el) indul mindig a tuti buli.
riddle_english: Big teens’ adventures; the sure party always starts from an iconic capital site named after another capital.

riddle_original: Egy államférfi megbotlik, mert nem veti meg a másik nemet és ez rengeteg bajba sodorja őt is, környezetét is, egy pesti belvárosi szálloda kulisszái között.
riddle_english: A statesman trips up because he can’t resist the other sex, causing trouble for himself and others amid a downtown Pest hotel’s corridors.
reference_answer_english: Out of Order (The Minister is Stepping Aside)

riddle_original: Az anyák megmentője, egy jó szokás bevezetésével neve világszerte fogalommá vált.
riddle_english: The savior of mothers, their name became a worldwide concept by introducing a good habit.

riddle_original: Neve egy Kemény Nagymacskát is jelenthetne, de a Marslakók egyikeként is ismerhetjük ezt a lángelmét.
riddle_english: Their name could also mean a Tough Big Cat in Hungarian, but we can also know this brilliant mind as one of the Martians.

riddle_original: Az emberiség legszörnyűbb rémtetteiről szóló, saját keserű és tragikus élményeit is feldolgozó írásáért megkapta a legnagyobb elismerést.
riddle_english: They received the greatest recognition for their writing about the most terrible atrocities of humanity, which also processed their own bitter and tragic experiences.

riddle_original: Egy New York-i kerületről elnevezett projekt repítette világhírig, bár nem emiatt vagyunk büszkék erre a zseniális fizikusra.
riddle_english: A project named after a New York district made them world famous, although that is not why we are proud of this brilliant physicist.

riddle_original: Az utolsó világjárvány megfékezésében kulcsszerepe volt ennek a Tisza partjáról származó hölgynek.
riddle_english: This lady from the banks of the Tisza River played a key role in curbing the last pandemic.

riddle_original: Nélküle nem léteznének számítógépek, ugyanis működési elvüket ő dolgozta ki (és később róla nevezték el ezt az elvet).
riddle_english: Without them, computers would not exist, as they developed their operating principle (and the principle was later named after them).

riddle_original: A szegedi fűszerpaprikában talált valamit, ami miatt az orvostudomány egyik kiemelkedő alakja lett.
riddle_english: They found something in the Szeged spice paprika that made them one of the outstanding figures in medical science.

riddle_original: Sakkozó "gépe" messze megelőzte korát, a XVIII. században ámulatba ejtette a világot.
riddle_english: His chess "machine" was far ahead of its time, astonishing the world in the 18th century.

riddle_original: Minden mindennel összefügg, csak meg kell látni a mintázatot, vallja eme Erdélyből indult Amerikában élő világhírű fizikusunk.
riddle_english: Everything is connected to everything, you just have to see the pattern, says this world-famous physicist from Transylvania who lives in America.

riddle_original: Ő is abban az évben kapta meg a legmagasabb tudományos kitüntetést, amikor az első hölgy honfitársa érdemelt ki ilyet, igaz, más területen.
riddle_english: He also received the highest scientific award in the same year that the first lady's compatriot earned it, albeit in a different field.

riddle_original:
Aku dilahirkan bersama terbitnya fajar, namun separuh masa mudaku dihabiskan dalam bayang-bayang pengasingan. Aku berhasil merantai ribuan pulau yang terpecah hanya dengan satu lidah
 namun pada akhirnya aku harus terasing di tanah yang kubangun dengan tanganku sendiri. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
I was born at the break of dawn, yet I spent half my youth in the shadow of exile. I managed to unite thousands of scattered islands with just my words,
but in the end, I found myself exiled from the land I built with my own hands. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku menaklukkan Indonesia selama tiga puluh dua tahun. Aku memenangkan setiap pemilihan, mendikte parlemen, dan menguasai seluruh aparatur negara. 
Namun ironisnya, selama masa kejayaan absolut itu, aku sama sekali tidak pernah berstatus sebagai partai politik. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I ruled Indonesia for thirty-two years. I won every election, dictated the will of parliament, and controlled the entire state apparatus. 
Yet ironically, during that era of absolute dominance, I never held the status of a political party. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Kalkulasiku di udara diakui oleh dunia tanpa bantahan. Namun, saat aku turun tangan mencoba memperbaiki mesin birokrasi negeriku sendiri yang rusak parah, 
mereka hanya memberiku waktu kurang dari dua tahun sebelum memintaku pergi. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
My calculations in space were universally acknowledged. Yet, when I stepped in to try to fix my own country’s severely broken bureaucratic machinery, 
they gave me less than two years before asking me to leave. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku menggunakan bahasa dan pemikiran musuh untuk menaklukkan mereka, menyelamatkan republik dari kehancuran absolut. Namun sebagai imbalannya atas rasionalitas itu, 
aku diculik oleh bangsaku sendiri dan mati sebagai tahanan dari sahabat yang kubela. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
I used the enemy’s language and logic to defeat them, saving the republic from utter ruin. But in exchange for that rationality, I was kidnapped by my own people and died as a prisoner 
of the very friends I had defended. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku didirikan oleh darah campuran yang menghancurkan batasan ras, mengklaim bahwa tanah ini adalah milik siapa saja yang mengabdi padanya. Aku adalah partai pertama, namun aku dibinasakan oleh 
ketakutan musuh bahkan sebelum perlombaan kekuasaan benar-benar dimulai. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I was founded on a mix of blood that shattered racial boundaries, claiming that this land belongs to anyone who serves it. I was the first party, 
yet I was destroyed by my enemies’ fear even before the race for power had truly begun. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Secara fisik aku telah dimusnahkan dan dikubur lebih dari setengah abad yang lalu. Namun ironisnya, eksistensiku terus dihidupkan sebagai hantu abadi, 
digunakan sebagai senjata psikologis untuk menyerang lawan politik hingga hari ini. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
Physically, I was destroyed and buried more than half a century ago. Yet, ironically, my existence continues to be kept alive as an eternal specter, used as a psychological 
weapon to attack political opponents to this day. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Senjata musuh tak pernah berhasil memaksaku bertekuk lutut. Aku justru ditumbangkan oleh rasa kasihan dari pengawalku sendiri. Sang panglima perang yang ditakuti itu, pada akhirnya menutup mata 
hanya sebagai seorang guru mengaji di tanah yang asing. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
The enemy’s weapons never succeeded in forcing me to my knees. Instead, I was brought down by the pity of my own guards. That feared warlord ultimately closed his 
eyes as nothing more than a Quran teacher in a foreign land. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Tanda tanganku adalah satu dari dua kunci yang melahirkan negara ini. Namun, aku menghukum diriku sendiri dengan menjauh dari panggung kekuasaan, menolak berlumur lumpur politik kotor, 
dan memilih mati dalam kesederhanaan tanpa mewariskan apa pun selain ribuan buku. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
My signature was one of the two keys that gave birth to this nation. Yet I have punished myself by stepping away from the seat of power, refusing to get my hands dirty in the mire of politics, 
and choosing to die in simplicity, leaving behind nothing but thousands of books. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah arsitek pertama yang tak pernah menempati istana yang kubangun. Aku merumuskan nama negara ini dari pengasingan, namun sejarah menghukumku dengan kejam: dianggap terlalu radikal 
oleh kaum moderat, dan dicap pengkhianat oleh kaum radikal. Siapa aku?
riddle_english:
I am the first architect who never lived in the palace I built. I coined the name of this country from exile, yet history has punished me cruelly: considered too radical 
by the moderates, and branded a traitor by the radicals. Who am I?

riddle_original: Selembar kertas sakti yang terbit di bulan Maret. Diberikan untuk meredam kekacauan, namun justru menjadi kunci yang mengakhiri takhta sang proklamator. Peristiwa apa aku?
riddle_english: A fateful piece of paper published in March. Intended to quell the chaos, it instead became the key that brought an end to the Proclamation Leader’s reign. What event am I?

riddle_original: Aku adalah pergolakan bersenjata dari timur Nusantara. Aku meletus bukan untuk menghancurkan negara, melainkan menuntut keadilan ekonomi dari pusat yang menguasai segalanya. Peristiwa apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am an armed uprising from the eastern part of the Indonesian archipelago. I erupted not to destroy the nation, but to demand economic justice 
from the central government that controls everything. What event am I?

riddle_original:
Kau menghabiskan kekuatan militer dan dana tak terbatas untuk memaksaku tunduk menjadi milikmu. Namun kekalahan absolutmu atasku bukan terjadi karena peluru di medan perang, melainkan oleh selembar 
kertas suara yang kau fasilitasi dengan tanganmu sendiri. Peristiwa apakah aku?
riddle_english:
You spent unlimited military might and funds to force me to submit and become your possession. Yet your utter defeat at my hands did not come from bullets on the battlefield, 
but from a single ballot that you facilitated with your own hands. What event am I?

riddle_original:
Kelahiranku tidak dirancang dalam ruang sidang yang mewah, melainkan direbut secara paksa di dalam ruang hampa kekuasaan akibat jatuhnya dua bom atom. 
Teks yang melahirkanku dibacakan dengan sangat sederhana, namun resonansinya mengubah status jutaan manusia seketika. Peristiwa Apa ini?
riddle_english:
My birth was not planned in a lavish courtroom, but was forcibly brought about in the power vacuum created by the dropping of two atomic bombs. 
The text that gave birth to me was read out in the simplest of terms, yet its resonance instantly changed the lives of millions of people. What was this event?

riddle_original:
Sang panglima bahkan tak mampu melangkahkan kakinya sendiri, namun pergerakan pasukannya tak bisa dihentikan oleh persenjataan paling modern sekalipun. 
Kami memenangkan perang ini justru dengan cara secara konsisten menolak untuk mempertahankan satu jengkal tanah pun. Taktik apakah aku?
riddle_english:
The commander could not even walk on his own, yet not even the most modern weaponry could stop his troops’ advance. We won this war precisely by consistently refusing 
to defend a single inch of ground. What was my tactic?

riddle_original: Dua arsitek bangsa diculik oleh darah muda pada waktu fajar. Mereka tidak ditawan untuk disiksa, melainkan dipaksa untuk mengabaikan janji penguasa asing dan segera mempercepat lahirnya sebuah negara. Peristiwa apakah aku?
riddle_english:
Two of the nation’s architects were swept up by the fervor of youth at dawn. They were not taken captive to be tortured, but rather compelled to set aside the promises of foreign rulers and hasten 
the birth of a nation. What event am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah sebuah operasi pembersihan kilat yang hancur berantakan sebelum fajar menyingsing. Kegagalanku mengamankan ibu kota justru memicu pemusnahan massal jutaan nyawa 
dan meruntuhkan pilar kekuasaan Orde Lama untuk selamanya. Peristiwa apa ini?
riddle_english:
I was a lightning-fast cleanup operation that fell apart before dawn broke. My failure to secure the capital actually triggered the mass slaughter of millions of lives and 
brought down the pillars of the Old Order’s power forever. What event was this?

riddle_original:
Sebuah rezim raksasa yang membeku selama tiga puluh dua tahun akhirnya mencair dan runtuh dalam hitungan hari. Kekuatan ini tidak digulingkan oleh invasi asing atau kudeta jenderal, melainkan oleh kebangkrutan mata uang 
dan lautan pemuda yang turun ke jalan. Peristiwa apa ini?
riddle_english:
A colossal regime that had remained frozen for thirty-two years finally thawed and collapsed in a matter of days. This power was not overthrown by a foreign invasion or a military coup, 
but by currency collapse and a sea of young people taking to the streets. What event was this?

riddle_original:
Sejarah memujaku sebagai penguasa mutlak seluruh Nusantara. Namun sejatinya, hegemoni raksasa ini tidak dibangun dengan menduduki setiap jengkal tanah jajahan secara fisik, 
melainkan melalui teror armada laut dan diplomasi upeti yang memaksa raja-raja lokal tunduk tanpa perlu kuperangi. Entitas apakah aku?
riddle_english:
History portrays me as the absolute ruler of the entire archipelago. But in truth, this colossal hegemony was not built by physically occupying every inch of the colonies, 
but rather through the terror of a naval fleet and a tribute-based diplomacy that forced local kings to submit without my having to fight them. What kind of entity am I?

riddle_original: Aku memobilisasi kapal selam dan armada udara paling mematikan dari blok timur ke perairan Nusantara. Namun ironisnya, daratan raksasa itu kurebut lewat sebuah tanda tangan di benua barat. Operasi apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I mobilized the deadliest submarines and air force from the Eastern Bloc to the waters of the Indonesian archipelago. Ironically, however, I seized that vast landmass with a single signature on 
the Western continent. What operation was I conducting?

riddle_original:
Kelahiranku dipicu oleh arogansi tuan rumah yang menolak visa dua negara pada ajang sebelumnya. Aku lahir untuk menampar wajah Olimpiade, membuktikan bahwa kami tak butuh pengakuan dari hegemoni
 Barat untuk membangun panggung kelas dunia. Apa ini?
riddle_english:
My birth was sparked by the host country’s arrogance in denying visas to two nations at the previous Games. I was born to slap the Olympics in the face, proving that we don’t need recognition from 
Western hegemony to build a world-class stage. What is this?

riddle_original: Aku adalah kerajaan tanpa istana dan tanpa raja. Dunia membayarku mahal bukan untuk melihat daratanku, melainkan untuk melihat apa yang berhasil kusembunyikan saat daratanku tenggelam. Wilayah manakah aku?
riddle_english: I am a kingdom without a palace or a king. The world pays me dearly—not to see my land, but to see what I managed to hide as my land sank. Which land am I?

riddle_original:
Aku menyembunyikan jantung republik di dalam istanaku selama empat tahun masa kritis. Setelah musuh pergi dan jantung itu dipindahkan kembali, akulah satu-satunya wilayah yang secara legal diizinkan untuk 
tidak pernah mempraktikkan demokrasi utuh di tanahku sendiri. Daerah manakah aku?
riddle_english:
I hid the heart of the republic within my palace for four critical years. After the enemy departed and the heart was moved back, I was the only region legally permitted to 
never practice full democracy on my own soil. Which region am I?

riddle_original: Berada di ujung Nusantara, aku dijuluki serambi dari tanah suci. Hukum yang berlaku di tanahku tak sama dengan wilayah republik lainnya. Wilayah apakah aku?
riddle_english: Located at the edge of the archipelago, I am known as the “veranda of the holy land.” The laws that apply in my land are different from those in other parts of the republic. What region am I?

riddle_original: Bentuk tubuhku meniru huruf kesebelas dalam abjad. Aku berdiri di tengah nusantara, menjadi rumah bagi pelaut tangguh dan fauna purba bertanduk yang tak ada di daratan lain. Pulau apakah aku?
riddle_english:
My shape resembles the eleventh letter of the alphabet. I stand in the heart of the archipelago, home to intrepid sailors and ancient horned creatures found nowhere else on land. 
Which island am I?

riddle_original: Nilai jualku sangat mahal, namun aku bukanlah atraksi utamanya. Aku hanyalah dermaga singgah dan ruang tunggu mewah yang mengkapitalisasi rasa penasaran dunia terhadap monster dari zaman prasejarah. Apa aku?
riddle_english: My market value is sky-high, but I’m not the main attraction. I’m just a stopover and a luxurious waiting area that capitalizes on the world’s curiosity about prehistoric monsters. What am I?

riddle_original: Aku dibangun di atas abu kota pelabuhan yang ditaklukkan. Selama tiga abad, aku menjadi markas utama serikat dagang paling serakah di dunia sebelum merdeka dan mengganti namaku. Kota apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I was built on the ashes of a conquered port city. For three centuries, I served as the headquarters of the world’s most greedy trading guild before gaining independence and changing my name. 
What city am I?

riddle_original:
Tubuhku menyerupai burung purba raksasa yang melayang. Aku adalah satu-satunya daratan yang berani melawan teriknya matahari khatulistiwa dengan memamerkan mahkota 
salju abadi di puncak kepalaku. Pulau apakah aku?
riddle_english:
My body resembles a giant prehistoric bird soaring through the sky. I am the only landmass that dares to defy the scorching equatorial sun by displaying a crown 
of eternal snow atop my head. What island am I?

riddle_original: Kami adalah dua nama yang abadi diikat dalam satu lagu wajib nasional. Yang satu menatap matahari terbenam di lautan barat, yang lain menjadi saksi pertama fajar di ujung timur. Siapakah kami berdua?
riddle_english: We are two timeless names bound together in a national anthem. One gazes at the sunset over the western sea, while the other is the first to witness the dawn in the far east. Who are we?

riddle_original: Daratanku tak punya ruang untuk membentang rata, memaksaku menumpuk kehidupan dari bukit hingga ke bibir pantai. Aku dijuluki kota berair, bertahta di lengan timur pulau berbentuk laba-laba. Kota apakah aku?
riddle_english:
My land has no room to spread out flat, forcing me to stack life from the hills all the way to the shoreline. I am known as the city of water, enthroned on the eastern arm of the spider-shaped island. 
What city am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah kota sejuk yang dijaga oleh Gunung Marapi dan Singgalang. Di jantung kotaku, berdiri sebuah menara jam raksasa hadiah dari masa kolonial, dan dari tanahku lahirlah sang wakil proklamator yang berotak kalkulator. 
Kota apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am a cool city guarded by Mount Marapi and Mount Singgalang. At the heart of my city stands a giant clock tower, a gift from the colonial era, and from my soil was born the vice-proclaimer 
with a mind like a calculator. What city am I?

riddle_original:
Untuk melahirkan wujudku, kau tak butuh kuas, melainkan air mata gelap yang membakar permukaanku. Aku adalah peta yang diselamkan ke dalam lautan noda berulang kali, 
menyisakan garis-garis suci yang menolak untuk tenggelam. Karya apakah aku?
riddle_english:
To bring me into being, you need no brush, but rather dark tears that burn my surface. I am a map repeatedly submerged in a sea of stains, leaving behind sacred lines that refuse to sink. 
What kind of work am I?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya semesta di mana wujud asliku disembunyikan di balik layar, sementara manusia bersorak dan menangis murni karena melihat proyeksi bayanganku. Apakah aku?
riddle_english: The only universe where my true form is hidden behind the screen, while people cheer and weep simply at the sight of my shadow’s projection. Am I?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya pertunjukan di mana telapak tangan dilarang menganggur dan kaki dilarang melangkah. Kami merakit badai suara hanya bermodalkan lipatan tubuh dan benturan kulit berkecepatan tinggi. Siapakah kami?
riddle_english:
The only performance where hands are forbidden to rest and feet are forbidden to move. We create a storm of sound using nothing but the contours 
of our bodies and the high-speed impact of our skin. Who are we?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya pertunjukan di mana keindahan diukur dari seberapa kaku tubuhmu menahan diri, sementara kakimu dipaksa bekerja layaknya mesin tik yang mencetak ritme di atas kayu. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english: The only performance where beauty is measured by how rigidly your body holds itself, while your feet are forced to work like a typewriter, pounding out a rhythm on the wood. Who am I?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya brankas purba di mana ketiadaan pigmen yang membentuk sebuah telapak tangan justru menjadi data paling berharga, mengubah garis waktu peradaban manusia tanpa perlu mengucapkan sepatah kata. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
The only ancient safe where the absence of pigment forming a handprint is actually the most valuable evidence, reshaping the timeline of 
human civilization without uttering a single word. Who am I?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya monster cacat yang dipuja, di mana kau dituntut untuk secara sukarela masuk ke dalam mulutnya demi membuktikan bahwa jiwamu bersih dari kotoran dunia. Apakah aku?
riddle_english: The only deformed monster that is worshipped, where you are required to voluntarily enter its mouth to prove that your soul is free from the filth of the world. Is that me?

riddle_original:
Satu-satunya cermin beku di mana kekalahan diubah menjadi arogansi lewat manipulasi sudut pandang. Di duniaku, sang pahlawan yang marah sedang menatap detik-detik awal sebelum 
kebebasannya dirampas, sebuah rute yang kelak akan memaksanya membusuk dan mati di tanah yang sama tempat kakimu berpijak hari ini. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
The only frozen mirror where defeat is transformed into arrogance through the manipulation of perspective. In my world, the angry hero is staring at the opening moments before his freedom 
is taken away—a path that will eventually force him to rot and die on the very ground where your feet stand today. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: Painting of the arrest of Prince Diponegoro

riddle_original: Satu-satunya seni komunal di mana diammu dihitung sama pentingnya dengan gerakmu. Aku meminjam getaran dari tanganmu untuk mengubah benturan kayu-kayu kosong menjadi satu kesadaran yang utuh. Apakah aku?
riddle_english:
The only communal art form in which your silence counts just as much as your movements. I borrow the vibrations from your hands to transform the clatter of empty wood into a single, 
unified consciousness. Is that me?

riddle_original:
Satu-satunya pertunjukan di mana paru-paru ratusan manusia diubah menjadi mesin perkusi massal. Kami membentuk pusaran suara yang mengawal sebuah tragedi penculikan, 
tanpa pernah menyentuh satu pun alat musik. Tarian apakah kami?
riddle_english:
The only performance in which the lungs of hundreds of people are transformed into a massive percussion machine. We form a vortex of sound that accompanies a kidnapping tragedy, 
without ever touching a single musical instrument. What kind of dance are we?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya kesatuan di mana puluhan raga logam harus disiksa dengan pukulan palu bertubi-tubi, murni untuk menginjeksi ilusi tentang kedamaian massal. Instrumen apakah aku?
riddle_english: The only place where dozens of metal bodies must be battered by relentless hammer blows, purely to instill an illusion of mass peace. What kind of instrument am I?

riddle_original: Aku adalah medan tempur di mana tangan menjadi lumpuh dan kaki menjadi otak. Peluruku terbuat dari kayu yang berlubang, terbang lewat koordinasi yang mustahil. Jika aku jatuh, poinmu gugur. Olahraga apakah aku?
riddle_english: I am a battlefield where hands become paralyzed and feet become the brain. My bullets are made of hollow wood, flying through impossible coordination. If I fall, you lose a point. What sport am I?

riddle_original: Aku adalah seni yang bisa membunuh, namun sering kali terlihat seperti sedang memuja. Aku mengalir hampir di seluruh nadi Nusantara, bersembunyi di balik indahnya bunga-bunga gerakan. Apakah aku?
riddle_english: I am an art that can kill, yet I often appear to be worshiping. I flow through nearly every vein of the archipelago, hiding behind the beauty of the flowers of movement. Who am I?

riddle_original: Sang Pangeran menciptakanku untuk mengolah bumi, tapi manusia justru menjadikanku ajang pembuktian gengsi. Di atasku ada pecut, di bawahku ada debu Madura yang berterbangan. Apakah aku?
riddle_english: The Prince created me to cultivate the earth, but humans have turned me into a battleground for prestige. Above me is a whip; below me, Maduran dust swirls in the air. What am I?

riddle_original:
Tuanku adalah kemaharajaan yang kini tinggal abu, musuhku adalah hantu-hantu ombak yang serakah. Aku dilahirkan bukan oleh satu guru, melainkan dari sayembara hidup dan mati demi melindungi urat nadi 
perdagangan. Apakah aku?
riddle_english:
My lord is an empire now reduced to ashes; my enemies are the greedy ghosts of the waves. I was born not of a single teacher, but from a life-and-death struggle to protect the lifeblood 
of trade. Who am I?

riddle_original: Aku adalah satu-satunya taktik menyerang tanpa perlu menghancurkan gerbang musuh. Dari insting bertahan hidup di medan tempur kuno, kini aku menyusut menjadi tontonan melawan monolit yang bisu. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am the only offensive tactic that doesn’t require destroying the enemy’s gate. From a survival instinct on ancient battlefields, 
I have now been reduced to a spectacle against a silent monolith. Who am I?

riddle_original: Kaki-kakimu berhenti menjadi milikmu sejak kau menginjak punggungku. Ini adalah satu-satunya perlombaan di mana berlari kencang tidak ada gunanya tanpa kerjasama tim. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english: Your legs stopped belonging to you the moment you stepped on my back. This is the only race where running fast is useless without teamwork. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah naga kayu yang membelah arus, di mana puluhan orang merelakan tulang punggung mereka menjadi mesin. Aku tidak peduli apakah aku merayakan doa suci atau mahkota asing, tugasku hanya satu: 
tiba di ujung sungai lebih dulu. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am a wooden dragon that splits the current, where dozens of people have sacrificed their spines to become engines. I don’t care whether I’m celebrating a sacred prayer or a foreign crown, 
I have only one mission: to reach the river’s end first. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah seni membunuh yang menyamar sebagai meditasi. Senjataku membelah udara untuk mencabut nyawa, tapi kakiku menolak meninggalkan bumi dan memilih melipat diri. 
Para bangsawan kuno menggunakanku untuk memanah tanpa perlu melihat, membiarkan keheningan yang membidik sasaran. Olahraga apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am the art of killing disguised as meditation. My weapon slices through the air to take a life, but my feet refuse to leave the ground and choose to fold in on themselves. 
The nobles of old used me to shoot without looking, letting the silence take aim. What sport am I?

riddle_original:
Kau memelukku bukan dengan tangan, tapi dengan jari kaki. Aku adalah satu-satunya kendaraan vertikal yang tak punya roda, memaksa manusia meminjam sepasang kaki palsu hanya 
untuk merasa lebih dekat dengan langit. Olahraga apakah aku?
riddle_english:
You embrace me not with your hands, but with your toes. I am the only vertical vehicle without wheels, forcing people to borrow a pair of prosthetic legs just to feel closer to the sky. 
What sport am I?

riddle_original: Lahir dari jalanan, bukan dari padepokan. Aku adalah satu-satunya seni yang menganggap rasa sakit sebagai bahan bakar dan menganggap gerakan indah sebagai sebuah kecacatan taktis. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english: Born on the streets, not in padepokan. I am the only art form that sees pain as fuel and beautiful movement as a tactical flaw. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Senjataku membelah udara seperti petir yang mencari punggung. Kami merayakan luka secara sadar, karena setiap tetes merah yang menyentuh debu bukanlah lambang kekalahan, 
melainkan doa agar bumi sudi memberikan panennya. Aku adalah pertumpahan darah yang dibalut oleh senyuman dan nyanyian. Apakah aku?
riddle_english:
My weapon slices through the air like lightning striking the earth. We celebrate our wounds with full awareness, for every drop of red that touches the dust is not a symbol of defeat, 
but a prayer that the earth will deign to yield its harvest. I am bloodshed cloaked in smiles and songs. What am I?

riddle_original: Satu-satunya peta menuju ketiadaan yang dirancang dari jutaan ton batu. Di atasku, kau berjalan memutar melewati kurungan-kurungan berbentuk lonceng, mencari cahaya yang tak bisa disentuh. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english: The only map to nothingness, carved from millions of tons of stone. Above me, you walk in circles past bell-shaped enclosures, searching for a light you cannot touch. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah satu-satunya kurungan segi delapan bermuka merah di tanah ini. Wujudku adalah monumen ketakutan pendatang, dirancang menatap delapan mata angin karena musuh mereka bisa 
menyerang dari bayangan mana saja. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am the only red-faced octagonal fortress in this land. I stand as a monument to the settlers’ fear, designed to face 
all eight cardinal directions because their enemies could attack from any shadow. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Ratusan celahku diciptakan untuk melawan panas matahari, namun manusia zaman sekarang justru mendatangi dan mengingatku murni karena hawa dingin dari lantai basemenku. 
Aku adalah markas kereta yang tak bernapas dengan asap. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
My hundreds of cracks were created to ward off the sun’s heat, yet people today come to me and remember me solely for the cool air rising from my basement floor.
I am a train depot that breathes no smoke. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Mahkotaku adalah identitas barat khatulistiwa, namun akarku dipaksa mencengkeram tanah timur jauh. Aku adalah monumen kepanikan Belanda sebuah sangkar batu tempat seorang ulama besar 
dibiarkan mati menjadi debu dalam keheningan total. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
My crown is the identity of the West of the Equator, yet my roots are forced to cling to the soil of the Far East. I am a monument to Dutch panic—a stone cage where a great scholar 
was left to die and turn to dust in utter silence. Who am I?
reference_answer_english: The tomb of my lord Imam Bonjol

riddle_original:
Aku adalah ruang transisi tempat pencipta detak jantung negaramu mati membusuk oleh sakit dan pengejaran. Ia menulis mantra yang membuatmu hormat pada kain dua warna, 
namun tak sekalipun dindingku melihatnya menikmati kemerdekaan itu sendiri. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am the transitional space where the creator of your nation’s heartbeat lies decaying from pain and persecution. He wrote a spell that made you revere the two-colored cloth, 
yet not once did my walls see him enjoy that freedom himself. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Saat aku bernapas, aku adalah denyut nadi seluruh kepulauan yang diikat oleh satu sumpah puasa yang kejam. Saat aku mati, aku menyusut menjadi fondasi-fondasi buntu yang harus susah 
payah digali dari bawah persawahan agar peradaban ini tidak amnesia. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
When I breathe, I am the pulse of the entire archipelago, bound by a cruel vow of fasting. When I die, I shrink into the forgotten foundations that must be painstakingly 
dug up from beneath the rice fields so that this civilization does not lose its memory. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah dokumen paling mahal dalam sejarah bangsamu, yang draf aslinya harus diselamatkan dari tumpukan sampah dapur. Hanya butuh kurang dari lima puluh kata dariku untuk mengusir mesin 
perang asing dari tanah ini. Apakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am the most valuable document in your nation’s history, the original draft of which had to be rescued from a pile of kitchen trash. It took fewer than fifty words 
from me to drive foreign war machines from this land. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah himpunan ratusan reruntuhan yang dituduh lahir dalam satu malam demi seorang wanita yang menolak dinikahi. Angka pada identitasku adalah kebohongan, menyembunyikan fakta bahwa 
kuota pembangunanku tak pernah benar-benar terpenuhi sesuai legenda. Siapakah aku?
riddle_english:
I am a collection of hundreds of ruins, said to have been built in a single night for a woman who refused to be married. The numbers on my ID are a lie, hiding the fact that 
the construction quota was never actually met, as the legend goes. Who am I?

riddle_original:
Di bilik utamaku bersemayam sang dewi kematian bertangan banyak yang menunggangi singa, namun lidah bangsamu bersikeras memanggilnya dengan nama seorang putri jelita penolak lamaran. 
Aku adalah mahkota runcing yang membatalkan pesta pernikahan. Bangunan apakah aku?
riddle_english:
In my main chamber dwells the many-armed goddess of death riding a lion, yet the tongues of your people insist on calling her by the name of a beautiful princess who rejected a suitor. 
I am the pointed crown that called off the wedding. What structure am I?

riddle_original: Semakin keras dua pihak berusaha saling menjauh, semakin kuat mereka terikat. Pertarungan ini tidak selesai dengan menghancurkan lawan, tapi dengan memaksanya melewati seutas batas ilusi yang mereka sepakati sendiri. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
The harder the two sides try to push each other away, the stronger their bond becomes. This battle isn’t won by destroying the opponent, but by forcing them to cross an
 illusory boundary they’ve agreed upon themselves. Who am I?

riddle_original: Benteng ini sama sekali tak punya dinding, hanya ilusi kapur di atas tanah. Sang palang pintu takkan pernah mengejarmu ke tengah, ia hanya diam menunggumu melakukan kebodohan dengan melintasi garis kekuasaannya. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
This fortress has no walls at all—just a chalk outline on the ground. The gatekeeper will never chase you into the center; he simply stands there, waiting for you to make 
the mistake of crossing the line of his authority. What am I?

riddle_original:
Aku menghitung waktu mundurnya kehancuranmu, sementara kau mencari keselamatan dalam pengasingan. Di sini, kesunyian adalah perisaimu, namun detak jantungmu sendiri adalah 
pengkhianat terbesar yang menuntunku menemukannya. Apa aku
riddle_english:
I’m counting down the days until your downfall, while you seek safety in exile. Here, silence is your shield, yet your own heartbeat is 
the greatest traitor, leading me to find you. Am I

riddle_original: Aku menuntut pandangan yang tajam dan satu mata yang terpejam. Senjataku harus membentur target agar aku bisa tetap bertahan di medan laga, karena jika aku meleset, aku justru menjadi mangsa berikutnya. Permainan apa aku?
riddle_english: I need sharp eyesight and one eye closed. My weapon must hit the target so I can stay alive on the battlefield, because if I miss, I’ll become the next victim. What game am I playing?

riddle_original:
Aku memintamu menyerahkan kepemilikan satu-satunya peluru kepada musuh setelah kau memukulnya. Semakin kuat kau menghantamnya, semakin banyak waktu yang kau miliki 
untuk melarikan diri dari sasaran tembak mereka. Apa aku
riddle_english:
I’m asking you to hand over your only bullet to the enemy after you hit them. The harder you hit them, the more time you’ll have 
to escape their line of fire. Am I

riddle_original: Aku memberimu pelindung yang justru melemahkanmu. Semakin keras kau mencoba melangkah seperti biasa di dalamku, semakin cepat kau akan tersungkur mencium tanah. Apa aku?
riddle_english: I’ve given you a shield that actually weakens you. The harder you try to walk as usual inside me, the faster you’ll fall flat on your face. What am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah musuh yang bergerak melingkar, menciptakan ritme yang harus kau ikuti dengan patuh. Caraku mengalahkanmu bukan dengan mengejarmu, melainkan dengan membiarkanmu
melompati tubuhku berkali-kali hingga kau sendiri yang lelah dan menyerahkan kakimu untuk kuikat. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I am an enemy that moves in circles, creating a rhythm you must follow obediently. I defeat you not by chasing you, but by letting you
jump over my body again and again until you grow tired and surrender your feet for me to bind. What am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah kompetisi di mana kau harus melangkah maju demi membuat lawanmu mundur. Namun ingat, jika kau terlalu bernafsu mendorong tanpa pijakan yang kokoh, bobot tubuhmu sendiri yang akan menjadi senjata lawan 
untuk merubuhkanmu. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I am a competition where you must step forward to force your opponent to retreat. But remember, if you push too hard without a solid footing, your own body weight will become your 
opponent’s weapon to bring you down. What am I?

riddle_original:
Aku adalah pertempuran di mana menyentuh markas lawan adalah kemenangan mutlak, namun pertahanan terbaik justru dilakukan dengan cara membiarkan musuhmu mendekat hingga mereka kehilangan hak atas kebebasannya 
sendiri. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I am a battle in which reaching the enemy’s base is an absolute victory, yet the best defense is achieved by letting your enemies get close enough that they lose their own freedom.
What am I?

riddle_original:
Aku memberimu kebebasan untuk melempar tinggi harapanmu, namun aku mengikatmu pada aturan ketat untuk menata kekacauan di bawahnya sebelum waktu yang kuberikan habis. 
Jika kau terlalu serakah meraup semuanya sekaligus, kau justru akan kehilangan kendali atas segalanya. Apa aku?
riddle_english:
I give you the freedom to set your hopes high, but I bind you to strict rules to bring order to the chaos beneath before the time I’ve given you runs out. 
If you’re too greedy and try to grab everything at once, you’ll actually lose control of it all. Who am I?

riddle_original: Jemarimu bisa memutar dan menarikku kapan saja, tapi seumur hidup matamu takkan pernah bisa membuktikan keberadaanku secara langsung. Aku adalah penerima pesan yang bersembunyi dari cahaya pandanganmu. Apakah aku?
riddle_english: Your fingers can twist and pull me at any time, but your eyes will never be able to directly confirm my existence. I am the message-bearer hiding from the light of your gaze. Who am I?

riddle_original: Aku ada di pinggir api, dan ada juga di tengah air, apakah aku?
riddle_english: I am at the edge of the fire, and I am also in the middle of the water—what am I?

riddle_original: Masuknya miring, keluarnya juga miring, apa itu?
riddle_english: It goes in at an angle, and it comes out at an angle too what is that?

riddle_original: Pintu apa yang kalau dibuka dapat membahayakan banyak orang?
riddle_english: What kind of door, if opened, could endanger many people?

riddle_original: Tra memorie e un po’ di follia, rese il cinema una pura magia.

riddle_english: We are two warriors who emerged from salt, having remained naked for millennia. We waited a long time at the bottom of the sea before finding land again on the tip of the boot.

riddle_english: In Rome, they call me by an affectionate augmentative name. I am the most famous dome in the world, and my artistic 'father' wanted me large enough to dominate every other roof in the eternal City.

riddle_english: I live in a hollow trunk inside a colorful courtyard. I am a white polka-dot rag bird who taught generations of children how to use scissors and glue during Rai afternoon shows.

riddle_english: In this group game, someone calls out a color and everyone must run to touch an object of that color to be safe before getting caught.

riddle_english: It doesn't go on your feet, but it's the most sincere way to compliment the chef.

riddle_english: He spoke with creatures without speech, and was listened to by them.

riddle_original: Il protettore più comune nelle case degli anziani, forse perché gli vengono attribuiti innumerevoli miracoli.
riddle_english: The most common protector in the homes of the elderly, perhaps because countless miracles are attributed to him.

riddle_english: A very high arch built in a single night thanks to a pact with the devil. The price was to be a human soul, but the unfortunate one to cross was a dog.

riddle_english: So are the hands... of those who always spend too much.
