riddle_original:
De todas as flores,
esta pôs fim a imensas dores.
Trouxe o valor de algo novo,
movendo consigo todo o povo.
riddle_english:
Of all flowers,
this one put an end to countless pain.
It brought with it the value of something new,
moving with it all the people.

riddle_original:
Uma união mal amanhada por definição,
mas uma solução de mestre por necessidade.
Montada com peças que muitos consideravam incompatíveis, 
apenas para provar que o que é frágil no papel pode ser sólido na prática.
Moveu um país enquanto todos esperavam que eu ficasse pelo caminho.
riddle_english:
A poorly constructed union by definition,
but a master solution out of necessity.
Assembled from pieces that many considered incompatible,
just to prove that what is fragile on paper can be solid in practice.
It moved a country while everyone expected me to fall by the wayside.

riddle_original:
Não sou médico, mas fui chamado quando a febre das contas subiu. 
Entrei com receita amarga e deixei a palavra austeridade à mesa.
riddle_english:
I'm not a doctor, but I was called in when the bills started piling up.
I came in with a bitter prescription and left the word austerity at the table.

riddle_original:
Tenho casa de pedra e debates de espuma. Uns entram pela esquerda, outros pela direita, 
hoje em dia é tudo uma salganhada.
riddle_english:
I have a house of stone and debates of foam. Some enter from the left, others from the right,
nowadays it's all a hodgepodge.

riddle_original: Presido às reuniões em São Bento, mas o meu verdadeiro poder mede-se na paciência de aturar cativações e debates quinzenais.
riddle_english: I chair the meetings in São Bento, but my true power is measured by the patience to endure fund withholdings and biweekly debates.

riddle_original: Moro num palácio cor-de-rosa perto dos pastéis, sou homem de poucas exuberâncias e tenho uns sapatos grandes para preencher.
riddle_english: I live in a pink palace near the pastries and am famous for taking dips in the sea and taking selfies with everyone.

riddle_original: Sou a praça onde os ministérios se alinham e os reformados e turistas se sentam a comentar as obras públicas debaixo das arcadas.
riddle_english: I am the Lisbon's square where ministries line up and retirees and tourists sit under the arcades commenting on public works.

riddle_original: Sou a reunião semanal, habitualmente à quinta-feira, onde os membros do executivo decidem o que vai ser impresso no Diário da República.
riddle_english: I am the weekly meeting, usually on Thursday, where members of the executive decide what will be printed in the Diário da República.

riddle_original:
Fui o homem da sombra que guardava os segredos do topo, mas acabei no banco dos réus. 
O meu apelido evoca o mar, mas foi na terra que criei a maior tempestade política do século, fazendo tremer ministros e palácios sem nunca ter sido eleito.
riddle_english:
I was the shadow man who kept the secrets of the top, but ended up in the dock. 
My last name evokes the sea, but it was on land that I created the biggest political storm of the century, making ministers and palaces tremble without ever being elected.

riddle_original:
Nasci para quebrar o ritmo dos grandes e trago o barulho no nome. 
Sentado bem à direita, transformei o debate num espetáculo de cartazes, protestos e murros na mesa, dividindo o país entre o aplauso e o escândalo.
riddle_english:
I was born to break the rhythm of the big guys and I bring noise in my name. Sitting far to the right, 
I transformed the debate into a show of posters, protests and fists on the table, dividing the country between applause and scandal.

riddle_original: Durante esta altura governá-mos um mundo partilhado com o vizinho que era apenas mapa e linha.
riddle_english: During this time we ruled a world shared with our neighbor that was merely a map and a line.

riddle_original:
Com uma pá e muita lenda, ajudei a virar uma batalha em história de forno. 
Quando se fala de mim, há pão e pancada.
riddle_english:
With a shovel and a lot of legend, I helped turn a battle into an oven story.
When people talk about me, there's bread and blows.

riddle_original:
Durou décadas de lápis azul, medo baixo e retrato na parede. 
Prometia ordem, mas ensinou muitos a falar por meias palavras.
riddle_english:
It lasted for decades, marked by blue pencils, low fears, and portraits on the wall.
It promised order, but taught many to speak in half-truths.

riddle_original: Reconstruí a capital com linhas retas e esquadro, expulsando jesuítas e criando a gaiola de madeira contra a fúria da terra.
riddle_english: I rebuilt the capital with straight lines and a set square, expelling Jesuits and creating the wooden cage against the earth's fury.

riddle_original:
Troquei o trono pela miragem de uma batalha num deserto distante, mas o meu verdadeiro legado foi psicológico. 
Transformei-me numa obsessão meteorológica para um país inteiro, que aprendeu a cruzar os braços e a olhar para o horizonte cinzento à espera que eu apareça para resolver o destino da pátria.
riddle_english:
I traded the throne for the mirage of a battle in a distant desert, but my true legacy was psychological. 
I turned into a meteorological obsession for an entire country, which learned to fold its arms and look at the gray horizon waiting for me to appear to solve the country's destiny.

riddle_original:
Uma linha invisível traçada à mesa com astúcia diplomática, que fatiou o desconhecido antes de ele ser mapa. Empurrámos a fronteira náutica uns graus para oeste num golpe de mestre, 
garantindo que um gigante do outro lado do Atlântico ficasse guardado para a nossa língua muito antes de sabermos o seu tamanho exato.
riddle_english:
An invisible line drawn at a table with diplomatic cunning, which sliced the unknown before it was even a map. 
We pushed the nautical border a few degrees west in a masterstroke, ensuring that a giant on the other side of the Atlantic was saved for our language long before we knew its exact size.

riddle_original:
O meu sangue manchou as pedras de um jardim por ordem política, mas a minha história recusou-se a morrer no caixão. Sentaram o meu corpo frio num trono para receber juras de lealdade 
e hoje repouso de pés voltados para o meu amor, para que ele seja a primeira coisa que vejo no fim dos tempos.
riddle_english:
My blood stained the stones of a garden by political order, but my story refused to die in the coffin. 
They sat my cold body on a throne to receive oaths of loyalty and today I rest with my feet facing my love, so that he is the first thing I see at the end of time.

riddle_original: Derrubei uma longa ditadura colocando flores nos canos das espingardas, ao som de uma canção proibida que tocou na rádio de madrugada.
riddle_english: I overthrew a long dictatorship by putting flowers in the barrels of rifles, to the sound of a forbidden song that played on the radio at dawn.

riddle_original: Fui a bófia sombria de fato e gabardina que vigiava as conversas de café e silenciava quem ousasse pensar diferente antes de 1974.
riddle_english: I was the shadowy police in suit and trench coat who monitored café conversations and silenced anyone who dared to think differently before 1974.

riddle_original:
Fui a ponte aérea do desespero e o adeus forçado a uma terra que muitos chamavam sua. 
Em 1975, enchi o Tejo de caixotes de madeira e o país de corações desalojados, que regressaram com as mãos vazias mas com a vida para reconstruir.
riddle_english:
I was the airlift of despair and the forced farewell to a land that many called their own. In 1975, 
I filled the Tagus with wooden crates and the country with displaced hearts, who returned empty-handed but with a life to rebuild.

riddle_original:
Esta cidade é famosa por não ser, 
apesar de toda a gente saber quem sou. 
Habita na memória e em fotografias,
 mas desvanece perante qualquer cartógrafo.
É a cidade que todos conhecem,
 mas que ninguém consegue provar que existe.
riddle_english:
This city is famous for not being,
although everyone knows who I am.
It lives in memory and in photographs,
but fades before any cartographer.
It's the city everyone knows,
but no one can prove exists.
riddle_note:
This one is a very popular Portuguese meme,
 however since it's mostly known on the internet it might not be known by the older generations.

riddle_original:
O paraíso de quem vem de longe e a saudade de quem ficou.
Feito para dar descanso, mas agora canso quem me tenta habitar.
 No Verão, o centro do mundo, 
mas no resto do ano, um segredo que os locais já não reconhecem como casa.
riddle_english:
The paradise for those who come from afar and the longing of those who stayed.
Made to give rest, but now I tire those who try to inhabit me.
In the summer, the center of the world,
but for the rest of the year, a secret that the locals no longer recognize as home.

riddle_original:
Sou planície que parece parada, mas canta devagar. 
Tenho sobreiros, calor sem pressa e horizontes que não cabem no retrovisor.
riddle_english:
I am a plain that seems still, but sings slowly.
I have cork oaks, unhurried warmth, and horizons that don't fit in the rearview mirror.

riddle_original:
Tenho canais, moliceiros e ovos que não vêm da capoeira. Chamam-me Veneza, 
mas falo com sotaque do centro.
riddle_english:
I have canals, moliceiros (traditional boats), and eggs that don't come from the henhouse. 
They call me Venice, but I speak with a downtown accent.

riddle_original: Sou o único maciço montanhoso onde a neve chega para atrair famílias inteiras e onde grandes cães felpudos têm a missão de guardar ovelhas.
riddle_english: I am the only mountain massif where the snow is enough to attract entire families and where large furry dogs have the mission of guarding sheep.

riddle_original: Somos nove ilhas onde as vacas pastam serenas em crateras de vulcões adormecidos e o cozido de carnes se faz debaixo da terra quente.
riddle_english: We are nine islands where cows graze serenely in the craters of dormant volcanoes and the meat stew is cooked under the hot earth.

riddle_original: Sou as margens escarpadas cheias de socalcos vinhateiros, onde a uva ferve no verão sufocante para um dia vir a ser um vinho generoso.
riddle_english: I am the steep banks full of vine terraces, where the grape boils in the suffocating summer to one day become a generous wine.

riddle_original: Onde eu acabo, o mar começa; sou o penhasco ventoso de Sintra que ostenta o título de ponta mais ocidental do continente europeu.
riddle_english: Where I end, the sea begins; I am the windy cliff in Sintra that boasts the title of the westernmost point of the European continent.

riddle_original: Sou o curso de água dos estudantes, banho as escadarias antigas da velha academia e oiço as serenatas cantadas de capa e batina rasgada.
riddle_english: I am the watercourse of the students, I bathe the ancient steps of the old academy and listen to the serenades sung in torn capes and cassocks.

riddle_original: Sou a planície dourada imensa onde o calor aperta sem piedade no verão e os sobreiros dão a sua cortiça à sombra do montado.
riddle_english: I am the vast golden plain where the heat is mercilessly intense in the summer and the cork oaks yield their cork in the shade of the wooded area.

riddle_original:
Traz no apelido a gente inteira,
Mas na alma, a falta de unidade.
Mentia tão bem a dor que sentia,
Que até a si próprio se convencia.
riddle_english:
His nickname embodies the whole of us,
But his my soul, a lack of unity.
He lied so well about the pain he felt,
That he even convinced himself.

riddle_original:
Sou a canção da desgraça e do desabafo, 
cantada à luz das velas por quem tem o peito cheio de nó na garganta. 
Não preciso de grandes berros, basta uma guitarrada por trás 
e uma alma que saiba o que é estar na penúria ou de coração lixado.
riddle_english:
I am the song of misfortune and venting, sung by candlelight by those with a knot in their throat.
 I don't need loud shouting; all it takes is a guitar behind me
 and a soul that knows what it's like to be broke or heartbroken.
riddle_note: This might be easier to guess by older generations since they are the ones who would listen to fado the most.

riddle_original: Sou a peça de roupa escura e franjada que abraça rigorosamente os ombros da cantadeira enquanto a guitarra chora a sina pelas ruelas.
riddle_english: I am the dark, fringed piece of clothing that strictly embraces the singer's shoulders while the guitar cries fate through the alleys.

riddle_original: Usei o meu escopro e o memorial de um convento para moldar a prosa portuguesa, mas prescindi dos pontos finais para ganhar a medalha em Estocolmo.
riddle_english: I used my chisel and a convent's memorial to shape Portuguese prose, but I dispensed with periods to win the medal in Stockholm.

riddle_original: Pintei mulheres cruas e contos folclóricos com traços inquietantes e pastel seco, vivendo em Londres mas mantendo a alma assombrada por histórias de embalar macabras.
riddle_english: I painted raw women and folktales with unsettling strokes and dry pastel, living in London but keeping a soul haunted by macabre lullabies.

riddle_original: Fui a melodia fraterna cantada a capella que tocou à meia-noite na Rádio Renascença, servindo de senha definitiva para os militares saírem à rua.
riddle_english: I was the fraternal melody sung a cappella that played at midnight on Rádio Renascença, serving as the definitive password for the military to take to the streets.

riddle_original: Dei voz a uma casa portuguesa, vesti de luto a saudade e levei o choro inconfundível do destino lisboeta aos palcos iluminados do mundo.
riddle_english: I gave voice to a Portuguese house, dressed longing in mourning, and brought the unmistakable cry of Lisbon's fate to the lit stages of the world.

riddle_original: Sou o pedaço quadrado de barro vidrado, quase sempre pintado de azul e branco, que reveste capelas e conta episódios em estações de comboio.
riddle_english: I am the square piece of glazed clay, almost always painted blue and white, that coats chapels and tells episodes in train stations.

riddle_original: Perdi um olho em Marrocos, mas vi muito mais além com a pena na mão, imortalizando o peito ilustre lusitano numa viagem até à Índia.
riddle_english: I lost an eye in Morocco, but saw much further with a pen in hand, immortalizing the illustrious Lusitanian chest on a journey to India.

riddle_original: Sou a peça intrincada de filigrana em ouro que arde no peito das minhotas vestidas a rigor nos dias exuberantes de romaria nortenha.
riddle_english: I am the intricate piece of gold filigree that burns on the chest of the Minho women dressed to the nines on exuberant days of northern pilgrimage.

riddle_original:
Já treinou muitos craques da bola e leva no peito o orgulho de quem percebe disto a dormir.
Com uma fala à bruta e mal parida,  onde o gramática é o que menos importa, encarna a pinta to tuga.
riddle_english:
He has coached many great soccer players and proudly carries the knowledge
 of someone who understands the sport even in his sleep.
With a blunt and poorly conceived way of speaking, where grammar is the least important thing, 
he embodies the typical Portuguese flair.

riddle_original:
Sou treinador de frases afiadas e finais europeias. 
Chamam-me de especial e não faço grande esforço para discordar.
riddle_english: I'm a coach of sharp wit and European finals. They call me special, and I don't make much effort to disagree.

riddle_original: Sou dragão do norte, e tripeiro no centro e sul. Represento o desporto nortenho em Portugal.
riddle_english: I am a dragon from the north, and a tripeiro from the center and south. I represent northern sport in Portugal.

riddle_original: Sou felino de onde venho, mas réptil para outros. Vivo uma rivalidade eterna de onde sou.
riddle_english: I am feline where I come from, but reptile to others. I live in an eternal rivalry with where I am from.

riddle_original:
Na canoagem, sou força de rio e silêncio de treino. 
Apesar de todas as minhas conquistas sou conhecido pelas minhas fitas e mau em perder.
riddle_english:
In canoeing, I am the strength of the river and the silence of training.
Despite all my achievements, I am known for my ribbons and for being a bad loser.

riddle_original: Sou a icónica corrida de agosto onde os ciclistas derretem no asfalto a quase quarenta graus na exigente subida à Senhora da Graça.
riddle_english: I am the iconic August race where cyclists melt on the asphalt at almost forty degrees on the demanding climb to Senhora da Graça.

riddle_original: Sou a lenda humilde vinda de África que vestiu a camisola do Benfica, fuzilou redes em 66 e cujo corpo descansa no Panteão Nacional.
riddle_english: I am the humble legend from Africa who wore the Benfica jersey, blasted nets in 66, and whose body rests in the National Pantheon.

riddle_original: Corri os quilómetros todos pelas ruas do mundo e sorri até à linha da meta, ganhando a maratona em Seul com as quinas ao peito.
riddle_english: I ran all the kilometers through the streets of the world and smiled all the way to the finish line, winning the marathon in Seoul with the national shield on my chest.

riddle_original: Ganhei dezenas de troféus e nasci no Funchal, mas o meu grito gutural de vitória saltando de costas tornou-se imitado em todos os recreios.
riddle_english: I won dozens of trophies and was born in Funchal, but my guttural victory cry jumping backward became imitated in all playgrounds.

riddle_original:
Não preciso de relva nem de botas com pitons, o meu palco é de rodas e o meu stick dita a lei. 
Dei a Portugal os primeiros mundiais de orgulho quando o futebol ainda gatinhava, e continuo a fazer a bola rolar mais rápido do que o olho humano consegue seguir.
riddle_english:
I don't need grass or studded boots, my stage is on wheels and my stick dictates the law. 
I gave Portugal its first world cups of pride when football was still in its infancy, and I keep making the ball roll faster than the human eye can follow.

riddle_original: Fico junto ao Tejo como guarda de pedra, com renda manuelina e memória de partidas. Vi caravelas antes de ver turistas.
riddle_english:
I stand by the Tagus River like a stone guardian, adorned with Manueline lace and memories of departures.
I saw caravels before I saw tourists.

riddle_original: Dizem que aqui nasceu o país, mas eu não peço certidão. Tenho castelo, berço e orgulho escrito nas muralhas.
riddle_english:
They say the country was born here, but I don't ask for a birth certificate. 
I have a castle, a birthplace, and pride written on the walls.

riddle_original:
Sou canto sem pressa, feito de vozes fundas e planície.
 Não preciso de grande palco, só alma de quem vive além do tejo.
riddle_english:
I am a song without haste, made of deep voices and plains.
I don't need a grand stage, just the soul of those who live beyond the Tagus.

riddle_original: Sou som de doze cordas que faz a saudade ganhar dedos. Sem mim, muito fado ficava sem chão.
riddle_english:
I am the sound of twelve strings that makes longing grow on its fingers. 
Without me, much fado would be left without a foundation.

riddle_original: Nasci dos ovos e do açúcar nos fornos de um mosteiro, mas fui batizado na fábrica ao lado, recheado de creme amarelo tostado e polvilhado a canela.
riddle_english: I was born from eggs and sugar in a monastery's ovens, but baptized in the factory next door, filled with toasted yellow cream and sprinkled with cinnamon.

riddle_original: Sou a sopa reconfortante de madrugada depois dos bailaricos dos Santos Populares, feita de couve fina e sempre coroada com uma rodela de chouriço.
riddle_english: I am the comforting late-night soup after the popular saints' dances, made of fine cabbage and always crowned with a slice of chorizo.

riddle_original: Durmo pacientemente em cascos grossos de carvalho na margem sombria de Gaia, para acabar a adoçar e aquecer a boca no fim das refeições festivas.
riddle_english: I sleep patiently in thick oak casks on the shady bank of Gaia, to end up sweetening and warming the mouth at the end of festive meals.

riddle_original: Sou a tapeçaria de chão feita de pedra calcária branca e preta que deslumbra a vista e faz tropeçar e escorregar turistas nas colinas molhadas.
riddle_english: I am the floor tapestry made of white and black limestone that dazzles the eye and makes tourists trip and slip on wet hills.

riddle_original: Pingo a minha gordura nas brasas acesas nas noites de Santo António, deitando um fumo caraterístico antes de aterrar em cima da fatia de pão rústico.
riddle_english: I drip my fat onto the hot coals on the nights of Santo António, emitting a characteristic smoke before landing on top of a slice of rustic bread.

riddle_original: Apareci sobre a copa de uma pequena azinheira perante três pastores atónitos, transformando a árida Cova da Iria no maior altar branco da nação.
riddle_english: I appeared over the canopy of a small holm oak before three astonished shepherds, transforming the arid Cova da Iria into the nation's largest white altar.

riddle_original: Danço numa perna só, mas não sou bailarina. Se me dás corda, fico a dormir em pé, mas assim que acordo, caio para o lado.
riddle_english: I dance on one leg, but I'm not a ballerina. If you give me enough rope, I'll fall asleep standing up,but as soon as I wake up, I fall to the side.

riddle_original: Este jogo de recreio treinava-nos, sem sabermos, para o triplo salto olímpico. Marcava-mos o chão com o que havia à mão, muitas vezes, bastavam três pedras.
riddle_english: This playground game unknowingly trained us for the Olympic triple jump.We marked the ground with whatever was at hand, often, three stones were enough.
riddle_note: This was a children game however it might be generation-specific.

riddle_original: Sou bicho de plástico que cresce em colecção e cabe numa mão fechada. No recreio, a minha força media-se em pancadas e regras inventadas.
riddle_english: I'm a plastic creature that grows up in a collection and fits in a closed fist. At recess, my strength was measured in punches and invented rules.

riddle_original:
No dia certo, bato à porta por doces e frutos. Não sou Halloween, 
mas também sei pedir com saco e lenga-lenga.
riddle_english: On the right day, I knock on the door for sweets and fruit. I'm not Halloween,but I also know how to ask with a bag and a little spiel.

riddle_original:
Tenho jogadores sem pernas e gritos de bancada em miniatura. 
Com duas mãos e muita raiva, faço campeonatos de café e garagem.
riddle_english:
I have players without legs and miniature crowd cheers.
With two hands and a lot of anger, I organize coffee shop and garage tournaments.

riddle_original:
Sou pequeno planeta de vidro que cabe no bolso. 
Quanto mais certeira a mira, mais amigos perdem tesouros no intervalo.
riddle_english:
I'm a small glass planet that fits in your pocket.
The more accurate the aim, the more friends lose treasures in between.

riddle_original: Com a minha eterna careca e camisola amarela, fui dobrado num estúdio e fiz as birras caseiras que todos os pais desesperavam a ver na televisão.
riddle_english: With my eternal bald head and yellow sweater, I was dubbed in a studio and threw the domestic tantrums that all parents despaired watching on television.

riddle_original: Fui o rapazinho rural de chapéu de palha que ensinou os miúdos a irem dormir mal a música de boa noite terminava no único canal da RTP.
riddle_english: I was the rural little boy with a straw hat who taught kids to go to sleep as soon as the goodnight song ended on the only RTP channel.

riddle_original: Apresentávamos desenhos animados ao fim da tarde no estúdio, mas uma suposta agressão física em direto transformou-nos num dos maiores mitos urbanos televisivos portugueses.
riddle_english: We presented cartoons late in the afternoon in the studio, but an alleged physical assault live on air turned us into one of the biggest Portuguese TV urban myths.

riddle_original:
Sou um herói de quatro patas que trocou a corte de França pelas vossas televisões. Juntos éramos um, dois e três, sempre prontos para a ação, 
e bastava ouvir os primeiros acordes da minha música para coláramos os olhos ao ecrã antes de ir brincar para a rua.
riddle_english:
I am a four-legged hero who traded the French court for your televisions. Together we were one, two and three, always ready for action, 
and it was enough to hear the first chords of my song to glue our eyes to the screen before going out to play.

riddle_original:
Não sou carpinteiro, mas de tanto insistir, faço serradura da tua paciência. Sou um bichinho de ouvido que não canta, mas cansa, batendo sempre na mesma tecla até te saltar a tampa.
O que te estou a fazer?
riddle_english:
I'm not a carpenter, but by insisting so much, I'm making sawdust out of your patience.
I'm a little earworm that doesn't sing, but gets tired, always hammering on the same note until you lose your temper.
What am I doing to you?

riddle_original: Nunca as tenho na língua quando falo sem rodeios. Sou bem direto e digo tudo o que me vem à cabeça sem pensar duas vezes.
riddle_english: I never have them on my tongue when I speak bluntly. I'm very direct and say whatever comes to my mind without thinking twice.

riddle_original: Quando o ar está gélido e o frio está de rachar está ganda...?
riddle_english: When the air is freezing and the cold is bone-chilling, it's great...?
riddle_note: This one is mainly popular on younger generations.

riddle_original: Algo excelente e muito bem composto dito muitas vezes em sarcasmo acompanhado de exclamação.
riddle_english: Something excellent and very well composed, often said sarcastically and accompanied by an exclamation.

riddle_original: Muito disto se tem, quando pouca vergonha se detém.
riddle_english: Much of this you have, when little shame you hold.

riddle_original:
Aquele que resta quando todos os outros já foram, mas que se comporta como se o mundo inteiro tivesse sido feito à sua medida. 
Confiante demais para passar despercebido, dono de si ao ponto de irritar quem o rodeia.
riddle_english:
The one who remains when everyone else has gone,but who behaves as if the whole world were made to measure for him.
Too confident to go unnoticed, so self-assured as to irritate those around him.

riddle_original: Não sou ferramenta, mas abro portas que a fila mantinha fechadas. Nasço de um primo, de um conhecido ou de alguém que conhece alguém.
riddle_english: I'm not a tool, but I open doors that the queue kept closed.I'm born from a cousin, an acquaintance, or someone who knows someone.

riddle_original: Sou dívida pequena com confiança grande. Escrevem-me no caderninho da mercearia e pagam-me quando o mês deixar.
riddle_english: I am a small debt with great trust. They write me down in the grocery store's ledger and pay me when the month allows.

riddle_original: Ficas assim quando estás todo partido, parecendo que alguém te deu um nó. Estás feito num quê?
riddle_english: You look like this when you're all broken up, like someone tied you in a knot. What's that all about?

riddle_original: Um local está assim quando não caberia nem mais um cabelo naquelas andanças. Está à?
riddle_english: A place is in such a state that there wouldn't even be room for another hair on those streets. It's on the..?

riddle_original: Num dia de calor, acompanha qualquer jola, oferecido até nos restaurantes mais leais ao costume.
riddle_english: On a hot day, it goes with any beer, often served for free in the most traditional restaurants.
riddle_note: This one uses a specific word to describe beer "jola" which is a popular term used by the people.

riddle_original: Conta-se que foi um mendigo, que a fazer a ronda, acabou por criar esta maravilhosa sopa.
riddle_english: The story goes that it was a beggar on his rounds who ended up creating this marvelous soup.

riddle_original:
Neste sítio sentes-te em casa porque aqui não procuras perfeição,procuras a paternidade da tradição. É o lugar para estares na boa, de cotovelos no balcão
 a aviar uma bifana acompanhada de uma imperial ou de um copo de vinho da casa.
riddle_english:
In this place you feel at home because here you don't seek perfection, you seek the legacy of tradition. It's the place for you to relax, elbows on the counter,
enjoying a bifana accompanied by a beer or a glass of house wine.

riddle_original: No final tudo é jola, num entanto enquanto no centro e no sul se avia uma fresquinha batizada em honra da realeza, no norte tem outro nome.
riddle_english:
In the end, everything is beer, however, while in the center and south you drink a fresh, 
baptized beer in honor of royalty, in the north it has another name.
riddle_note: This is a another term for 250ml tap beer used specifically in the north of Portugal and Azores.

riddle_original:
Sirvo-me curta, escura e a escaldar, sou o nome dado pelos lisboetas e outros para sul ao pequeno-almoço de Portugal. Enquanto no norte me chamam pelo nome da máquina, 
aqui sou o acrónimo de quem não aguenta o amargo.
riddle_english:
I serve myself short, dark, and scalding hot; I am the name given by Lisbon residents and others
in the south to Portuguese breakfast. While in the north they call me by the name of the machine, 
here I am the acronym for those who can't stand the bitterness.

riddle_original: Sou gostoso ao lanche e enquanto no norte tenho nome de Imperador, aqui no sul perco a patente.
riddle_english: I'm tasty as a snack, and while in the north I'm called an Emperor, in the south I lose my rank.

riddle_original: Quando a comida parece estar mesmo no ponto e estamos com aquele apetite chamamos-lhe de....
riddle_english: When the food looks on point and we're feeling that appetite, we call it...
riddle_note: This expression is more relevant to specific younger generations.

riddle_original: Sou sandes com alma de tasca e molho que não aceita timidez. No Porto, como-me de faca, garfo e respeito.
riddle_english:
I'm a sandwich with the soul of a traditional tavern and a sauce that doesn't tolerate shyness. 
In Porto, I eat with a knife, fork, and respect.

riddle_original:
Sou um segurança guloso que guarda um tesouro amarelo bem escondido numa dobra de pão que é na verdade um bolo. 
O meu nome diz que sirvo para limpar a boca, mas a verdade é que, se o fizeres, ficas ainda mais lambuzado.
riddle_english:
I'm a greedy security guard who keeps a well-hidden yellow treasure in a fold of bread that's actually a cake. 
My name says I'm for wiping your mouth, but the truth is, if you do, you'll get even more messy.

riddle_original:
Contaram uma piada tão boa na vitrina que a minha massa se partiu toda a rir. Tenho as tripas todas de fora, os miolos de gila à mostra e as amêndoas fora do sítio. 
Se alguém me tentar pôr direito, perco a piada toda.
riddle_english:
They told such a good joke in the shop window that my dough broke apart laughing.
My guts are all hanging out, my pumpkin brains are showing, and my almonds are out of place.
If anyone tries to straighten me out, it'll be ruining the whole joke.

riddle_original:
Os dicionários normais não reconhecem os meus dialectos, e os ginásios não ensinam a minha ginástica pélvica. 
Fui a surpresa que o país não pediu numa manhã de televisão, cantando como uma rola engasgada.
riddle_english:
Regular dictionaries don't recognize my dialects, and gyms don't teach my pelvic floor exercises.
I was the surprise the country didn't ask for on a morning television show, singing like a choking dove.

riddle_original:
A minha altura é inversamente proporcional à energia que gasto logo pela manhã a estragar as letras de músicas famosas. 
O rádio é a minha casa, mas à noite, se te vires aflito a responder a perguntas, eu lanço-te um curinga.
riddle_english:
My height is inversely proportional to the energy I expend first thing in the morning ruining the lyrics of famous songs.
The radio is my home, but at night, if you find yourself struggling to answer questions, I'll throw you a wild card.

riddle_original:
O meu armário parece uma paleta de aguarelas, mas a minha postura é sempre de lorde e trato toda a gente por 'você'. 
Já partilhei o trono com a rainha das manhãs, mas hoje sou o confessor das tardes chorosas.
riddle_english:
O meu armário parece uma paleta de aguarelas, mas a minha postura é sempre de lorde e trato toda a gente por 'você'. 
Já partilhei o trono com a rainha das manhãs, mas hoje sou o confessor das tardes chorosas.

riddle_original:
Sou o único homem em Portugal a quem todos confiam as chaves para estacionar na garagem da vizinha. 
O meu chapéu é a coroa não oficial das festas da terrinha e, na minha mesa, o cheiro é sempre a bacalhau.
riddle_english:
I'm the only man in Portugal everyone trusts with the keys to park in the neighbor's garage.
My hat is the unofficial crown of the local festivities, and my table always smells of cod.

riddle_original:
Considero a água um insulto à sede e prefiro líquidos com mais graus. 
Exijo que a festa dure toda a noite, sempre com o peito ao fresco, e quando o refrão pede ajuda, mando de imediato chamar o António.
riddle_english:
I consider water an insult to thirst and prefer liquids with higher alcohol content.
I demand that the party last all night, always keeping my chest cool, and when the chorus calls for help, I immediately send for António.

riddle_original:
Se me pedires para imitar um animal, sai-me um felino muito afeminado.Transformei uma ofensa de rua numa coroa de diamantes, 
e fui a única pessoa capaz de ir para uma quinta no meio do mato de saltos altos e plumas.
riddle_english:
If you ask me to imitate an animal, I'll come out looking like a very effeminate feline.
I transformed a street insult into a diamond crown,
and I was the only person capable of going to a farm in the middle of nowhere wearing high heels and feathers.

riddle_original:
O meu verbo favorito é 'rodar' e não há balança que me assuste. Não sou vendedor de eletrodomésticos, mas ao final da tarde dou frigoríficos a pessoas certeiras. 
O meu adjetivo de eleição resume-se a uma palavra que grito com os braços no ar.
riddle_english:
My favorite verb is 'to rotate' and no scale scares me. I'm not an appliance salesman,
but at the end of the day I give refrigerators to discerning people.
My adjective of choice can be summed up in one word that I shout with my arms in the air.

riddle_original:
Comecei por beber café de roupão e pantufas a comentar a vida alheia, mas agora sou o dono da casa nas manhãs. 
Falo mais rápido que a minha própria sombra e adoro fechar portugueses dentro de uma casa vigiada.
riddle_english:
I started out drinking coffee in my bathrobe and slippers, gossiping about other people's lives, but now I'm the master of the house in the mornings.
I talk faster than my own shadow and I love locking Portuguese people inside a guarded house.

riddle_original:
A minha carreira começou misturada com uma fruta doce e muito açúcar, mas sem nunca ir ao pomar. 
Entre saltos de canais e panelas verdadeiras na cozinha, sou o galã de novelas que todas as mães portuguesas queriam ter como genro.
riddle_english:
My career began mixed with sweet fruit and lots of sugar, but without ever going to the orchard.
Between channel surfing and real pots in the kitchen, I'm the soap opera heartthrob that every Portuguese mother would want as a son-in-law.

riddle_original:
Nunca precisei de beber café porque já nasci ligado aos 220 volts. Consigo correr um estúdio inteiro sem respirar, 
tenho um verdadeiro jardim zoológico no meu quintal e sou o grande show de sorrisos da televisão.
riddle_english:
I've never needed to drink coffee because I was born wired for 220 volts. I can run around an entire studio without breathing, 
I have a veritable zoo in my backyard, and I'm the biggest smile show on television.

riddle_original: Про этого политика говорят, что он предсказывал будущее
riddle_english: They say this politician predicted the future
riddle_hint:
Мем
Он просил Сафонова оплатить в аптеке
human_answer_comment: We could not solve it, as we did not know about Safonov. May be it makes sense to replace it with the riddle based on its hint "Про этого политика говорят, что он предсказывал будущее?"

riddle_original: Этого политика можно навестить после его смерти
riddle_english: This politician can be visited after his death
riddle_hint: Его мемориал на главной площади страны
human_answer_comment: We solved it, but were confused by "встретиться" and suggest to reformulate it with "Этого политика можно навестить после его смерти"?

riddle_original: Он подал в отставку от усталости под Новый год
riddle_english: He resigned on the New Year's Eve because he was tired
riddle_hint:
Мем
В реальности он не произносил эту известную фразу

riddle_original: Он часто публично целовался с другими политиками
riddle_english: He often publicly kissed other politicians
riddle_hint: На Берлинской стене есть граффити, изображающее его поцелуй

riddle_original: Он известен своей любовью к телефонам и гаджетам
riddle_english: He is known for his love for smartphones and gadgets

riddle_original: Он говорит на английском от всего сердца с сильным акцентом
riddle_english: He speaks English sincerely, with a strong accent

riddle_original: По какому ювелирному изделию можно судить о политике центробанка
riddle_english: By what piece of jewelry can you judge the central bank's policy?

riddle_original: Он известен своей суровостью, и его любимым вином была Хванчкара
riddle_english: He was known for his harshness, and his favorite wine was Khvanchhkara

riddle_original: Он снимался в американской рекламы пиццы
riddle_english: He appeared in American pizza commercial

riddle_original: Он постоянно устраивает смену напольного покрытия в честь наступления нового сезона
riddle_english: He constantly changes the flooring to celebrate the new season

riddle_original: Популярный вид проживания с соседями в квартире
riddle_english: Popular style of living with roommates in an apartment

riddle_original: Он потерялся с иностранцами в лесу и вошел в историю
riddle_english: He got lost with foreigners in the woods and made history
riddle_hint: Так еще называют человека, уверенно ведущего людей в неизвестном направлении

riddle_original: Магическая фигура начала 20 века с плохой репутацией и влиятельными друзьями
riddle_english: Magical figure of the early XX century with a bad reputation and influential friends.

riddle_original: Столько пальцев эта женщина из XVII века показывает на известной картине.
riddle_english: This many fingers does this woman from the 17th century show in a famous painting.

riddle_original: Государь Император скоропостижно скончался от апоплексического удара...
riddle_english: His Imperial Majesty suddenly passed away from an apoplectic stroke...
human_answer_comment: would specify "Государь Император скоропостижно скончался от апоплексического удара этим предметом"

riddle_original: Какое "животное" утонуло в Чудском озере?

They do not bow down to anyone, but patiently wait for others to come and admire them.						
They cannot be found inside of a cave, but more resemble to stalactites that have descended to the ground.

riddle_original: Оаза усред града, џунгла унутар бетонске џунгле, место где су ретке птице нашле свој дом.
riddle_english: An oasis in the middle of the city, a jungle within a concrete jungle, a place where rare birds have found their home.

riddle_original:
Стоји као острво усред мора у близини Дунава.
Планински ланац пун минералних извора, где су своје уточиште нашли свештеници и виноградари.
riddle_english:
It stands like an island in the middle of the sea near the Danube.					
A mountain range full of mineral springs, where priests and winegrowers have found their refuge.

riddle_original:
Има мало нафте у њој. Свуда око ње су њиве, а у њој као на песковитој плажи у Мексику.
Темишвар је близу, али се налази с друге стране границе.
riddle_english:
There is some oil in it. All around it are fields, and inside it is as if one were to find themself on a sandy beach in Mexico.						
Timisoara is not so close, but on the other side of the border nevertheless.

riddle_original:
Место рођења и резиденција многих владара.
Иако је у Војводини, са својим значајем и величином се у давна времена могао поредити са Лондоном и Римом.
riddle_english: The birthplace and residence of many rulers. Although it is in Vojvodina, its importance and size could have been compared to London and Rome during ancient times.

riddle_original: Због српске краљице, један топоним у Србији носи назив по биљци из породице маслина.
riddle_english: Because of a Serbian queen, a place in Serbia bears the name of a plant from the olive family.

riddle_original: Точи као у кафићу, али не пиво него искључиво воду, мада личи на чинију са куваним вином.
riddle_english: It pours like in a cafe, not beer, but instead exclusively water, although it resembles a bowl with mulled wine.

riddle_original: Густо као џунгла, али нема тло. Иако је близу Саве, увис расте висока трска кроз коју и чамац тешко пролази.
riddle_english: Dense as a jungle, but has no firm ground. Although it is close to the Sava River, there are tall reeds that make it difficult even for a boat to pass through.

riddle_original: Место сусрета двеју река. Иако му име тврди супротно, ту ништа не стоји мирно већ неометано протиче.
riddle_english: The meeting place of two rivers. Although its name claims the opposite, nothing stands still there but instead flows unhindered.

riddle_original: Шта се бјели у гори зеленој?
riddle_english: What's so white upon yon verdant forest?
reference_answer_english: The tent of Aga, Hasan Aga

riddle_original: Који познати српски филм снимљен деведесетих година носи у свом називу нову нијансу царске боје?
riddle_english: Which famous Serbian film made in the 1990s carries a new shade of imperial color in its title?

riddle_original: Уз који инструмент су се певале јуначке народне песме?
riddle_english: Which instrument accompanied the singing of heroic folk songs?

riddle_original: Које коло не чује?
riddle_english: Which circuit doesn't hear?

riddle_original: Како се зове уметнички покрет у чијем настанку у Београду је учествовало и двоје Руса?
riddle_english: What is the name of the artistic movement in whose creation in Belgrade two Russians participated?

riddle_original: Која птица је приказана у нашем грбу?
riddle_english: What bird is depicted in our coat of arms?

riddle_original: У које пристаниште се упутила француска лађа са српским војницима?
riddle_english: Which port did the French ship with Serbian soldiers head to?

riddle_original: Која уметница је данима корачала Кинеским зидом да би се срела са својим партнером и да би озваничила крај везе?
riddle_english: Which artist walked the Great Wall of China for days to meet her partner and make the end of the relationship official?

riddle_original: Који део наше народне ношње се односи на војничку традицију?
riddle_english: What part of our national costume relates to military tradition?

riddle_original: Како се зове вила која се натпевавала са Милошем на Мирочу?
riddle_english: What is the name of the fairy who competed in singing with Miloš on Miroč?

riddle_original: Фудбалер који је спона између напада и одбране, у језику врста речи.
riddle_english: Footballer who is a link between offense and defense, a word category

riddle_original: Њихови навијачи себе сматрају јунацима, а њихови ривали их зову погрдном речју за националну мањину
riddle_english: Their fans consider themselves heroes, their rivals call them a slur

riddle_original: Бивши фудбалер који је био зид за црвене ђаволе из Манчестера
riddle_english: The former footballer who was a stalwart for the red devils from Manchester

riddle_original: Са три злата на Олимпијади и светском првенству у овом тимском спорту Србија је међ најбољима на свету
riddle_english: With 3 golds at the olympic games and 3 world cups Serbia is one of the best at this team sport

riddle_original: Италијанска игра која је популарна међ старијим мушкарцима
riddle_english: Italian game which is popular with older men

riddle_original: Краљ НБА лиге који више воли коње и игрице него свој спорт
riddle_english: The king of the NBA who likes horses and video games more than his sport

riddle_original: Први фудбалски тим из Србије у европском финалу, из Брисела су се вратили само са болом пораза од белих.
riddle_english: The first Serbian football team in a European final, from Brussels they returned only with the pain of defeat at the hands of "Los Blancos"

riddle_original: Нападач који свим својим срцем игра за стару даму
riddle_english: Striker who played for the old lady with his whole heart

riddle_original: Српски спортиста који је стриктном дијетом дошао до дуге каријере на врху свог спорта
riddle_english: Serbian athlete who achieved everything in his sport with a strict diet over his long career

riddle_original: Легенда у крејвен котеџу рођен у Смедереву вољен код сврака на северу Енглеске
riddle_english: A legend at Craven Cottage, born in Smederevo also beloved by the Magpies in the north of England

riddle_original:
Лађа насукана на сувом.
Има два рога као неки инсект, али не мрда из шуме у којој се налази.
Није фатаморгана, него морепловац са севера који се обрео на Балканском полуострву.
riddle_english:
A ship stranded on dry land.					
It has two horns like an insect, but it doesn't move from the forest which it inhabits.					
It's not a mirage, but a sailor from the north who found himself on the Balkan peninsula.

riddle_original:
Ратник који неуморно бди над Београдом, голуб му је пријатељ,
гледа ушће двеју река, али изнад свега жели мир.
riddle_english:
A warrior who tirelessly watches over Belgrade, a pigeon is his friend,				
he looks at the confluence of two rivers, but above all he wants peace.
reference_answer_english: Statue of the Victor on Kalemegdan

riddle_original: Није из Арабије, већ са југа Србије. Шаре су им сличне, али овде нема Аладина да полети на њему.
riddle_english: It is not from Arabia, but from the south of Serbia. Their patterns are similar, but here there is no Aladdin to take off and fly on it.

riddle_original:
Стоји изнад Дунава, као знамење и подсетник,
ванвременска порука да сваког морнара подсети
да су овом великом реком некад пловили велики владари.
riddle_english:
It stands above the Danube, as a sign and a reminder,			
a timeless message to remind every sailor			
that this great river was once sailed by great rulers.

riddle_original:
Место верског ходочашћа чији су прозори послужили
као дизајнерски узор савременим модернистичким и минималистичким архитектама.
riddle_english:
A place of religious pilgrimage whose windows served				
as a design model, a template for contemporary modernist and minimalist architects.

riddle_original:
Нису маријачи, али по својој умешности умногоме подсећају на њих,
само што не користе гитаре.
Окупљају се једном годишње, да прославе свој позив, одсвирају своје највеће хитове, и да виде ко је најбољи.
riddle_english:
They are not mariachis, but they resemble them a lot in terms of their skills,						
only they don't use guitars.						
They gather once a year to celebrate their calling, playing their greatest hits, and determining who is the best.

riddle_original:
Облика је као једно, али нема љуску.
Тврђе је од камена, струја чини да се креће, али га испећи не може.
riddle_english:
It is shaped like one, but it has no shell.				
It is harder than stone, electricity makes it move, but it cannot be baked.

riddle_original:
Глава му је гола као врхови планина на којима борави,
а крагна светло сива, подсећа на арктичку капуљачу или ролку.
Крила су му сива, а може да прелети и преко 2000 километара.
riddle_english:
His head is as white and bare as the peaks of the mountains on which he dwells,				
and the collar is light gray, reminiscent of an arctic hood or a turtleneck.				
Its wings are gray, and it can fly over 2000 kilometers.

riddle_original:
Село древног народа. Делимично закопано испод слојева земље на обали Дунава,
стециште људи који су били обични рибари, али такође истовремено и врсни математичари и астрономи.
riddle_english:
The village of the ancient people. Partially buried under layers of earth on the banks of the Danube River,                                                        
a meeting place of people who were ordinary fishermen, at the same time excellent mathematicians and astronomers.

riddle_original: Када млада дође први пут у младожењину кућу, подиже га и окреће три пута укруг.
riddle_english: When a bride enters the groom's home for the first time, she lifts it up and turns it around three times.

riddle_original: Ова дечија игра захтева спретност и снагу, победнички тим узима једног играча из пораженог тима; данас назив победничког романа на конкурсу Book-e.
riddle_english: This children's game requires agility and strength; the winning team takes one player from the losing team. Today, it is also the title of the winning novel in the Booka competition.

riddle_original: Од стакла је, а унутра има перо разних боја. Неки су их само скупљали, а други су се њима играли. Ко убаци у рупу, добија поен.
riddle_english: It is made of glass and contains a colorful swirl inside. Some children simply collected them, while others played with them. Whoever gets one into the hole scores a point.

riddle_original: Користи се у изради одеће, а деца га користе за игру у којој се прескаче. Можеш је играти сам или у друштву.
riddle_english: It is used in making clothing, and children use it in a game where they jump over it. You can play it alone or with friends.

riddle_original: Тимска игра лоптом, започиње се ногом или руком, а наставља било којим делом тела осим руке. Сваки играч има своје поље.
riddle_english: A team ball game that starts with a kick or hand, and continues using any part of the body except the hands. Each player has their own field.

riddle_original: Ову дечију емисију водио је глумац који је добио надимак по имену емисије и има везе са геометријским телима.
riddle_english: This children's TV show was hosted by an actor who earned a nickname based on the show's title, which is related to geometric solids.

riddle_original: Дечија музичка емисија која се емитовала недељом ујутру, а презиме водитеља те емисије је назив једног дана у седмици.
riddle_english: A children's music show that aired on Sunday mornings; the host's surname is also the name of one day of the week.

riddle_original: Омиљена посластица свих малишана, најлепше се једе са млеком а има везе са агрегатним стањем материје.
riddle_english: A favorite treat of all children, best eaten with milk, and its name is related to a state of matter.

riddle_original: Омиљени дечији слаткиш. Маже се на хлеб, а може и без хлеба. Заштитни знак му је веверица.
riddle_english: A favorite children's sweet spread. It is usually spread on bread, but can be eaten without bread as well. Its trademark symbol is a squirrel.

riddle_original: Омиљени дечији слаткиш, који у имену има једну врсту воћа.
riddle_english: A favorite children's candy whose name contains the name of a type of fruit.

riddle_original: Јунакиње српског цртаног филма, добиле су имена по ћеркама познатог певача забавне музике.
riddle_english: The heroines of a Serbian animated series, named after the daughters of a famous pop singer.

riddle_original: Прави се од теста, а име му има везе са црквеном одеждом.
riddle_english: Made from dough, and its name is related to a piece of church vestment.

riddle_original: Ово јело се прави од зимнице, а по називу би човек помислио да се једе на једном породичном слављу.
riddle_english: This dish is made from winter preserves, and judging by its name, one might think it is eaten at a family celebration.

riddle_original: Пратилац је свих српских славља, одлично иде уз печење а име носи по једном великом народу.
riddle_english: A companion to every Serbian celebration, it goes perfectly with roast meat and is named after a great nation.

riddle_original: Некад су га бабе деци мазале на хлеб као посластицу и стављале као облогу против кашља.
riddle_english: Grandmothers used to spread it on bread as a treat for children and also apply it as a remedy for coughs.

riddle_original: Изазива страх у Срба, па држе затворена врата и прозоре да их не убије.
riddle_english: It causes fear among Serbs, who keep their doors and windows shut so it will not kill them.

riddle_original: Имају је само Срби, а највећа је у децембру кад цела земља стане јер нема ко да ради.
riddle_english: Only Serbs have it, and it is at its biggest in December, when the whole country seems to come to a standstill because nobody is working.

riddle_original: Рекло би се да је омиљена животиња у Срба пошто свако друго дете носи име по њему.
riddle_english: One might think it is Serbs' favorite animal, since every other child seems to be named after it.

riddle_original: Навикао да стоји, има ребра, али не дише, а нема кичму. Стално има вишка енергије коју шири око себе.
riddle_english: Used to stand constantly, it has ribs, but it doesn't breathe, and it doesn't have a spine. It constantly has excess energy that it spews around.

riddle_original:
Може да добаци у вис више него што било ко може да скочи;
никад се не помера лево-десно или напред-назад, али те увек одведе на путовање.
riddle_english:
It can throw higher than anyone is able to jump;				
it never moves left and right or back and forth, but always takes you on a journey.

riddle_original:
Нема ноге нити грбу као камила,
и није пустиња једино место где га можете наћи,
али уме под‌једнако добро да чува воду, док му се кофа увек нађе негде у близини.
riddle_english:
It has no legs or hump like a camel,					
and the desert isn't the only place where one can find it,					
but it knows how to conserve water just as well, while its bucket is always somewhere nearby.

riddle_original: Троглаве Нишлије који су зачарали рок сцену региона
riddle_english: The three-headed Niš natives who captured the rock scene in the region

riddle_original: Култни бенд из Београда који дели име са руском царицом
riddle_english: The cult group from Belgrade which shares a name with a Russian tsarina

riddle_original: Песма легендарног новосадског певача која је постала химна младих социјалиста у Југославији.
riddle_english: A song of the legendary Novi Sad singer which became an anthem of the socialist youth in Yugoslavia

riddle_original: Певач и текстописац родом из Сарајева који је радио са Игијем Попом и Кајом.
riddle_english: A singer-songwriter from Sarajevo known for working with Iggy Pop and Kayah

riddle_original: Гитариста, текстописац и певач бенда који носи његово име, познат по продавници тајни и јелу од рибе.
riddle_english: Guitarist and singer-songwriter for a band named after him, known for the store of secrets and a dish made of fish

riddle_original: Алт-рок група из Новог Сада, почетна слова њихових албума заједно дају име њиховог родног града
riddle_english: Alt-rock group from Novi Sad, the starting letters of their albums spell their hometown

riddle_original: Хип-хоп састав који у свом називу носи свој родни град
riddle_english: Hip-hop union which carries their home town in their name

riddle_original: Омиљена песма Европе 2007. године.
riddle_english: Europe's favourite song in 2007

riddle_original: Српски класични композитор, на љубичастој новчаници.
riddle_english: Serbian classical composer, on the purple bill

riddle_original: Народна песма о Крфу у првом светском рату
riddle_english: Folk song about Corfu in the First World War

riddle_original: Српски инжењер и изумитељ који има око 300 патената
riddle_english: Serbian engineer and inventor who has around 300 patents

riddle_original: Рибар и доктор математике чије име носи једна од београдских гимназија
riddle_english: Fisherman and doctor of maths after whom a Belgrade gymnasium is named

riddle_original: Астроном, геофизичар и климатолог, његова теорија је објаснила промене у клими и ледена доба
riddle_english: Astronomer, climatologist, geophysicist whose theory explained climate change and ice ages

riddle_original: Течно сребро које има душу, број 80
riddle_english: Liquid silver which has a soul, number 80

riddle_original: Машина која електромагнетном индукцијом постиже обртање
riddle_english: A machine which uses electromagnetic induction to create rotational movement

riddle_original: Рођен у Наполеоновој Француској, овај ботаничар је коначно доказао постојање зимзеленог дрвета названог по њему
riddle_english: Born in Napoleonic France, this botanist finally proved the existence of an evergreen named after him

riddle_original: Ову машину из Крагујевца користи Брус Вилис у филму Умри Мушки
riddle_english: This machine from Kragujevac used by Bruce Willis in Die Hard

riddle_original: Први кућни рачунар у бившој Југославији
riddle_english: The first home computer in former Yugoslavia

riddle_original: Један од оснивача претходнице НАСЕ, његов рад је помогао Америчкој војсци да лакше пронађу немачке подморнице у првом светском рату
riddle_english: One of the founders of NASA's predecessor, his research helped the United States Army to easily find German U-boats in WWI

riddle_original: Животиња дугачког репа, уређај које се користи за прецизније управљање рачунаром
riddle_english: A long-tailed animal, a device which allows a more precise use of a computer.

riddle_original: සිංහයෙක් අතින් කඩුවක් දරා සිටියත්, මම යුද්ධයක් නොව රජයේ මුද්‍රාවක්. නිල ලියවිල්ලක මගේ පෙනුම ආ විට රටම කතා කරයි. මම කවුද?
riddle_english: Though a lion holds a sword in me, I am not a war but the state seal. When I appear on an official document, the country speaks. What am I?

riddle_original: රතු, තැඹිලි, කොළ, මරූන් වටයක් මැද බෝ කොළ හතරක් රැකගත් සිංහයාගේ නිවස මමයි. මම කවුද?
riddle_english: I am the home of the lion guarded by four bo leaves, with red, orange, green, and maroon around me. What am I?

riddle_original: රජෙක් නොවෙමි, නමුත් රාජ්‍ය නායකයාගේ වචනය බොහෝ නිල දොරවල් අරියි. ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ මේ තනතුර කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: I am not a king, but the words of this head of state open many official doors in Sri Lanka. What office is this?

riddle_original: ජනතාව තෝරන අය වාද කරන්නේ මෙහිදීය; නමෙන් එය ගඟක් අසල දූපතක මෙන් ඇසේ. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Those chosen by the people debate here; its name sounds like an island by water. What is it?

riddle_original: සමහරු මාව 'නිදහස් චතුරශ්‍රයේ මතකය' අසලින් දකී; නමුත් මගේ කාර්යය රටේ නීති රකින්නයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Some see me near the memory of Independence Square, but my role is to guard the laws of the country. What am I?

riddle_original: මගේ නම අගමැති සමග බැඳී ඇත; රජයේ වැඩ බෙදන කාමර ගොඩක් මගේ යටතේ ගැණේ. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: My name is tied to the prime minister; many rooms of government work are grouped under me. What am I?

riddle_original: ඡන්ද පෙට්ටියට කලින් පත්‍රිකාවේ ලකුණක් ඉදිරියේ කතිරයක් දමන දිනය මමයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: I am the day when a cross is marked before a symbol on a paper before it enters the ballot box. What am I?

riddle_original: මගේ පළාත් නම නවයක් වුණත්, දිස්ත්‍රික්ක විසි පහක් මගේ ඇඟේ රේඛා වෙයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: My provincial names are nine, but twenty-five districts draw lines on my body. What am I?

riddle_original: රටේ නීතියේ ඉහළම පොත මමයි; අලුත් වචනයක් එකතු කිරීමටද විශේෂ බහුතරයක් අවශ්‍ය වේ. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: I am the highest book of law in the country; even adding new words to me may need a special majority. What am I?

riddle_original: සියලු දෙනා එකම ඡන්ද අයිතිය' යන සිතුවිල්ල ලංකාවට ඉක්මනින් ගෙන ආ පරණ කොමිසම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Which old commission brought the idea of universal franchise early to Ceylon?

riddle_original: තඹ පාට වැලි මත ආ අමුත්තාගේ නමෙන් රටේ එක් පරණ නමක් උපන්නේය. ඒ අමුත්තා කවුද?
riddle_english: From the visitor who came to copper-colored sand, one old name of the island was born. Who was he?

riddle_original: කැලණිතිස්ස රජුගේ දියණියක් මුහුදට පූජා වූ කතාවෙන් දකුණු රටේ නමක් බොහෝ දෙනා මතක තබා ගනී. ඇය කවුද?
riddle_english: A king’s daughter offered to the sea in a famous legend makes many remember a southern name. Who is she?

riddle_original: එළාර සමඟ ඇති වූ ගැටුමෙන් පසු රුවන්වැලි සෑය ගොඩනැඟූ අනුරාධපුර වීරයා කවුද?
riddle_english: Who was the Anuradhapura hero who fought Elara and built Ruwanweliseya?

riddle_original: එක මහාවැවක් නිසා නම පතළ වුණ, 'අහසෙන් වැටෙන ජල බිඳුවක්වත් මුහුදට නොයවන්න' කියූ රජු කවුද?
riddle_english: Which king, famous for a great reservoir, is remembered for not letting even rainwater flow unused to the sea?

riddle_original: බ්‍රිතාන්‍යයට උඩරට භාර වූ ලේඛනයේ නම, මඟුල් මඩුවේ සෙවණැල්ල සමඟ මතකයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: The document by which Kandyan rule passed to the British is remembered with the shadow of the Magul Maduwa. What is it?

riddle_original: වෙල්ලස්සේ කැරැල්ලේ කඩුවක් මෙන් මතකයේ සිටින, මරණයෙන් පසුවත් වීර නාමයක් ලැබූ මොනරවිල කෙනා කවුද?
riddle_english: The Monarawila figure remembered like a sword in the Uva-Wellassa rebellion later received a hero’s name. Who is he?

riddle_original: පෘතුගීසි, ලන්දේසි, ඉංග්‍රීසි යන තුන් මුහුදු බලවතුන් ලංකාවේ වෙරළ අල්ලා ගත් යුගය කුමක් ලෙස හැඳින්වේද?
riddle_english: What is the period when Portuguese, Dutch, and British sea powers controlled Sri Lanka’s coasts called?

riddle_original: අනුරාධපුරයේ පරණම බෞද්ධ උරුමයක් ලෙස බෝධි ශාඛාවක් රැගෙන ආ තෙරණිය කවුද?
riddle_english: Which nun brought the Bo sapling linked to one of Anuradhapura’s oldest Buddhist inheritances?

riddle_original: පොළොන්නරුවේ ගල් පොතක දිගු අකුරු මෙන් අදත් ඉතිහාසය කියවන ස්මාරකය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Which Polonnaruwa monument still reads history through long letters on stone?

riddle_original: 1948 පෙබරවාරි හතරේ උදෑසනින් පසුව, කඩුවක් නැතිව ලැබුණු ජය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: After the morning of February 4, 1948, what victory was gained without a sword?

riddle_original: මා වටේ මුහුද, මැද කඳු, නම 'මුතු ඇටය' කියා ආදරයෙන් කියයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Sea around me, hills in my middle, lovingly called a pearl. What am I?

riddle_original: වලාකුළු අතට අල්ලන්න යන තේ රටේ සීතල හදවත මමයි. මගේ නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: I am the cold heart of the tea country where clouds feel close enough to touch. What is my name?

riddle_original: පාදයක් මෙන් නමක් ඇති, ඉර නැගීමට පෙර පහන් රැස් දකින කන්ද කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Which mountain has a name like a foot and sees lights before sunrise?

riddle_original: කන්ද උඩරටට වළල්ලක් මෙන් පෙනෙන වැව, නගරයේ දළදා මාලිගාව අසල නිහඬයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: The lake like a ring in the hill capital lies quietly near the Temple of the Tooth. What is it?

riddle_original: මහවැලි ගඟ මුහුදට සමු දෙන නැගෙනහිර වරාය නගරය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What eastern port city is near where the Mahaweli River says goodbye to the sea?

riddle_original: ගල් පර්වතයක් උඩ සිංහ පාද ඉතිරි කර රාජධානියක් අහසට නැඟුණ තැන කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Where did a kingdom rise into the sky, leaving lion paws on a rock?

riddle_original: උතුරේ අගට ළං වූ නගරය, යාල් සංගීත නමක් දරයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: The city close to the northern tip carries a name linked to the yaal instrument. What is it?

riddle_original: කොළඹ සහ ගාල්ල අතර මුහුදු දොරකඩ, බෝට්ටු හා කැස්බෑ කතා ගැලපෙන වෙරළ නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Between Colombo and Galle, a coastal name fits boats and turtle stories. What is it?

riddle_original: වියළි කලාපයේ විශාල වැවක් අසල ඉදිවූ පරණ රාජධානියේ දෙවන මහා නගරය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What is the second great ancient capital built near a large dry-zone reservoir?

riddle_original: ඉන්දියාවට ආසන්නම දිගු වැලි මංතීරුවේ කථා කරන පාලම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What is the long sandy chain near India often spoken of as a bridge?

riddle_original: මුහුණ වර්ණවත්, ඇඳුම විශාල, නර්තනය පහතරට; යක් දෙවි අතර කතා කරන මම කවුද?
riddle_english: My face is colorful, my costume large, my dance low-country; I speak between yakku and gods. What am I?

riddle_original: බෙර හඬට වෙස් මුහුණක් නොව, උඩරට ඇඳුමක වෙස් තට්ටුවක් පැළඳ නටන කලාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not a mask but a headpiece in Kandyan costume dances to drums. What art is this?

riddle_original: පන්සල් බිත්තියක වර්ණයෙන් බුදු කතා කියන පැරණි සිතුවම් සම්ප්‍රදාය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What old painting tradition tells Buddhist stories in color on temple walls?

riddle_original: ගැටබෙරය හඬන විට උඩරට පාද මාරුවෙන නර්තන පවුල කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When the geta bera sounds, the hill-country feet change. What dance family is this?

riddle_original: එක් අතක තාලය, තවත් අතක වචනය; කවි මඩුවේ ඉක්මන් උත්තර දෙන ජනකලා රටාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Rhythm in one hand and words in another; what folk art gives quick answers in a poetry contest?

riddle_original: සීගිරි ගලේ බිත්තියක අහසේ මෙන් පාවෙන පරණ රූප නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What are the old figures that seem to float in the sky on Sigiriya’s wall?

riddle_original: දෙපසම තල දෙකක් ඇති බෙරයක්, උඩරට නැටුමට හදගැස්ම දෙයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A drum with two heads gives a heartbeat to Kandyan dance. What is it?

riddle_original: මැටි රූප, ලී කැටයම්, ලෝහ වැඩ—කන්ද උඩරට අතකඩ වැඩ සිහි කරන නගරය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Clay figures, wood carvings, metalwork—which hill-country town is known for handicraft hands?

riddle_original: ගැමි වේදිකාවක රාජකතා හා විහිළු එකට ගෙන යන පරණ නාට්‍ය කලාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What old village theatre art carries royal tales and jokes together?

riddle_original: සරල වචනත් ගැඹුරු සමාජ හඬත් එක් කළ 'මනමේ' වේදිකාවට ගෙනා නාමය කවුද?
riddle_english: Who brought Maname to the stage, joining simple words with a deep social voice?

riddle_original: බැට් එකක්, පන්දුවක්, දූපතක් සතුටින් අඬවූ 1996 රාත්‍රිය—මෙහි ක්‍රීඩාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A bat, a ball, and a 1996 night that made an island cry with joy—what sport is this?

riddle_original: සනත් හා කළු එක්ව ආරම්භයේම බිය නැතිව පහර දුන් ලෝක කුසලාන වසර කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: In which World Cup year did Sanath and Kalu attack fearlessly from the start?

riddle_original: යොර්කර් එකක් අවසානයේ වැටෙන විට, රැලි සහිත කොණ්ඩයත් සිනහවත් මතක් කරන පන්දු යවන්නා කවුද?
riddle_english: When a yorker falls at the end, which bowler with curly hair and a smile comes to mind?

riddle_original: ඔලිම්පික් ධාවන පථයේ රිදී මතකයක් ගෙනා, 'ආසියාවේ කළු මැණික' ලෙස කියන ක්‍රීඩිකාව කවුද?
riddle_english: Which athlete brought an Olympic silver memory and is called Asia’s Black Mare?

riddle_original: දකුණු අතින් පන්දුව කැරකී, පරීක්ෂණ කඩුලු අටසියයේ කන්දට නැගුණු ක්‍රීඩකයා කවුද?
riddle_english: Who spun the ball with his right hand and climbed to the mountain of 800 Test wickets?

riddle_original: දියගම නොව, මුහුද අසල රග්බි හඬ නිතර ඇසෙන කොළඹ ක්‍රීඩා සමාජයක නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not Diyagama; which Colombo club near the sea is often associated with rugby noise?

riddle_original: පාසල් දෙකක්, මහනුවර ක්‍රීඩාංගණයක්, 'බිග් මැච්' උණුසුමක්—මේ සංස්කෘතියේ ක්‍රීඩාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Two schools, a Kandy ground, big-match heat—what sport carries this culture?

riddle_original: කබඩි මැද 'කබඩි' කියා හුස්ම රැකගෙන පසෙකට යන ක්‍රීඩකයාගේ ඉලක්කය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: In kabaddi, while saying 'kabaddi' and holding breath, what is the raider’s aim?

riddle_original: ඇළ, වැව, මුහුද නොව; පාසල් ක්‍රීඩා උළෙලක නිල් පීල්ලේ වේගයෙන් දිය කපන ක්‍රීඩාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not a canal, tank, or sea; what sport cuts water fast in the blue lanes of a school meet?

riddle_original: ගාලු කොටුව පෙනෙන තණබිමක පන්දුව ඉහළට යන විට, පිටරට කණ්ඩායම්ද මතක් කරන ක්‍රීඩාංගණය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When a ball rises on a field with Galle Fort in view, which ground do foreign teams remember too?

riddle_original: දළදාව රැකගත් නගරයේ පහන් පෙරහැරෙන් ලොවට හඬ දෙන මාලිගාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Which temple in the city of the Tooth speaks to the world through a lit procession?

riddle_original: අනුරාධපුරයේ අතු පැලයක් නොව, රාජකීය මුරකාවල් ලැබූ පූජනීය බෝධිය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not just a sapling in Anuradhapura, which sacred Bo tree received royal guardianship?

riddle_original: සුදු ගෝලයක් මෙන් අහසට නැඟී, දුටුගැමුණු නම සමඟ පූජා ලබන සෑය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Which white dome rises to the sky and is worshipped with Dutugemunu’s name?

riddle_original: අටමස්ථානය කියන විට අනුරාධපුරයේ පූජනීය අටක් මතක වෙයි. ඒ පවුලේ නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When Atamasthana is said, eight sacred places in Anuradhapura are remembered. What is the group called?

riddle_original: ගල් ලෙනක් නොව, පර්වතයක් තුළ රන් බුදු රූප හා සිතුවම් සඟවාගෙන ඇති දඹුල්ලේ උරුමය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not just a cave, what Dambulla heritage hides golden Buddha images and paintings inside rock?

riddle_original: මුහුදට බැස ඇති ලන්දේසි බිත්ති, ගාලු නගරය පරණ ලෝකයක් බවට පත් කළේය. ඒ උරුමය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Dutch walls reaching the sea made Galle an old world. What heritage is this?

riddle_original: කටාරම් සහ ගල් පිළිම අතර, දඩයමේ හඬ නැතිව බෞද්ධ ඉතිහාසය ආරම්භ වන මිහිඳු ස්ථානය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Among rock steps and stone images, where does Buddhist history begin without the sound of hunting?

riddle_original: සීගිරිය චිත්‍රවලට පහළින්, අකුරු කැටපතක් මෙන් අදටත් කියවෙන පවුර කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Below Sigiriya’s paintings, which wall still reads like a mirror of letters?

riddle_original: රජවරුන්ගේ නාන තටාක නොව, අනුරාධපුරයේ මලක් මෙන් කැටයම් කළ ජල උරුමය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not royal bathing ponds; what Anuradhapura water heritage is carved like a flower?

riddle_original: මුහුද, සඳ, පෙරහැර, කාවඩි—උතුරේ හින්දු උරුමයක රතු-සුදු කෝපුරම් නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Sea, moon, procession, kavadi—which northern Hindu heritage has a red-white gopuram?

riddle_original: අලුත් පොත්, සුදු ඇඳුම, බෙල් එක; පොඩි කාලේ උදේ හතහමාරේ ලෝකය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: New books, white uniform, a bell; what is the 7:30 morning world of childhood?

riddle_original: අවුරුදු දවසේ කුඩා අත් දෙකක් ඇස් බැඳගෙන මැටි බඳුනක් සොයයි. ඒ ක්‍රීඩාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: On New Year’s day, small hands with covered eyes search for a clay pot. What game is this?

riddle_original: දරුවන් රවුමට ඉඳගෙන තාලයට අත් ගසන විට 'එළුවන් කෑම' කියා මතක් වන ක්‍රීඩාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Children sit in a circle and clap to a rhythm; which game remembers goats eating?

riddle_original: කඩදාසි අහසට යවන්නේ නූලකින්; වෙසක් කූඩුවක් නොව සුළඟේ සෙල්ලම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Paper is sent to the sky by a string; not a Vesak lantern, what is this wind game?

riddle_original: කොළ පාට පුවරුව, සුදු හුණු, 'අ' කියා පළමු අකුර දක්වන කාමරය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A green board, white chalk, and the first letter 'අ'—what room is this?

riddle_original: වෙසක් රෑට දරුවාගේ අතේ කුඩා ආලෝකයක්, කඩදාසි තරු මැද එල්ලෙයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: On Vesak night, a child’s small light hangs among paper stars. What is it?

riddle_original: පාසල් වාරය අවසන් වූ විට, පොත් බෑග් නිහඬ කර දරුවන් ගමට දුවන කාලය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When the school term ends, book bags go quiet and children run to the village. What time is this?

riddle_original: කුඩා අයෙකුගේ කෑම පෙට්ටියේ කෙසෙල් කොළ සුවඳත්, පොල් සම්බෝල රසත් ගෙන යන මැදහන කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: In a child’s lunch box, banana leaf scent and coconut sambol taste travel. What meal is it?

riddle_original: අවුරුදු උළෙලේ කුඩා පාද දෙකක් ගෝනි ඇතුළේ පැන පැන යන තරඟය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: At a New Year festival, small feet jump inside a sack. What race is it?

riddle_original: ඉරිදා උදේ මල් වට්ටිය අතේ, දරුවා පන්සලට යන පාඩම් පන්තිය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: On Sunday morning with a flower tray, what class does a child go to at the temple?

riddle_original: කහ, මිරිස්, කරපිංචා හඬන කුස්සියක, බත් එක්ක වැඩිපුරම ගමන් කරන දියර කතාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: In a kitchen where turmeric, chili, and curry leaves speak, what liquid story most often travels with rice?

riddle_original: උදේ වැඩට යන විට 'කොන්දොස්තර මල්ලි' හඬ ඇසෙන රතු-නිල් මාර්ග ලෝකය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: On the way to work, where do you hear the conductor’s call in a red-blue road world?

riddle_original: ගෙදර දොරට අමුත්තෙක් ආ විට, ප්‍රශ්නයට පෙර ලැබෙන උණුසුම් කෝප්පය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When a guest comes home, what warm cup is offered before the questions?

riddle_original: වැසි දවසක ගෙදර දොරට කුඩයක් වගේ නොව, පාද දෙකට මඩ වලක්වන සෙරෙප්පු මිතුරා කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: On a rainy day, not an umbrella, what sandal-friend saves feet from mud?

riddle_original: වෙළඳපොළේ 'කීයද අන්තිම?' කියා සිනහවකින් පටන් ගන්න දිනපතා කලාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: At the market, what daily art begins with a smile and 'what is the final price?'

riddle_original: කොළ කෑල්ලක ඔතා, හුණු, පුවක්, කරාබු නටන වැඩිහිටි පුරුද්ද කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Wrapped in a leaf, lime, areca nut, and clove dance in which elder’s habit?

riddle_original: විදුලිය ගිය විට ඉස්සර කාලේ ගෙදර සාකච්ඡාව පටන් ගන්නා කුඩා ආලෝකය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When power goes out, what small light starts the old-style home conversation?

riddle_original: දොර ළඟ පාවහන් ගලවා ඇතුල් වීමෙන් පෙන්වන නිහඬ ගරුකම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What silent respect is shown by removing footwear at the door?

riddle_original: කෙසෙල් කොළයක් පිඟානක් වී, බත්, මාලු, සම්බෝල එකට නටන වේල කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When a banana leaf becomes a plate and rice, fish, and sambol dance together, what meal is this?

riddle_original: සිංහල ගෙදරක වැඩිහිටියෙකුට කතා කරන විට නමට පසුව ගරු ලෙස එකතු වන වචනය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: In a Sinhala home, what respectful word is added after a name when speaking to an elder?

riddle_original: අවුරුදු උදේ කිරි උතුරන විට, ගෙදර පළමු සුබ ශබ්දය මමයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When milk boils over on New Year morning, I am the first auspicious sound in the house. What am I?

riddle_original: කැවුම්, කොකිස්, මුං කැවුම් එක්ව මේසය පුරවන කාලය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What season fills the table with kavum, kokis, and mung kavum?

riddle_original: කොළවල නම තිබුණත්, එය පත්‍රයක් නොව උදේ පානයක්; සහල්, පොල් කිරි, පලා එකට උණුවෙයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Though it has leaves in its name, it is not a leaf but a morning drink; rice, coconut milk, and greens boil together. What am I?

riddle_original: පොල් කිරි බත්ට එක්වී සුදු පැහැති චතුරස්‍රයක් වෙයි; අවුරුදු මේසයේ මුල්ම ආහාරය මමයි. මම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Coconut milk joins rice and becomes a white square; I am a first food on the New Year table. What am I?

riddle_original: තෙල් වළල්ලක මලක් පිපෙනවා; සිංහල අවුරුද්දේ මේසය එයින් හිස් නොවේ. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A flower blooms in a ring of oil; the Sinhala New Year table is rarely empty of it. What is it?

riddle_original: පොල් පැණි මැදින්, සහල් පිටි පිටින්, ත්‍රිකෝණයක් වගේ වාෂ්පයෙන් එන රසය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Treacle-coconut inside, rice flour outside, a triangular steamed taste—what is it?
riddle_hint: Needs local review: clue may fit lavariya better

riddle_original: කැටයක් නොවෙයි, කෙසෙල් කොළයක ඔතා ඉරිදා උදේ වෙළඳපොළෙන් එන සුදු-රතු උදේ කෑම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not a cube; wrapped in banana leaf and coming from Sunday market, what white-red breakfast is this?

riddle_original: කට්ට සම්බෝලය එක්වූ විට තවත් රස වන, නූල් වැනි උදේ ආහාරය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What string-like breakfast tastes even better with katta sambol?

riddle_original: පැණි පිරුණු කළු කුඩා ගෙඩියක්, තෙල් තටාකයෙන් අවුරුදු මේසයට එයි. එය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A small dark sweet ball comes from an oil pool to the New Year table. What is it?

riddle_original: පහන්, මල්, සුවඳ දුම් සමඟ පොහෝ දවසේ නිහඬව පිරෙන ස්ථානය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: With lamps, flowers, and incense, what place quietly fills on a Poya day?

riddle_original: තැන නොබලා කතා කළ විට, 'කට' ගැන කියන සිංහල උපමාව මතක් වේ. පාලනය කළ යුතු දේ කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When someone speaks without minding the place, a Sinhala saying about the mouth comes to mind. What must be controlled?

riddle_original: වැඩක් නරක නම් 'අත' මත දෝෂය දමනවා; සිංහල වාක්‍යයේ වගකීම ගන්නා ශරීර කොටස කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When work is bad, blame may fall on the 'hand'; in Sinhala phrasing, which body part takes responsibility?

riddle_original: වචනයක් පමණක් නොව, ලොකු අයෙකු අමතන විට නමට පසුව එන ගරු පදය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Not just a word; what respectful term comes after a name when addressing an elder?

riddle_original: අ' සිට '෴' දක්වා යන අකුරු ලෝකයේ නම කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: What is the world of letters that runs from 'අ' to '෴'?

riddle_original: නංගි, අක්කා, අයියා, මල්ලි—වයස හා ලේ බැඳීම එකම වචනවලින් කියන පවුල් භාෂාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Nangi, akka, aiya, malli—what family language tells age and kinship in single words?

riddle_original: පොඩි කෙනෙකුට ආදරයෙන් 'පුතා' කියයි; ලේ බැඳීම නැති විටත් එය භාවිතා වන සමාජ පදය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: A younger person is lovingly called 'putha'; even without blood relation, what social term is this?

riddle_original: වෙළඳසැලක මිල අඩු කරන්න ඉල්ලන විට, සිංහලෙන් 'කේවල්' කියන ක්‍රියාව කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When asking to reduce a shop price, what action is called 'kewal' in Sinhala?

riddle_original: ආයුබෝවන්' කියන විට වචනයට වඩා දිගු ආශිර්වාදයක් සැඟවී ඇත. එහි අදහස කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When saying 'Ayubowan', a blessing longer than the word is hidden. What does it mean?

riddle_original: දොරට ආ අමුත්තෙකුට 'කාලා යන්න' කියන එක, බඩට වඩා හදවත ගැන කියන පුරුද්ද කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: Telling a guest 'eat before you go' speaks more of heart than stomach. What custom is this?

riddle_original: සිංහලයේ 'ළ' හා 'ල' දෙකම ඇසෙන විට, ඉගෙන ගන්නා අයගේ දිවට වැඩිපුරම අමාරු වෙන දෙය කුමක්ද?
riddle_english: When both 'ළ' and 'ල' appear in Sinhala, what becomes hardest for learners’ tongues?

riddle_original: "Jamás permitas que se apague la llama". ¿Quién lo decía?
riddle_english: "Never let the flame extinguish". Who said it?
reference_answer_original: Slogan del Partido Nuevo (PANU) de Tato Romero Feris.
reference_answer_english: Slogan of the New Party, by the politician Tato Romero Feris.

riddle_original: Cuando terminaron, quedé como una galletita Traviata. ¿Quién soy?
riddle_english: When they finished, I looked like a Traviata cracker.

riddle_original: De deportista accidentado pasó a versatil politico.
riddle_english: Once an injured athlete, he became a versatile politician.

riddle_original: Con el peso devaluado irás a llorar, al que te invite que “lo sigas, que no te va a defraudar”.
riddle_english: With your devalued peso you’ll end up sobbing, to the one that invited you to “follow him, cause he won’t let you down”.

riddle_original: León electo. Sin melena, con peluca.
riddle_english: Elected lion. He has no mane, only a wig.
riddle_hint: “Peluca” is both a wig and the nickname of a particular President.

riddle_original: "Qué peligroso. Qué triste." ¿Quién posteó esto en X?
riddle_english: "So dangerous. So sad." Who posted this on X?

riddle_original: "No fue magia."
riddle_english: "It was not magic."

riddle_original: Mandatario reelecto por siete mandatos consecutivos, luego de dos mandatos como vicegobernador.
riddle_english: An elected official re-elected for seven consecutive terms, following two terms as lieutenant governor.
riddle_note: Formosa, Argentina.

riddle_original: Me dediqué a la actuación, aunque me reconocen más en otros campos. Una figura del pop me dio vida en una película que lleva mi nombre. ¿Quién soy?
riddle_english: I pursued acting, though I am better known in other fields. A pop icon brought me to life in a movie named after me. Who am I?

riddle_original: Quién dijo "Dicen que soy aburrido"?
riddle_english: Who said "they say I'm boring"?

riddle_original: Después de una trifulca en un bar, se convirtió en un mítico gaucho cuyo apodo correspondía a su vestimenta.
riddle_english: After a fight in a bar, he became a legendary gaucho whose nickname matched his clothing.

riddle_original: Toqué el tambor hasta perder la vida. ¿Quién soy?
riddle_english: I played the drum until I lost my life. Who am I?

riddle_original: Aguerridos guerrilleros con ponchos, aterrorizaban a los realistas en el oeste argentino. ¿Cómo se llamaban?
riddle_english: Fierce guerrilla fighters wearing ponchos terrorized the royalists in western Argentina. What were they called?
